docs.title: Autoware CARLA Scenario
docs.text: Welcome to the documentation for autoware-carla-scenario, a CARLA scenario testing framework for Autoware autonomous driving software.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This package provides a framework for creating and running automated scenario tests in the CARLA simulator, designed for validating Autoware's autonomous driving capabilities.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Automated scenario execution in CARLA simulator (UE5: 0.10.0 and ue5-dev), through the statically typed typesafe_carla client
  • Configurable scenarios using Hydra compose + structured configs
  • Glob-pattern batch execution of multiple scenarios in a single CARLA session
  • Condition-based scenario evaluation: timing, collisions, traffic signals, speed / standstill, lane / area position, waypoint crossing, plus logical (And / Or / Not), latching (Sticky), and persistent combinators
  • Action system for side effects: turns, lane changes, traffic-light state, on-demand camera attachment
  • Entity management for ego (EgoVehicle) and NPC vehicles with spawn retry and ground projection
  • Coordinate transforms between Lanelet2, OpenDRIVE, and CARLA world
  • Lanelet-based constraint sweeping via a Hydra lanelet_constraint sweeper plugin (also resolvable without CARLA from the viewer)
  • Web UI (FastAPI + Uvicorn) for browsing results and triggering runs
  • A trajectory log of every run (actors, lights, map, plan, conditions, verdict; JSON Schema published), which a Rerun recording is made from to see the run (Seeing a run), beside CARLA's native recording
  • scenario-setup downloads CARLA's nightly build, which the runner then launches by itself
  • pytest integration via CarlaScenarioFixture (auto-skip when there is no CARLA to launch)

docs.title: Adversarial Actions and NADE
docs.text:
The framework ports TeraSim's adversarial behaviour generation (#385). There are three ways to use it:

  • An adversarial action: one named NPC or pedestrian does one adversarial thing when its trigger holds. For example, it brakes hard in front of a follower, or cuts in.
  • NADE: an environment action that picks, every tick, which agent near the ego carries out which adversity. It samples them more often than they happen naturally, and keeps the importance-sampling weight that makes the run's statistics unbiased.
  • Scheduled static adversities: a stalled vehicle, or the aftermath of a collision, from one time to another.

docs.title: The layers
docs.text: Layer Module What it does Observation adversity.observation Builds a Scene of the agents in the Lanelet2 map frame. It answers TeraSim's traci questions: the leader and follower within 40 m, the lanes beside, the next signal, a pedestrian's crosswalk and nearest road. Triggers adversity.triggers One pure function per kind. Each takes what the agent sees and returns an AdversarialCommand, or None. adversity_command applies the location gate first, then the kind's trigger. Location adversity.location AdversityLocation: ANY, INTERSECTION, HIGHWAY, ROUNDABOUT. These are read from the map by the ODD's own probes, so an adversity fires where coverage records that location. Commands adversity.command An acceleration, a lane change or a path, planned along the lanes into a timed path (plan_command, predict_command). Execution actions._adversarial_execution Drives the path: it takes the vehicle from its traffic backend, follows the path, then hands the vehicle back. NADE adversity.nade, adversity.avoidance Candidates, prediction, challenge, avoidability, importance sampling and the victims' response. Actions actions.adversarial, actions.adversarial_traffic, actions.stalled_object What a scenario registers.

docs.title: The kinds
docs.text:
The numbers are TeraSim's defaults; each can be overridden in TriggerThresholds. The accelerations come from the Intelligent Driver Model (adversity.idm), which stands in for SUMO's car-following model.

Kind Action TeraSim Fires when Does BRAKE_CHECK AdversarialBrakeAction Follower A follower is close behind, and neither is stopped. The agent is not speeding up, and the follower is not slowing. Brakes at the emergency deceleration (9 m/s²) for 2 s. IGNORE_LEADER IgnoreLeaderAction Leader Its leader holds it back by more than 1.5 m/s² (free flow against car following), and the speed difference is at least 2 m/s. Accelerates at the free-flow rate for 2 s. CUT_IN AdversarialCutInAction LaneChange A lane beside is blocked only by the vehicle behind there (closer than SUMO's secure gap). Changes into that lane in 1 s. LANE_CHANGE_ABORT LaneChangeAbortAction LanechangeAbort Blocked as for CUT_IN. The agent is moving, and its lanelet lasts at least 1 s more at its speed. Drifts half a lane toward that side and back in 1 s. HEAD_ON HeadOnAction Headon As for IGNORE_LEADER, but the agent's lanelet and its leader's start more than 120° apart. Uses IGNORE_LEADER's command. TRAFFIC_RULE RunTrafficRuleAction TrafficRule It is stopping for a red or yellow light rather than for its leader. Drives on through at the free-flow rate for 2 s. MERGE AdversarialMergeAction Merge It is beside a merging lane with traffic on it, and not already changing lanes (turned 5° or more off its lane). One lane over: speeds up as if the merging vehicle ahead were not there, when that beats giving way by more than 1.5 m/s², for 2 s. Two lanes over: changes into the lane between in 1 s, when nobody there is within 2 s of headway. JAYWALKING JaywalkAction Jaywalking A pedestrian is off any crosswalk, with a road within 10 m. Walks straight across at its speed (1.4 m/s if it stands) × U(0.5, 2.0), for up to 5 s. RUNNING_RED_LIGHT PedestrianRunRedLightAction RunningRedLight A pedestrian is waiting (at most 0.2 m/s) within 3 m of a crosswalk whose light is red. Crosses it end to end at 2.8 m/s. STOP_CROSSING StopCrossingAction StopCrossing A pedestrian is on a crosswalk. Stands still for N(2 s, 0.5 s), then walks a crosswalk's length on along its heading at 2.8 m/s.

The pedestrian kinds (PEDESTRIAN_KINDS) are only ever a pedestrian's, and the other kinds only a vehicle's.

docs.title: When an action fires
docs.text:
Each adversarial action takes the entity and a required location. Its default trigger is an AdversityFeasibleCondition of its kind at that location, which holds while the kind's trigger would fire. When the action fires, the command the condition found is planned on the map and driven (following_mode: FOLLOW by default, or POSITION, as TeraSim's moveToXY does). At the end of the path the vehicle is handed back to its traffic backend.

A condition given instead decides when the action fires. On that tick the adversity's own trigger is still asked; when it does not hold, nothing is done and a warning is logged. To require both, give the AndCondition of the two.

from autoware_carla_scenario import (
    AdversarialCutInAction,
    AdversityLocation,
    ElapsedTimeCondition,
)

# Cuts in on a highway whenever the gap allows it.
self.register_pre_tick(AdversarialCutInAction("npc1", AdversityLocation.HIGHWAY))
# Asked once, 3 s in: cuts in if it can then, else logs a warning.
self.register_pre_tick(
    AdversarialCutInAction(
        "npc2", AdversityLocation.ANY, ElapsedTimeCondition(3.0, label="later")
    )
)

docs.title: What is a merging lane
docs.text: TeraSim recognises a ramp by its SUMO edge name, which contains "Ramp". Lanelet2 has no such name, so MapFeatures.merges defines a merging lane as a lane that ends into the lane on its left. It either ends beside that lane, or shares what follows with it. This holds at the lanelet itself, or along its straightest successors within 100 m (MERGE_WINDOW_M).

docs.title: A crosswalk's light
docs.text: RUNNING_RED_LIGHT reads the Lanelet2 traffic-light regulatory element that the crosswalk lanelet carries. That is the pedestrian signal in an Autoware map. A crosswalk without one has no red light to run.

docs.title: NADE
docs.text:
AdversarialTrafficAction runs TeraSim's NADE loop on every tick of the run:

  1. Candidates: the max_controlled (5) vehicles nearest the ego within control_radius (50 m), and every pedestrian there.
  2. Adversity: each candidate's adversity is the first entry of adversities whose trigger fires. That gives {normal: 1 - p, adversarial: p}.
  3. Prediction: horizon (5 s) every resolution (0.5 s). The ego is predicted normal: it holds its acceleration along its lane, or changes lane when its turn indicator says so.
  4. Challenge: the candidate's adversarial future conflicts with the ego's normal future (TeraSim's AV-centred NADE). With challenge_npcs, it is also checked against the other candidates' futures.
  5. Avoidability: if no victim can brake out of the conflict (emergency brake, with a 0.5 m buffer), p is multiplied by 3e-4 and the magnitude by 40.
  6. Importance sampling: q = clip(p × magnitude (20), 0, max_is_probability (0.05)), or fixed_is_probability when that is set. At most one adversity is sampled per tick, the nearest challenger first, and none for cooldown (5.5 s) after one.
  7. Response: the sampled adversity's NPC victims avoid it with probability q = 0.2 (p = 0.99) by braking at the emergency deceleration for 3 s, or else accept it and hold their speed for 2 s. That response carries its own weight. An ego victim is never driven.
from autoware_carla_scenario import (
    AdversarialTrafficAction,
    AdversityKind,
    AdversityLocation,
    NadeAdversity,
)

self.register_pre_tick(
    AdversarialTrafficAction(
        [
            NadeAdversity(AdversityKind.CUT_IN, AdversityLocation.HIGHWAY, 0.002),
            NadeAdversity(AdversityKind.BRAKE_CHECK, AdversityLocation.ANY, 0.001),
        ],
        seed=7,
    )
)

It drives the NPCs and pedestrians a scenario registers, and with drive_background (the default) the traffic backend's background vehicles in the world too (#417): the TrafficManager's background traffic (background<N>), SUMO's ambient vehicles (sumo:<id>). One that carries out an adversity, or responds to one, is taken over for as long as its path lasts -- off autopilot, or published into SUMO from CARLA like a released entity -- and handed back to the backend after. SUMO's mesoscopic vehicles have no actor to take over, and SUMO's pedestrians are not driven.

docs.title: The weight
docs.text:
Each tick of a run multiplies the run's likelihood ratio by one factor:

  • p / q when an adversity is sampled;
  • (1 - p) / (1 - q) for each candidate whose adversity challenged a victim but was not drawn;
  • the response's own factor, when one is drawn.

A statistic weighted by this ratio is the naturalistic one. The action's weight is the ratio. BaseScenario.importance_sampling_weight is the product of every action's weight, which is 1.0 without NADE. You can read it:

  • as the built-in metric importance_sampling_weight (aggregation last; see Metrics);
  • in the trajectory log, where each sampled adversity is an adversity record with its p, its q, the weight at that point, the victims and the response (see Trajectory Log).
  • in the run's coverage file, as outcome.weight: a run is importance sampled when one of its actions is (BaseScenario.outcome_weight; NADE is), and only such a run records a weight.

To count which kinds were sampled, register a coverage item on AdversarialTrafficAction.sampled_kind (see Coverage). Merging a batch's coverage files (scenario-coverage) then estimates the naturalistic failure rate per scenario and environment: the mean of the weighted failures with its 95% interval, the relative half width it has converged to (TeraSim's NADE stops below 0.3), the self-normalised rate and the effective number of runs (openodd's weighted outcomes, see Coverage).

docs.title: Whether an adversity is under way
docs.text:
AdversityActiveCondition holds while a road user is carrying out an adversity. It does not matter who started it: a named NPC's own adversarial action, or NADE sampling a background vehicle. An EntityFilter says whose adversities count, and a list of kinds says which (Conditions):

from autoware_carla_scenario import (
    AdversityActiveCondition,
    AdversityKind,
    EntityFilter,
    StickyCondition,
)

# A cut-in by anyone within 30 m of the ego, at any time in the run.
self.register_pass_condition(
    StickyCondition(
        AdversityActiveCondition(
            EntityFilter(max_distance_m=30.0),
            [AdversityKind.CUT_IN],
            label="cut_in_near_ego",
        )
    )
)
# A brake check by one of the TrafficManager's background vehicles ahead.
AdversityActiveCondition(
    EntityFilter(names=("background*",), min_ahead_m=0.0),
    [AdversityKind.BRAKE_CHECK],
    label="background_brake_check_ahead",
)

How long it holds. It holds from the tick the road user starts driving the adversity's path to the tick it is handed back to traffic. Under a StickyCondition it says that the adversity happened. With no filter and no kinds, it holds for any adversity anywhere.

Victims' responses. A NADE victim's response (it avoids or accepts another road user's adversity) counts only with include_responses=True. It counts as the adversity it responds to, and its message names whose that is.

Where the state comes from. Each adversity's execution records itself in adversity_activity when it starts and removes itself when it hands the road user back. The runner clears what is recorded before each scenario.

It is the adversity_active card. Its filter fields are the entity_count card's.

docs.title: Stalled objects and collisions
docs.text:
TeraSim's StalledObjectAdversity and CollisionAdversity are scheduled, not sampled. StalledObjectAction stands a vehicle still at a pose from start_time to end_time (scenario seconds; None means it is never removed). Outside that window the vehicle is out of the world.

A vehicle cannot be spawned once a run has started, so the scenario spawns it in setup, preferably out of the world (spawn.hidden). The action is a trajectory run (the engine of RoutingAction's position mode) of a held pose, with hidden_outside_trajectory. collision_objects creates two of them for a collision's aftermath.

from autoware_carla_scenario import Lanelet2Pose, StalledObjectAction, collision_objects

self.register_pre_tick(
    StalledObjectAction("stalled1", Lanelet2Pose(1043, 30.0), start_time=5.0)
)
for crashed in collision_objects(
    "npc3", "npc4", Lanelet2Pose(2001, 12.0), Lanelet2Pose(2001, 17.0, heading=0.4),
    start_time=0.0, end_time=60.0,
):
    self.register_pre_tick(crashed)

docs.title: Construction zones
docs.text:
ConstructionZoneAction lays out TeraSim's ConstructionAdversity along a lane (adversity.construction): from start_s to end_s metres along it, past its lanelet's end on along the straightest successors. These are the zones:

Zone Where Objects warning warning_zone_length (100 m) before the start signs on the shoulder, every warning_zone_spacing (30 m) taper_in taper_length_in (60 m) from the start cones, from 0.3 m inside the lane's edge to the work zone's offset buffer buffer_zone_length (10 m) cone, cone, barrier work to taper_length_out (30 m) before the end construction_type: cone, barrier, or mixed taper_out to the end cones, back to the edge termination termination_zone_length (30 m) after the end signs

spacing (20 m) is the distance between objects, scaled by 0.7 in a taper and 0.8 in the buffer. With use_dynamic_spacing and speed_limit_mph, MUTCD's spacings apply instead. A taper can be linear or curved (an s-curve). The zone closes in from side, "right" by default; TeraSim instead picked the side from the SUMO lane's index.

From start_time to end_time (None: never removed) the objects stand in the world as CARLA props, each added by a SpawnAction and named <label>/<zone>/<n> (docs/api.md). Unlike a vehicle, a prop may appear while a run is under way. When the zone appears, two things happen:

  • clear_traffic takes the backend's background vehicles in the zone off the road;
  • close_lane tells the backend the lane is closed. SUMO then disallows every vehicle class on it, as TeraSim's full_lane mode does. The TrafficManager cannot close a lane, and says so; a TrafficSinkAction on the zone keeps its traffic out.

TeraSim's full_lane mode places no object. Here the objects are always placed: a closure Autoware cannot see is one it drives into. At end_time the props are removed and the lane is reopened; when the run ends, the lane is reopened and the runner takes the props away with every other.

from autoware_carla_scenario import ConstructionSettings, ConstructionZoneAction

self.register_pre_tick(
    ConstructionZoneAction(
        1043, start_s=120.0, end_s=260.0,
        settings=ConstructionSettings(construction_type="mixed", side="right"),
        start_time=0.0,
    )
)

docs.title: Urban construction zones
docs.text:
layout="urban" lays out TeraSim's UrbanConstructionAdversity (adversity/static/urban_construction.py) instead (#445). TeraSim builds a corridor of SUMO edges across several intersections and lays out each edge on its own. Here one ConstructionZoneAction is one approach of that corridor: start_s is where the approach begins and end_s is the intersection it ends at. For a corridor, add one action per approach. Lane closure, clearing traffic and the props are the same as above. These are the zones:

Zone Where Objects warning from the start, warning_zone_length (200 m) but at most 0.3 of the approach at most three signs, every warning_zone_spacing (30 m) work to the merge taper (with no merge taper, to 0.9 of the approach) along the closed side, 0.5 m inside the lane's edge, every spacing (10 m); for construction_type="cone", every fifth object is a barrier merge_signs before the merge taper merge_signs (2) signs, 50 m apart, none before the start merge_taper the last merge_distance (150 m) before the end cones every half spacing (5 m), from 0.3 m inside the closed side's edge across to 0.3 m inside the other edge, shutting the lane before the intersection (TeraSim's merge_before)

An urban zone has no taper in, buffer or termination zone, and no work_zone_offset or MUTCD spacing. taper_type="curved" shapes the merge taper. The warning zone and the merge taper include their end, as TeraSim's do, so with a whole number of steps the last cone stands at the intersection. The work zone does too when there is no merge taper; with one, it stops short of its end, where the merge taper's first cone stands.

URBAN_CONSTRUCTION holds TeraSim's urban values. They come from the UrbanConstructionAdversity source and its Ann Arbor example (examples/scenarios/ann_arbor/urban_construction.yaml): cones every 10 m in the work zone and every 5 m in the merge taper, three warning signs 30 m apart, merge signs 50 m apart, signs 2 m out on the shoulder, a 200 m warning zone and a 150 m merge taper. In the editor, the urban_construction_zone action starts from these values.

from autoware_carla_scenario import (
    URBAN_CONSTRUCTION,
    ConstructionSettings,
    ConstructionZoneAction,
)

# The 300 m approach to an intersection, closed from the right.
self.register_pre_tick(ConstructionZoneAction(1043, 0.0, 300.0, URBAN_CONSTRUCTION))
# Closed from the left, with a shorter merge taper and three signs before it.
self.register_pre_tick(
    ConstructionZoneAction(
        1051, 0.0, 200.0,
        ConstructionSettings(
            layout="urban", spacing=10.0, warning_zone_length=200.0,
            warning_sign_offset=2.0, side="left",
            merge_distance=80.0, merge_signs=3,
        ),
    )
)

docs.title: Coordinate conventions
docs.text:
• Triggers and NADE: everything is in the Lanelet2 map frame: x East, y North, yaw in radians counter-clockwise from +x. Gaps run bumper to bumper along the lanes. A lane's s is measured along its centreline, and t is positive to the left.
  • Execution: planned paths are MapPose vertices in that frame. The trajectory follower places them in CARLA's left-handed world (y South, yaw in degrees clockwise) through the map's offset, as for any trajectory.
  • Signals: a light's state is keyed by its Lanelet2 traffic-light regulatory element's id, and read off CARLA by adversity.snapshot.

docs.title: Differences from TeraSim
docs.text: TeraSim (SUMO) Here (Lanelet2 and CARLA) SUMO's car-following model The Intelligent Driver Model, with TeraSim's gains as defaults getLeader, getLaneChangeStatePretty Scene: lane chains of the routing graph, with SUMO's secure gap for "blocked" convert2D along an edge The lanelet's centreline and its normal A ramp by its edge name "Ramp" MapFeatures.merges (above) A walking area controlled by a TLS link The crosswalk lanelet's own traffic light A person's SUMO maxSpeed pedestrian_max_speed, 2.8 m/s (the fastest jaywalker) StopCrossing counts steps at dt = 0.1 The wait is in seconds is_lane_changing: heading 5° or more off the SUMO lane's angle The same, off the Lanelet2 lanelet's direction (LanePosition.heading) Background vehicles are adversarial So are they, with drive_background (default): the backend's background vehicles in the world (#417) Construction zones: SUMO vtypes for cones, barriers and signs; full_lane only closes the lane CARLA props (static.prop.*), always placed, plus the lane closed to the backend (#402) UrbanConstructionAdversity: a corridor of edges across num_intersections, found by the edges' road priority, with a merge taper before each intersection One approach per ConstructionZoneAction (layout="urban"), from start_s to the intersection at end_s; a corridor is one action per approach (#445) Urban work zone: a barrier added beside every fifth cone The barrier replaces that cone, so the two props do not overlap Urban work zone up to the merge taper's start inclusive, where the taper's first cone stands too Short of it, so the two props do not overlap Urban spacings hard-coded: warning signs 30 m, work zone 10 m, merge taper 5 m; the merge taper always linear warning_zone_spacing, spacing and half spacing (the same with URBAN_CONSTRUCTION); taper_type="curved" shapes the merge taper Urban warning zone of no length: one sign at the edge's start No warning zone, no sign Urban signs: always on the right shoulder; merge signs named by merge_signs texts On the closed side's shoulder; merge_signs is how many, all the same prop Urban construction vehicles and workers (excavator, dump trucks, warning vehicles) Not placed

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text: This page lists the public surface of autoware_carla_scenario. All symbols exported via the top-level package (autoware_carla_scenario) are stable; symbols only reachable through deeper subpackages should be considered internal unless explicitly noted.

docs.title: Top-level package
docs.text:
from autoware_carla_scenario import (
    BaseScenario, EgoConfig, ScenarioQueue, ScenarioRunner,
    CarlaServerManager, CarlaScenarioFixture,
    # Conditions, actions, kinematics, coordinate poses ...
)

The full list of re-exports is defined in autoware_carla_scenario.__all__ and includes the conditions, actions, kinematics, coordinate, entity, and sensor types described below.

docs.title: Scenario orchestration
docs.text:
Symbol Module Purpose BaseScenario scenario_base Abstract base for user scenarios. Subclasses implement setup() and is_done(). EgoConfig scenario_base VehicleEntityConfig subclass that fixes role_name to EGO_ROLE_NAME and carries both ends of the run: the spawn and the ego's goal_pose. None means "not named yet" — a scenario may derive the goal in setup(), and one that ends setup with none is refused. ScenarioRunner scenario_runner Executes a single BaseScenario against a CARLA world (sync mode tick loop, recording, cleanup). ScenarioQueue scenario_queue Context manager that owns a CarlaServerManager and runs registered scenarios sequentially with cooldown / retry. CarlaServerManager server Starts, reuses, and stops the CARLA UE5 process. Reads CARLA_EXECUTABLE, else launches the CARLA scenario-setup installed. A server it launched is stopped when the launching process dies, even by SIGKILL; one it reused never is. CarlaScenarioFixture pytest_fixtures Helper that registers a scenario into a queue at import time and exposes a session-scoped pytest fixture for its ScenarioResult. EGO_ROLE_NAME constants Reserved CARLA role_name used for the ego actor. EntityRole entity_role Validated role_name wrapper for CARLA actors. Factories: EntityRole.ego(), EntityRole.npc(n).

CameraRecorder (the video renderer) was removed in 15.0.0 with the video itself: a run's trajectory log is what a run is seen from (Seeing a run).

docs.title: Coverage (autoware_carla_scenario.coverage)
docs.text:
See Coverage.

Symbol Purpose BaseScenario.register_cover(name, expression, *, unit, range, every, buckets, values, ignore, event, text, target, cover_by, min_stay) Declare a cover item, after cover() in OpenSCENARIO DSL. BaseScenario.register_cross(name, items, *, text, target, cover_by, min_stay) Cross coverage of cover items sampled on the same event. SamplingEvent When an item is sampled: START, END (default) or TICK. Re-exported from the top-level package. CoverItem, CrossItem The item definitions register_cover() / register_cross() build. autoware_carla_scenario.metrics: BUILT_IN_METRICS, Metric, read_metric(key, world), COLLISION_ANY, COLLISION_AT_FAULT, OFFROAD, WRONG_LANE, MIN_DISTANCE_TO_OBSTACLE_M, ... How the ego drives, read off the world per frame: AlpaSim's metrics. An outcome, which no ODD maps onto. See Metrics. BaseScenario.register_measure(key, read, *, unit, text), .measure(key, world), .measures A scenario's measures: what it sets up, under fixed keys (autoware_carla_scenario.measures: VEHICLE_AHEAD_GAP_M, VEHICLE_AHEAD_RELATIVE_SPEED_KPH, CROSSING_PEDESTRIAN_GAP_M, CROSSING_PEDESTRIAN_SPEED_MS). Replace a built-in one or add one of its own. See Scenario measures. CoverageCollector Samples items on their events during a run; written as {Scenario}_coverage.json. merge_coverage(documents), CoverageReport Merge coverage files and grade them. coverage.cod.export_cod(document, out_dir, stem) Write a run's ODD samples as an ASAM OpenODD COD table, manifest and taxonomy (scenario-coverage --export-cod).

docs.title: ODD (autoware_carla_scenario.odd)
docs.text:
See ODD.

Symbol Purpose OddAttribute(name, probe, *, unit, range, every, buckets, values, text, target, cover_by, min_stay) A measured taxonomy concept. Conditions: is_in, equals, between, at_least, at_most, greater_than, less_than, is_unknown. OddModule(name, *, include_and, include_or, exclude_and, exclude_or, labels, active, text, situation, target, cover_by, min_stay) A named rule; with situation=True, also covered as a situation. OddDefinition.situations() lists those. OddDefinition(name, attributes, modules, *, roots, text) The ODD: judges values with OpenODD's semantics (roots, labels, inactive modules, missing values), and marks buckets outside it. all_of, any_of, module_holds Group conditions; refer to another module or label. default_odd() The built-in ODD: openodd's bundled default (every attribute, no modules), measured in CARLA. register_odd(name, builder), resolve_odd(spec) Name an ODD; turn a name, .yaml path or module:function into one. Packages register through the autoware_carla_scenario.odds entry point group (a function calling register_odd). load_odd_file(path), load_odd_binding(path), load_openodd(*sources, bindings, name, text, situations) Read ASAM OpenODD 1.0 YAML (IMPORT, TAXONOMY, MODULES, ODD), with a binding file naming the probes. GitSource(url, rev, path), GitSourceError An OpenODD file in a git repository at a revision, for load_openodd() or a binding file's openodd list. ego_speed_kph, speed_limit_kph, lanelet_location, lanelet_subtype, lanelet_speed_limit_kph, in_junction, lane_count, illumination, rain, fog, traffic_density, pedestrian_nearby Built-in probes. lanelet_in_junction(lanelet), lanelet_road_type(lanelet), lanelet_speed_limit(lanelet) What the Lanelet2 probes read off one lanelet: its junction, road type (subtype) and speed limit (km/h). scenario_measure(key), ScenarioMeasure The probe mapping an attribute onto the running scenario's measure key (measure: in a binding file). See Scenario measures. typecheck.typecheck_odd(builder) Compile a Python ODD with Codon. plan_route_coverage(odd, scenario_or_route, *, lanelet_map, routing_graph, name) Check a planned route against the ODD on the Lanelet2 map: the verdict per lanelet (inside, outside, undecided) and the expected metres per bucket. Takes a scenario, a PlannedRoute(start, goal, via, name) or lanelet ids. Raises RouteError when the route cannot be planned. See Checking a planned route. combine_route_coverage(odd, routes) The expected coverage of several routes, and the buckets no route reaches. plan_route(route, lanelet_map, routing_graph) The lanelets of a PlannedRoute, with the metres driven on each. UNDECIDED What a probe's on_lanelet returns for a value only the run can tell. OddSampler(odd, knobs, *, controls, seed, strategy, coverage, max_tries, weights) Draws concrete cases inside the ODD: .sample(count) gives OddSample(index, overrides, buckets, values, situation). strategy="coverage" draws the least covered buckets and the uncovered situations first; weights={module: share} (strategy="weighted") puts that share of the cases in each module. See Sampling scenarios from the ODD. OddKnob(key, *, values, scale, offset, integer, range), knobs_from_mapping(raw), DEFAULT_KNOBS A control: the config key that sets a measure (or, as a sweep knob, an attribute), and what it can stage. Scenarios declare theirs under controls in their config, by measure key.

docs.title: Conditions (autoware_carla_scenario.conditions)
docs.text:
All conditions inherit from BaseCondition and return a ScenarioResult from check(world, elapsed) once triggered (or None when not yet triggered). At the end of a run the runner calls close() on every pass and fail condition and every action's trigger: a condition that holds something in the simulator -- CollisionCondition's listening sensor -- stops and destroys it there, through its own handle. close() does nothing by default, and composite conditions close their children. What a run left in a condition (a latched result, a collision seen) stays readable after close(); before every run the runner calls reset() on the conditions and actions the scenario's __init__ registered, which are the same objects on a retry or a second run_all(), so each starts the run as it was built. A condition or action that keeps state between ticks clears it in reset() (calling super().reset()), and composite conditions reset their children.

Symbol Description BaseCondition Abstract base class. Subclasses override _check(). ScenarioResult Pass / fail outcome with message, elapsed time, and per-condition statuses. ConditionStatus Per-condition leaf record used for reporting. AlwaysTrueCondition Default trigger for actions. AndCondition, OrCondition, NotCondition Logical combinators. AndCondition and OrCondition check every child on every tick, so a stateful child (PersistentCondition, StickyCondition) stays current wherever it sits; an AND of StickyConditions therefore says each state was visited, in any order. An AND fires only once every child has fired: a pending child holds back a failing one, so an AND holding a timeout or a collision fails the run only once its other children have fired. NotCondition(child, holds_when_pending=True) is the logical NOT -- it holds while the child has not fired -- where the default flips a fired child's verdict; with OrCondition over EntityLanePositionConditions it says "on none of these lanelets" (cut-in). StickyCondition, PersistentCondition Latch / persist a child condition's truth value. TimeoutCondition, ElapsedTimeCondition Time-based triggers. MetricCondition(metric, rule, value, tolerance, *, label) A built-in metric -- how the ego drives -- against a threshold; usually a fail condition. See Metrics. EntityDistanceCondition, TimeToCollisionCondition Relative conditions between two entities: separation, and time to collision along the line joining them. An entity parked under the map (spawned hidden, not yet brought in) is absent as either entity, so these -- and TimeHeadwayCondition, RelativeSpeedCondition and the reference of an entity-frame SpeedCondition -- do not hold for it whichever way round the two are named; for "the ego is near where a hidden entity will appear", use EntityPositionDistanceCondition on that place. CollisionCondition, EntityExistenceCondition Safety checks. EntityFilter(names=(), kind=RoadUserKind.ANY, reference="Ego", min_distance_m=None, max_distance_m=None, min_ahead_m=None, max_ahead_m=None, min_left_m=None, max_left_m=None, lanelet_ids=(), include_reference=False) Which road users a condition looks at, when it is about some of them rather than one named entity. names are role-name patterns (* any run of characters, ? any one), so the TrafficManager's (background*) and SUMO's (sumo:*) background vehicles can be picked out as well as a scenario's own; kind is vehicles, pedestrians or both (RoadUserKind); the distance between centres, and the offset ahead (negative: behind) and to the left (negative: to the right) in reference's frame on the ground plane, bound it relative to that entity; lanelet_ids require it on one of them. Every bound is optional. select(world) answers which match now, as SelectedEntity(name, actor_id, distance, ahead, left). The reference itself, actors without a role name and actors parked under the map are never taken (the reference is, with include_reference); a filter with a relative bound takes nothing while its reference is not in the world. EntityCountCondition(entities, rule=GREATER_THAN_OR_EQUAL, count=1, *, label) Holds while the number of road users entities (an EntityFilter) takes compares to count: "a vehicle within 30 m ahead of the ego" (EntityFilter(kind=RoadUserKind.VEHICLE, min_ahead_m=0, max_ahead_m=30)), "no pedestrian on the crosswalk" (EQUAL_TO 0). Its message names the ones it took. The entity_count card, whose filter fields every filtered condition shares. AdversityActiveCondition(entities=None, kinds=None, include_responses=False, *, label) Holds while a road user that entities (an EntityFilter; None: every one) takes is carrying out an adversity of one of kinds (AdversityKinds; None or empty: any). It counts a named NPC's own adversarial action and a background vehicle that NADE sampled. It holds from when the road user starts driving the adversity's path until it is handed back to traffic, so put it under a StickyCondition to mean "it happened". A NADE victim's response counts only with include_responses. Imported from the top level or conditions.adversity_active, because it pulls in the Lanelet2 layer. See Adversarial Actions and NADE. OffRoadFractionCondition(fraction, entity_name=None, *, label) Fails once at least fraction (in (0, 1]) of the sample points of a 5 x 3 grid over an entity's (default: the ego's) bounding box -- edges and corners included, not an area -- are on no driving lane. The pass/fail counterpart of the offroad metric, with a tolerance. See Metrics. TrafficSignalAction(..., route_junction=0, route_approach="same", route_turn="any") With lanelet2_traffic_light_ids=TrafficLightTarget.ROUTE: sets the lights of the paths through junction route_junction of the scenario's route that enter it from route_approach and turn route_turn, found on the map the run is on (route.positions.junction_traffic_lights). PlaceClearCondition(position, length, width, margin=0.3, *, label) Passes while no vehicle's or walker's bounding box comes within margin of a length x width rectangle at position (a Lanelet2Pose, facing along the lane turned by its heading; or any position a trajectory vertex takes -- a route pose is placed on the scenario's route when the place is first looked at). Actors parked under the map do not count; one put there on this tick does. The place_clear card; typically guards where an entity appears. TrafficSignalCondition Traffic-light state check: fires while every matching light shows the expected state, and is pending otherwise. RouteProgressCondition An entity's (default: the ego's) distance along the scenario's route, from an anchor (junction:0:entry, ...), compared with a rule; robust to lane changes. See Logical Scenarios from Routes. ComparisonRule, ScalarComparisonRule, compare Numeric comparison primitives. compare(actual, rule, value, tolerance) is the underlying helper. find_actor_by_role_name, find_actor_in_list Helpers for locating CARLA actors by role. find_actor_in_list is reachable via autoware_carla_scenario.conditions.

docs.title: Composition conditions (autoware_carla_scenario.conditions.composition)
docs.text:
These build on CompositionCondition, which composes a child condition tree internally:

  • EntityLanePositionCondition
  • SpeedCondition, SpeedDirection, SpeedCoordinateSystem
  • StandstillCondition
  • TurnIndicatorCondition, TurnIndicatorState -- the turn indicators a vehicle shows (OFF / LEFT / RIGHT / HAZARD), read off its CARLA light state
  • TemporaryStopCondition
  • WaypointCondition, WaypointCheckType

docs.title: Actions (autoware_carla_scenario.actions)
docs.text: Symbol Description BaseAction Abstract base. Owns a trigger BaseCondition, a TickTiming, and an execute(world) side effect. TickTiming Enum: PRE_TICK / POST_TICK. TurnAction, TurnDirection Steer the ego through left / right turns via the CARLA TrafficManager route hints. TurnIndicatorAction Light a vehicle's turn indicators (TurnIndicatorState: OFF / LEFT / RIGHT / HAZARD), its other lights as they are; they stay so until set again. CommunicationLossAction Stop data between the HILS bridge and an ECU under test (ego.entity=hils) while the action runs (until until fires or duration passes, else to the scenario's end): messages by name (a CAN frame, a LiDAR's scan) or everything of a device (or of every device), to_ecu / from_ecu / both; no effect on any other ego. See HILS. LaneChangeAction, LaneChangeDirection Trigger a TrafficManager lane change. TrafficSignalAction, TrafficLightTarget Set traffic-light states (e.g. all RED, all GREEN, or a specific actor). RoutingAction, RoutingMode Send the ego, a vehicle or a pedestrian to a goal through waypoints (a goal with Lanelet2 waypoints, or a trajectory); mode is DRIVER (its own driver, Lanelet2 legs, paced by speed to the waypoints' times), FOLLOW or POSITION (straight legs, as OpenSCENARIO follows a trajectory); speed paces the segments no time does; held_vertex names the vertex a waypoint condition is holding it at; it routes an entity in the scene (bring a hidden one in with SpawnAction), starting where it stands. See Trajectories and Recorded-Scene Replay.

docs.title: Adversarial actions (autoware_carla_scenario.actions.adversarial)
docs.text:
TeraSim's adversities, on a named NPC (exported from the top-level package, not from actions, which would pull in the Lanelet2 map layer). Each takes the entity and a required location (AdversityLocation: ANY, INTERSECTION, HIGHWAY, ROUNDABOUT); its default trigger is an AdversityFeasibleCondition of its kind there. When it fires, the command is planned on the map and driven (following_mode: FOLLOW by default, or POSITION), and the vehicle is handed back to its traffic backend at the end. A condition given instead fires the action, and the adversity's trigger is asked on that tick: when it does not hold, nothing is done. thresholds overrides TeraSim's numbers.

Symbol Description AdversarialBrakeAction Brake hard in front of a follower that keeps coming (BRAKE_CHECK). IgnoreLeaderAction Drive on as if the close, slower leader were not there (IGNORE_LEADER). AdversarialCutInAction Change lane in front of a vehicle too close behind in the next lane (CUT_IN). AdversarialMergeAction Beside a merging lane with traffic on it (MapFeatures.merges: a lane that ends into the lane on its left, there or within 100 m), cut a merging vehicle off: one lane over, speed up as if it were not there, when that beats giving way by more than 1.5 m/s², for 2 s; two lanes over, change into the lane between in 1 s when nobody there is within 2 s of headway (MERGE). LaneChangeAbortAction Start into the next lane in front of a vehicle too close behind there, drifting half a lane toward it, and swerve back, within 1 s (LANE_CHANGE_ABORT). HeadOnAction Drive on at a leader coming the other way: IgnoreLeaderAction's command, where the lanelets the vehicle and its leader are on start more than 120 degrees apart (HEAD_ON). RunTrafficRuleAction Run the red or yellow light the vehicle is stopping for (TRAFFIC_RULE). JaywalkAction Walk a pedestrian straight across the nearest road, off any crosswalk (JAYWALKING); seed seeds its speed. PedestrianRunRedLightAction Walk a pedestrian waiting at a crosswalk (at most 0.2 m/s, within 3 m) across it, end to end, when the crosswalk's Lanelet2 traffic light is red (RUNNING_RED_LIGHT). StopCrossingAction Stand a pedestrian on a crosswalk still for N(2 s, 0.5 s), then walk it a crosswalk's length on along its heading (STOP_CROSSING); seed seeds the wait. SpawnAction, clear_props Put something into the scene mid-run (autoware_carla_scenario.actions.spawn, the counterpart of DespawnAction): a vehicle or pedestrian spawned hidden, brought in at position (any trajectory-vertex frame; None: where it was declared) moving at speed, or with name a prop (blueprint, on_ground; PropAction until 1.0); shift_max takes the nearest clear place that far on along its lane when its own is taken. DespawnAction(name=...) removes a prop; the runner clears every prop between runs (clear_props). StalledObjectAction, collision_objects TeraSim's scheduled static adversities (autoware_carla_scenario.actions.stalled_object): a vehicle the scenario spawned (out of the world, spawn.hidden, best) stands still at a pose -- a Lanelet2Pose, or an xy+yaw MapPose / CarlaWorldPose -- from start_time to end_time (scenario seconds; None: never removed), and is out of the world before and after. A trajectory run (the engine of RoutingAction's position mode) of a held pose with hidden_outside_trajectory. collision_objects is two of them, for a collision's aftermath. ConstructionZoneAction, ConstructionSettings, URBAN_CONSTRUCTION TeraSim's construction zone (autoware_carla_scenario.actions.construction_zone): warning signs, an entry taper of cones, a buffer, the work zone, an exit taper and termination signs along a lane from start_s to end_s, as CARLA props from start_time to end_time; background traffic in it is taken off the road and the lane closed to the backend (SUMO). layout="urban" (preset: URBAN_CONSTRUCTION) lays out TeraSim's urban variant on an intersection approach instead: a short warning zone, cones along the curb and a merge taper that shuts the lane before the intersection. See Adversarial Actions and NADE. AdversarialTrafficAction, NadeAdversity, NadeSettings TeraSim's NADE as an environment action that runs for the whole run. Each tick, the NPC or pedestrian near the ego whose adversity (the first of adversities whose trigger fires) would challenge the ego carries it out, with the importance-sampling probability q = clip(p x magnitude, 0, max_is_probability), or a fixed one. One adversity at a time, then a cooldown. An adversity no victim can brake out of is unavoidable: its p is cut by 3e-4 and its magnitude multiplied by 40 (adversity.avoidance). With challenge_npcs, an NPC victim avoids it (emergency brake) or accepts it, with its own IS weight. weight keeps the run's likelihood ratio. It drives the registered entities and, with drive_background (default), the traffic backend's background vehicles (TrafficBackend.background_actors: TrafficManager background traffic, SUMO's ambient vehicles), each taken over while it carries out an adversity or responds to one and handed back after (#417). AdversityFeasibleCondition, AdversityKind, AdversityLocation Holds when the entity may carry out a kind adversity at location (autoware_carla_scenario.conditions.adversity_feasible).

docs.title: Trajectories (autoware_carla_scenario.trajectory)
docs.text:
See Trajectories and Recorded-Scene Replay.

Symbol Description Trajectory, TrajectoryVertex A named polyline and its vertices: a position and the condition the entity departs it on (advance) -- a time, TrajectoryTimeCondition(t) (read back as vertex.time), or any other condition (waypoint conditions; Trajectory.is_gated, Trajectory.gated({index: condition})). TrajectoryTimeCondition A vertex's time: depart when the trajectory's clock reaches it. MapPose An absolute pose in Autoware's map frame, as a recording states it. RelativeLanePose A pose relative to an entity in lane coordinates (ds, offset, d_lane, yaw, entity_ref; OpenSCENARIO RelativeLanePosition), placed when the action starts. RouteLanePose, RouteOppositePose, RouteCrossingPose, RouteCrosswalkPose, RouteRoadsidePose Poses placed against the scenario's route (a logical scenario) when the action starts: along the route and across lanes, on the opposite road, on a lanelet entering a route junction from the left / right / opposite, on a junction's crosswalk, at the roadside. TrajectoryTiming, ReferenceContext How vertex times map onto the scenario clock (τ * scale + offset, from the scenario or the action start). TrajectoryFollowingMode POSITION (kinematic replay) or FOLLOW (a controller tracks it): the adversarial actions' mode.

Recorded scenes (T4) are transcribed into documents outside the framework, by the separate scene_to_scenario_transpiler package (scenario-import-t4).

docs.title: Sensors (autoware_carla_scenario.sensor)
docs.text: Symbol Description CameraSensorBase, CameraSensorConfig Provider-agnostic camera sensor interface. CarlaCameraSensor, CarlaCameraSensorConfig CARLA RGB camera implementation, used by the driver rig.

docs.title: External driver (autoware_carla_scenario.driver)
docs.text:
Connects the ego to a driving policy served over alpasim's egodriver.EgodriverService. See External Driver Interface.

Symbol Description BaseEgoDriverClient Transport-agnostic client interface: session lifecycle, observation submission, drive. EgoDriverGrpcClient gRPC implementation against the vendored alpasim protos. DriverClientConfig, DriverCameraConfig Connection settings, policy cadence, and the camera rig streamed to the policy. ControlConfig, TrajectoryFollower, VehicleCommand Pure pursuit plus a port of Autoware's autoware_pid_longitudinal_controller (or the time_indexed tracker), turning a plan into carla.VehicleControl. Pose, Trajectory Rigid-transform primitives with protobuf conversions (right-handed frame). EgoObservation, DriveOutcome The state sent to the policy and the plan it returns. RendererDataBuilder Collects CARLA ground truth (governing traffic light, other vehicles, speed limit) into the renderer_data extension payload. driver.stop_lines.StopLines Which traffic light governs the ego (the lane graph walked ahead to the next junction) and the distance along its heading to where it stops for it (the stop waypoint walked to its junction's mouth); RendererDataBuilder reports both.

docs.title: Traffic backends (autoware_carla_scenario.traffic)
docs.text:
Owns the vehicles a scenario did not author, and answers the manoeuvre intents asked of the ones it did. See Traffic Backends.

Symbol Description TrafficBackend The interface: prepare / adopt / start / tick / close, plus the manoeuvre intents. TrafficContext The run a backend joins: client, world, map name, OpenDRIVE, step, seed, output directory. TrafficManagerBackend CARLA's TrafficManager — the default backend. NullTrafficBackend No traffic model at all (traffic=none). TrafficConfig, TrafficManagerBackendConfig Which backend drives a run, and the TrafficManager's own options. register_backend, build_backend, available_backends The registry a third-party backend joins through the autoware_carla_scenario.traffic_backends entry point. TrafficBackendError, TrafficBackendUnavailable A backend that cannot do what the run needs; the second names a simulator that is not installed.

docs.title: Coordinate transforms (autoware_carla_scenario.coordinate)
docs.text: Symbol Description Lanelet2Pose, OpenDrivePose, CarlaWorldPose, AnyPose Frame-tagged pose dataclasses. CoordinateFrame, FrameMismatchError, frame_of Coordinate-frame tagging and validation. MapManager Singleton owning the loaded LaneletMap, pyxodr road network, MGRS offset, and z offset. to_carla_world, to_carla_location, to_lanelet2, to_opendrive Pose conversion entry points (overload by input frame). project_onto_road Project a CarlaWorldPose onto a specified OpenDRIVE road. road_traffic_rule An OpenDRIVE road's traffic rule, "RHT" or "LHT" (its rule attribute, "RHT" where unset). snap_to_carla_road Ray-cast a pose onto the rendered CARLA ground surface. GroundProjectionConfig Ray-cast tuning for snap_to_carla_road. lanelets_ahead A lanelet and the lanelets that follow it in the routing graph (no lane changes, every branch), up to a distance: the lanes a vehicle keeps to without changing lanes. get_stop_line_poses, get_stop_line_poses_with_following Resolve stop-line Lanelet2Poses for a lanelet (optionally including following lanelets).

docs.title: Entities (autoware_carla_scenario.entity)
docs.text: Symbol Description VehicleEntity, VehicleEntityConfig Generic vehicle actor with retry-aware spawn. EgoVehicle Subclass with the fixed EGO_ROLE_NAME, plus the on_scenario_start / on_tick / on_scenario_end lifecycle hooks ScenarioRunner calls. ExternallyDrivenEgo Base of every ego driven by a stack of its own rather than the TrafficManager: opts out of autopilot, refuses TrafficManager manoeuvres, and carries the termination request. BridgeHandshake The mission and readiness handshake with a stack over the AutowareBridge, optionally launching it per scenario; held by an ego (entity.bridged_ego). BridgedEgoEntity The ego that is nothing but a BridgeHandshake: the stack drives. AutowareEgoEntity The BridgedEgoEntity driven by Autoware through autoware_carla_interface. See Autoware. CarlaDriverEntity Drives the ego from an external policy's plan over the egodriver gRPC contract; given a bridge, starts the policy once a stack serving its world is ready. See External Driver Interface. SpawnLocation (Protocol) Tag interface implemented by spawn-point providers. SpawnTransform Spawn at an explicit carla.Transform. SpawnPointIndex Spawn at the N-th map spawn point.

docs.title: Kinematics (autoware_carla_scenario.kinematics)
docs.text:
Frame-aware velocity / acceleration types with affine-space arithmetic (absolute - absolute = relative; absolute + relative = absolute).

Symbol Description Vector3 Frame-tagged 3-vector. CoordinateFrame, FrameMismatchError, frame_of Re-exported from coordinate.frames. AbsoluteVelocity, RelativeVelocity, FrenetVelocity Velocity types. AbsoluteAcceleration, RelativeAcceleration, FrenetAcceleration Acceleration types.

docs.title: Lanelet constraint sweeper (autoware_carla_scenario.sweeper)
docs.text:
Powers the Hydra lanelet_constraint sweeper plugin. Can also be used directly from Python:

Symbol Description LaneletConstraintSweeper The Hydra Sweeper implementation (also re-exposed via hydra_plugins.autoware_scenario_sweeper). Constraint (ABC) Base class of the constraints above, with an abstract evaluate(lanelet). A constraint of your own may derive from it or only define evaluate(): the matching takes either. EqualsConstraint, InSetConstraint, OnRouteConstraint, LaneletLengthConstraint, HasStopLineConstraint, HasTrafficLightStopLineConstraint, HasAdjacentConstraint, IsJunctionConstraint, PreviousOfConstraint, FollowingOfConstraint Atomic constraints. AndConstraint, OrConstraint, NotConstraint Combinators. parse_constraint, find_matching_lanelets YAML-to-Constraint parsing and lanelet matching. The corresponding YAML type: keys for the atomics above are equals, in_set, on_route, lanelet_length, has_stop_line, has_traffic_light_stop_line, has_adjacent, is_junction, previous_of, following_of. Binding (Protocol), StopLineOffsetBinding, parse_binding Per-match parameter derivation (e.g. compute ego.spawn_s from a stop-line offset). load_lanelet2_map Lightweight Lanelet2 loader used outside of CARLA.

A scenario whose sweep holds a route search instead of constraints is expanded over the routes of the map that match it (expand_route, one case per match); see Logical Scenarios from Routes.

docs.title: Logical scenarios (autoware_carla_scenario.route)
docs.text:
See Logical Scenarios from Routes.

Symbol Description parse_route_search -> RouteSearchSpec Read a route search (LaneSegmentSpec / JunctionSegmentSpec segments, Range bounds, ego placement, max_matches, seed). No map needed. RouteMatch, RouteSegmentMatch A concrete route: lanelet ids, start / end s, each segment's route-s span and lanelets; anchor_s(anchor), to_config() / from_config() (the scenario.route.* keys). parse_anchor start, end, segment:K:start|end, junction:K:entry|exit. route.search.find_route_matches Every route of a Lanelet2 map matching a search, sorted (or shuffled by seed). route.frame.RouteFrame, ego_placement A match on its map: locate(s), point(s), project(x, y); where the ego spawns and its goal is. route.positions.resolve_route_pose Place a route pose against a frame and the ego's route s. set_scenario_route, scenario_route, scenario_route_frame, clear_scenario_route The route the running scenario is about. route.geometry.MapFeatures The per-lanelet questions a search asks (lanes beside, opposite lane, junction members and approaches, crosswalks), cached.

The plugin is registered with Hydra under hydra/sweeper=lanelet_constraint; see src/hydra_plugins/autoware_scenario_sweeper/.

docs.title: Result viewer (autoware_carla_scenario.ui)
docs.text:
Used internally by the viewer CLI. The web app is the supported surface, but the helper modules are importable for tooling:

Symbol Description ui.app FastAPI application object and route handlers. ui.scanner Discover sessions / scenarios under outputs/ and multirun/, build condition trees. ui.runner Background subprocess.run(["uv", "run", "scenario", ...]) orchestration with thread-safe progress. ui.sweep_resolver.resolve_sweep Resolve a sweep without launching CARLA. ui.cases Which files are a session's cases: the stem each case's files share (a SLURM batch's manifest, or matched against batch_results.json). session_dir / job_dir / contained are the one check every path the viewer builds from a URL goes through: resolved, it must stay under multirun/ or outputs/, else the route answers 404. ui.results A session's cases with their case, coverage and metrics (load_results, case_metrics), the cases in an ODD cell, and sessions compared case by case and cell by cell (compare). ui.case_paths The path guard (contained, session_dir, job_dir), CaseFiles and the stems of a directory's cases, which ui.cases re-exports; checked by the library check. ui.comparison Sessions compared case by case and ODD cell by cell (compare, default_axes, varying_attributes, METRICS) on typed ComparedCase records, which ui.results builds from a case's coverage document (CaseResult.compared) and re-exports; checked by the library check. ui.drive_metrics The box gaps and the running metrics of the ego's ticks (DriveMetrics) that ui.results.case_metrics reads a trajectory log with; checked by the library check. ui.slurm_launch Submitting a batch with launcher=slurm from the viewer (build_command, start_submit), a SLURM batch's progress (batch_status), and scenario-slurm run on it. ui.slurm_options The launcher.* keys the viewer sets (SlurmOptions), the checks of each field (check_*), the Hydra overrides they become (SlurmOptions.overrides) and the scenario command line that submits the batch (build_command, given how scenario is started); ui.slurm_launch reads them off the run panel (SlurmOptions.from_request) and re-exports them. ui.recordings A case's Rerun recording, made on demand with autoware_carla_scenario_rerun when installed, and where the Rerun web viewer is loaded from. ui.models Pydantic models (SessionSummary, SessionItem, ConditionNode, ScenarioResultView, RunProgress).

docs.title: Scenario authoring (autoware_carla_scenario.authoring)
docs.text:
The declarative authoring layer behind the Scenario Editor. None of it imports CARLA or lanelet2, so a document can be loaded, validated, compiled and exported anywhere.

Symbol Description ScenarioDocument The Scenario IR: entities, actions, assertions, an optional route search (a logical scenario), and a ui block that is presentation only. RouteSearch, LaneSegment, JunctionSegment, LengthRange, CountRange The route search as the IR states it; RouteSearch.to_sweep_dict() is what the route search reads. Entity, SpawnSpec, SValue, BindingRef, GoalSpec, EgoDriver Actors, how they spawn (fixed lanelet, or a constraint search with an optionally derived offset), and — for the ego alone — which stack drives it and where it is sent. LaneletChoice, LaneletSlot, ScenarioDocument.lanelet_slots Fixed or searched, and one view over every place a document names a lanelet — a spawn, a goal, an action's or a condition's lanelet parameter — so the picker, the validator and the Hydra config read one answer. ActionNode, ConditionNode, ConstraintNode Recursive IR nodes; a node's meaning comes from its registry spec, not from a type switch. ActionSpec, ConditionSpec, ConstraintSpec, BindingSpec, FieldSpec, ConditionVisual Metadata describing how a primitive is presented, edited and built. register_action_spec, register_condition_spec, register_constraint_spec, register_binding_spec Add a primitive; the GUI, validation and the compiler pick it up with no template change. validate_document -> ValidationReport Metadata-driven validation; errors block export, warnings do not. compile_document -> CompiledScenario Resolve entity ids to CARLA roles and type-check parameters, without importing CARLA. authoring.builders Factories that turn a compiled plan into the framework's own BaseAction / BaseCondition. Imports CARLA lazily. build_scenario_config, dump_scenario_config Render a document as the framework's Hydra scenario config, including a sweep section the existing sweeper understands. export_package -> ExportResult Write a reproducible Scenario Package and the wheelhouse built from it; raises PackageExportError (leaving nothing behind) when locking, verification or the wheelhouse fails. build_wheelhouse -> Wheelhouse Resolve a locked package's whole dependency graph into wheels that pip install --no-index --find-links can install with no uv, git or network; raises WheelhouseError. DraftStore, Draft, load_document, save_document YAML persistence for editor drafts and exported documents. new_document, blank_document Starter documents.

docs.title: Declarative runtime (autoware_carla_scenario.declarative)
docs.text: Symbol Description DeclarativeScenario A BaseScenario whose content comes from a ScenarioDocument. Registers the same pre/post-tick actions and pass/fail conditions a hand-written scenario would. Imports CARLA. DeclarativeScenarioConfig Hydra config group: document_path, timeout_seconds, spawn_overrides (the addressable per-entity spawn keys a sweep drives), param_overrides, and route (a logical scenario's route match, as scenario-expand writes it).

docs.title: Scenario editor (autoware_carla_scenario.editor)
docs.text:
Used by the scenario-editor CLI. A separate application from ui; neither imports the other.

docs.title: Software Architecture
