After the compile, the checker runs mypy (a dependency of the framework) over the scenario's own modules, following imports silently, checking the bodies of unannotated functions too, and with no configuration file of the package's (so the verdict does not depend on how strict the package's own mypy settings are), and keeps only what it reports of a value that may be None used where it may not be: an attribute of it, an operator, an argument, an assignment, a return, an index, or an item of a list or dict display (mypy's union-attr, operator, arg-type, assignment, return-value, index, call-overload, list-item and dict-item; a set display's item is an arg-type to mypy), each only where None is the offending type (#267): the None item of a union an attribute is missing on (Item "None" of "Waypoint | None"), an operand, the value indexed or an argument that is None or a union holding it, or a value whose type holds None given where the type expected does not (incompatible type "float | None"; expected "float"), the key or the value of a dict entry included (Dict entry 0 has incompatible type "str": "float | None"; expected "str": "float"). An item matters because Codon unwraps it where the model iterates the sequence (#308): register_cover(..., buckets=[0.0, 10.0, cfg.min_speed_kmh]) and register_cross("c", ["speed", maybe_name]) compiled, and failed in Python on the None; [0.0, x or 0.0] passes. A message that only mentions None inside another type or in the type expected is not one: a reader returning Optional[str] given to register_measure(), which takes one returning Optional[float], is a str for a float, Codon's error to report, and a list[float] for a list[float | None] is mypy's invariance, which Codon accepts. An assignment that only declares is not one either: a None default for a non-Optional annotation (speed: float = None), or a value assigned to an attribute mypy inferred as None from its first assignment. Each finding fails the check at its line, after Codon's errors:

scenario.py:67:28: error: Unsupported operand types for / ("None" and "float"): Codon unwraps an Optional implicitly, so test the value for None before this use, or Python fails here when it is None (mypy: operator)
    Left operand is of type "float | None"

The same pass refuses a framework union used as one of its members (#309). Codon holds TrajectoryVertex.position (a TrajectoryPosition, the union of the ten poses) as a Union, and converts it to whichever member a use needs at run time (No attribute of a union, below), so v.position.lanelet_id of a MapPose vertex, or v.position passed to a parameter typed Lanelet2Pose, compiled, and raised AttributeError in Python. mypy reports both (union-attr, arg-type), and the pass keeps them where the union mypy names is made of the members of one of the unions the model holds: each module-level Name = Union[...] alias of typecheck/codon/autoware_carla_scenario/ (TrajectoryPosition, AnyPose) and each property it declares to return a Union[...] (TrajectoryVertex.position, CoverItem.event), read from the model, so the list follows it (none_check.framework_unions(); test_typecheck_none_check.py checks each against the union Python declares). mypy reports a missing attribute once per member lacking it; the check reports it once, naming them all, with its own advice:

scenario.py:71:27: error: Items "CarlaWorldPose", "OpenDrivePose", "MapPose", ... of "CarlaWorldPose | Lanelet2Pose | ... | RouteRoadsidePose" have no attribute "lanelet_id": Codon holds this union of the framework's (TrajectoryPosition) and converts it to the member this use needs at run time, so narrow it with isinstance first, or Python fails here on any other member (mypy: union-attr)

Narrowed code passes (if isinstance(p, Lanelet2Pose): p.lanelet_id), and so does the union passed on where the union is taken (TrajectoryVertex(v.position, advance=v.advance), a TrajectoryPosition parameter).

A field of a frozen dataclass of your own is read-only (#567). Codon compiles a frozen dataclass as an ordinary class, so mypy's verdict is used: p.x = 2.0, p.x += 1.0, self.x = ... in a method of the class, a loop variable's field and a frozen subclass's field are refused as Pt is a frozen dataclass; use dataclasses.replace(x, x=...), where the receiver's type is known to mypy (a value of unknown type, Any, is not). dataclasses.replace and object.__setattr__(self, ...) in __post_init__ stay valid. The class is found by its name: a name is treated as a frozen dataclass only where every class of that name in the scenario's modules is one (a same-named plain class with a read-only property is left alone, at the cost of a missed frozen assignment). The decorator may be @dataclass(frozen=True, ...), @dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True) or an aliased import. This rests on mypy, as the None check does: without it the check warns the None check did not run and a frozen assignment is not reported. setattr(p, "x", 1) is not caught.

bytes and str do not mix (#574). Codon's bytes is a str, so b"x" + "y", "sent " + name.encode(), a bytes returned for a -> str, passed to a str parameter or assigned to a str, "x" in raw and raw == "ab" compile, and Python raises TypeError (or the comparison is always False). They are refused with mypy's verdict, only where the offending pair is exactly bytes and str: bytes and str do not mix in Python: decode with .decode() / encode with .encode(). A str | bytes union, a bytearray and every other incompatible type are left alone, and b + b, s + s and .encode() used as bytes stay valid.

A comparison that is always False is refused (#575). The None check runs mypy with --strict-equality and keeps its comparison-overlap findings: an Enum member compared with its raw value (Color.RED == "red", mode == 1, mode in (1, 2)) or with a member of another enum is False in Python, and Codon compiles it. The advice is an Enum member never equals its raw value: compare with Color.RED, or use Color.RED.value. Only the findings with an enum as an operand are kept, not every comparison-overlap: mypy also reports two different literals (MODE: Final = 1 and if MODE == 2), a deliberate switch. The enum is found among the classes of the scenario's own modules (an enum imported from elsewhere is not recognised, so its non-literal comparisons are missed). mypy skips a class that defines __eq__, and IntEnum, StrEnum and (str, Enum) overlap their raw value in Python as well, so Level.LOW == 1 and Phase.GO == "go" are valid. Color.RED.value == "red" is the valid spelling. A member written out as a literal (Level.LOW == 1) is judged by mypy on identity, so it is kept only for a plain Enum / Flag defined in the scenario's own modules, and two members of one enum (Color.RED != Color.BLUE) are not a comparison with a raw value. The flag adds no other error, so the None check's other findings are unchanged; the framework's modules and the built-in scenarios have none of these comparisons. Like the rest of this section it rests on mypy.

A string formatting Python fails on is refused (#589). The None check keeps mypy's str-format findings of a str.format call or a % on a literal format string where Python raises at the call: a conversion the value does not take ("{:d} km/h".format(speed) for a float and "{:.2f}".format(name) for a str raise ValueError, "%d km/h" % name and "%x" % speed raise TypeError), too few or too many arguments ("%s %s" % (name,), "{} {}".format(name)), a missing named field or mapping key, an unknown format character or conversion ("%q", "{!x}"), a malformed spec ("{:abc}", an unmatched {), and mixing automatic and manual field numbering. Codon formats with its own rules and compiles all of them. The advice is Python raises ValueError, TypeError, IndexError or KeyError on this format string with these values (...); convert the value first (int(x), str(x)) or use "{}" / "%s". "%d" % speed (a float) and "{:.2f}".format(n) (an int) are valid, as in Python. A conversion the value does not take is kept only for a built-in type that fails for every value (str, float, None, bytes, complex, a list, ...): mypy does not count a class's __index__ ("%x" % obj runs) or a __getitem__ without keys ("%(k)s" % obj runs), and refuses "{:.2f}" of a complex or a Fraction, which run. Too many arguments is kept only for a % whose right operand is a tuple display or a constant: "{}".format(a, b) ignores the extra argument, and "abc" % d formats no key of a dict (or of a list, or bytes). An unknown spec is kept where the Python running the check refuses it ("{:z.1f}" runs on 3.11). Three more of mypy's str-format messages are not kept, because mypy gives them to valid code as well: Numeric flags are only allowed for numeric types ("{:05}".format(name) runs; "{:+}".format(name) does not, and the message does not say which flag), Syntax error in format specifier and the field-accessor ones ("{0[my key]}".format(d) and "{0['k']}".format(d) index d with "my key" and "'k'"). An f-string's spec (f"{speed:d}") is not checked: mypy does not check it, and rewriting it into a .format call for mypy would move the columns mypy reports. Like the rest of this section it rests on mypy.

Typing contracts you declared must hold (#577). Python mostly does not enforce these and Codon does not read them, so mypy's verdict is used, each kept only on its exact code and message (no other misc, override, index or attr-defined error is a finding; Codon reports attribute errors itself):

  • Final assigned again (MAX_SPEED: Final = 30.0, then MAX_SPEED = 40.0, self.LIMIT = 40.0, Cls.LIMIT = 1.0 or a Final local rebound): a name declared Final is bound once; .... Bind a new name or drop Final.
  • A ClassVar assigned through an instance (self.count += 1, c.count = 5): a ClassVar is shared by the class; .... Python creates a shadowing instance attribute and Codon treats the annotated name as an instance field, so what runs can differ. Assign through the class (Cls.count += 1) or drop ClassVar.
  • A method incompatible with the one it overrides: a narrowed argument type, a different return type, a required parameter added, or a parameter removed (the override must accept what the overridden method accepts ...). This covers the framework's hooks too: BaseScenario.is_done(self) -> bool overridden as is_done(self, strict: bool) is refused, since the framework calls it with the base signature. An extra parameter with a default, or a wider argument type, is fine, and # type: ignore[override] on the def line (mypy's own) silences it. The dunder methods are not checked (__eq__(self, other: Pt) is common and benign), nor is a method overriding object's. The built-in scenarios and the template produce none.
  • A Mapping, Sequence or AbstractSet mutated (m["k"] = 1, del m[k], s.append(3), s.sort(), m.update(...), a.add(1)): ... is read-only by its annotation; copy it first .... Only an attribute that mutates (append, extend, insert, pop, remove, sort, reverse, clear, update, setdefault, popitem, add, discard, the set *_update methods, __delitem__) on a receiver typed exactly as one of those three counts; a typo (s.appnd) or a missing attribute of another type is not reported here. Import them from typing or collections.abc (read as typing's, #586; its Set is AbstractSet): the check is the same.

Not checked: a name bound on one path only (#576). Python raises UnboundLocalError for if c: y = 1 followed by use(y), and mypy reports it only with --enable-error-code possibly-undefined. That code is not enabled: mypy's flow analysis cannot see that the branch that binds a name and the branch that reads it test the same condition (if x is not None: v = ... then if x is not None: use(v)), nor that a for over a non-empty constant runs, so valid code is refused and the cure is to restructure correct code. Run over the framework's 313 modules it reports 15 times in 11 modules: 9 are a condition tested twice or a try/with that binds on every path that reads, 4 are a loop mypy cannot see always binds (a for over a non-empty constant, a for/break/else), and 2 are latent edge cases in the framework (an unbound exit_code when server.cooldown_max_retries is negative, and an unbound port_file in slurm/worker.py's finally when layout.task_port raises after the port slot was taken), not scenario patterns. Probes of scenario-style branches showed the same: if/else, an exhaustive enum if/elif, try/except that raises or returns, match with a default and for/else pass, but a loop variable read after a for and a guard tested twice are refused. Bind the name before the branch when you mean to read it later.

The CARLA API's Optional results are checked too (#267). typesafe_carla's CPython package is a prebuilt extension with no .pyi and no py.typed, so mypy alone reads typesafe_carla.carla as Any. The checker gives mypy stubs of it instead, written from typesafe_carla's own inventory of its Codon library (typesafe_carla.pycarla.Inventory, which the CPython package is generated from; typecheck/carla_stubs.py) and put on MYPYPATH: every public class with its bases, and every method and property with the return type the library declares. So Map.get_waypoint(), ActorList.find(), World.get_actor(), World.try_spawn_actor(), Actor.parent, Vehicle.get_traffic_light(), Waypoint.get_left_lane(), Sensor.poll() and the library's other Optional results are Optional to mypy, and a use without a test for None is refused like a float | None config field:

scenario.py:76:16: error: Item "None" of "Waypoint | None" has no attribute "transform": Codon unwraps an Optional implicitly, so test the value for None before this use, or Python fails here when it is None (mypy: union-attr)

get_waypoint() is the one exception to the library's declarations: it returns None when no lane of lane_type matches, and projected onto the road (project_to_road=True, its default) that is only on a map with no such lane at all, so the stubs give that call a Waypoint (the framework uses it unguarded too). With project_to_road=False, or a flag mypy cannot read as True, it is Optional. The stubs type only what the None check needs: parameters are *args: Any, **kwargs: Any (the arguments are Codon's to check), and a return type mypy cannot be given (a pointer, a type parameter, overloads returning different types), an enumeration, carla.command and any name not written are Any, so they add no error of their own. They are written once per library, under ~/.cache/autoware_carla_scenario/carla-stubs/ (named by a digest of the library's Codon sources), or into a temporary directory where that cannot be written; where typesafe_carla's library cannot be read, mypy runs with CARLA untyped, as before.

Narrow the value first, as mypy reads it: if x is not None:, assert x is not None, an early return when it is None, or a default (x or 0.0). mypy keeps a cache in ~/.cache/autoware_carla_scenario/mypy (under $XDG_CACHE_HOME when it is set), so only the first check reads the framework (about ten seconds); where that directory cannot be written, as in a container with a read-only home, mypy runs without a cache. A scenario package installed as a wheel (not editable) is checked too: mypy would take site-packages for its source root, so the check gives it the package through a link in a directory of its own. When mypy gives no verdict (it ran out of time or crashed), the check keeps Codon's verdict and says so in a warning:

warning: the None check did not run (mypy did not finish within 600s), so an Optional used without a test for None is not reported

The error is reported at the scenario file's own line. One in a function's body is at that line, with the call that reached it in the trace:

scenario.py:88:16: error: 'MyConfig' object has no attribute 'timeout_secs'
    during the realization of _helper(self: MyScenario) [<scenario check: MyScenario._helper()>, scenario.py:87]

One in what the appended line compiles itself is at the line of the class-level default, or, for a parameter's default, at the def of its function, and the trace names the call (reached by <scenario check: class-level default of MyScenario.RETRIES>).

A function the check cannot call, because a parameter has no annotation, one Codon cannot express (Any, object, Callable[..., R]) or one naming a TypeVar (a generic function), is not refused: it is left out of the appended calls with a warning, and compiled where setup() and is_done() reach it, generically, as before. So is one whose return annotation names Any, such as a custom condition's get_details() -> dict[str, Any] of mixed value types, which Codon cannot build (the library check lists the framework's own as uncalled):

my_scenario.py:40: warning: MyScenario._scaled: parameter `x` has no annotation; the check does not call it on its own, so it is compiled only where the scenario's constructor, setup() and is_done() reach it

A helper with a **kwargs or a *args that the scenario calls is compiled through those calls (#266). The appended calls give a *args: T one T and a **kwargs no keyword at all, and Codon types each from the call: a Tuple[T], an empty NamedTuple. So def opts(**kw: float) reading kw["speed"] was refused ('NamedTuple' object has no attribute 'speed', reached by <scenario check: opts()>) although setup() calls opts(speed=2.0), and xs[1] of a *xs: float likewise. Such a function whose body reads what they hold (kw["speed"], xs[1], a, b = xs, g(*xs), g(**kw)) and that a function, a class body or the module's top level of the scenario's modules calls (by its name: opts(...), self.scale(...), helpers.opts(...), Tuner(...) for its __init__; its own recursive call does not count) is not called again: its callers' calls compile it with what they pass. One whose body does not read them (kw.get("speed", 1.0), sum(xs)) is called as before: a call is known by its name only, so a gains.update(p=1.0) would otherwise leave a helper update to a call of dict's, and nothing would compile it. One nobody calls is still called, so an error in it is found, unless it subscripts its **kwargs, which no call without a keyword compiles: that is left out with the warning above (MyScenario._opts: reads**kwby key, and nothing in the scenario calls it: the check has no keyword to call it with).

A warning does not fail the check (result.ok stays true; they are in result.warnings), and scenario-check and the runner print them. Annotate the parameter to have the function checked on its own. Refusing such a function would have refused a scenario that passed before, for a helper that compiles wherever it is called. No built-in example, the scenario package template or a scaffolded package has one.

An ODD written in Python (ODD) is checked the same way: the program calls its builder (odd: OddDefinition = urban_odd()). Every attribute's probe is then called with a world, and every condition must come from an attribute. The ODD's own modules have every function compiled as a scenario's do, with the same warning for one the check cannot call (compiled where the builder reaches it). The runner checks the ODD named by the odd key under the same typecheck mode, and scenario-odd check does it without running anything.

docs.title: The model
docs.text:
autoware_carla_scenario/typecheck/codon/ holds Codon declarations of everything a scenario imports from autoware_carla_scenario: the conditions, actions, poses and coordinate functions, entities, BaseScenario, the shared config dataclasses, with their static types. The CARLA API is not modelled: the checker puts typesafe_carla's Codon library next to the model, the way typesafe-codon puts it on CODON_PATH, and import typesafe_carla.carla as carla (the import the runtime uses) resolves to it, so a scenario is checked against the whole typed CARLA API. typesafe_carla's Python-API compatibility shortcuts (such as calling a Vehicle method on a plain Actor) compile, as they do outside strict mode. Nothing in the model runs; test_typecheck_model.py keeps each declaration it compares in step with the Python definition of the same name (parameter names, order, defaults, keyword-only parameters, methods, enum members): every name __init__.codon exports, the names the checked modules or a scenario import from the model beside those (_BOUNDARY), and every name of the model modules that stand for one framework module each (_MODULE_MODELS), which must declare exactly the names compared, beside model-only helpers named _acs_* (the list below). metrics.codon and measures.codon are two of those: each declares the whole of its module's __all__, and the test also compares by value their constants (the keys, VEHICLE_AHEAD_VERSION, the distances and speeds the vehicle-ahead measures read with), each built-in entry of BUILT_IN_METRICS (title, unit, text, aggregation) and of BUILT_IN_MEASURES (unit, text, version), the field types and defaults of Metric, Measure and Bumpers (frozen dataclasses, so @tuples: assigning to a field fails the check, as it fails the run), and the parameters of Metric's and Measure's __new__. Only a built-in's read differs: Python's is a private function of the module, which no scenario can import, and the model's a stub (_acs_unread), since nothing in the model is read. Metric(), Measure() and BaseScenario.register_measure() take any read a world can be passed to that returns a float, an int, None, or an Optional of a float or an int -- a function returning float, lambda world: None -- as Python's do, and refuse any other return type (a str, say) at the line that passes read, with "expected a float (or an int)". The three share that check (_reader.codon, outside measures.codon, which imports scenario_base), and Measure is defined there too, so BaseScenario.measures can return a Dict[str, Measure]; measures.codon re-exports it. Metric() and Measure() store the stub: a Codon Callable field takes a function of its exact type only, and Codon 0.19 crashes on any other. set_measured_scenario() takes a scenario of any BaseScenario subclass or None, which Python annotates Optional[BaseScenario]: Codon's Optional takes no subclass.

register_pre_tick(), register_post_tick() and register_init() take an Optional action or callable (#537): Codon does not narrow an Optional after if a is not None:, so the value registered there is still one, and the model unwraps it (None itself is refused). A reader that is maybe_float or 0.0 is a Union for Codon and passes the reader check (#538). An Optional of a subclass held where its base is declared (c: Optional[BaseCondition] = ElapsedTimeCondition(...), or an Optional[BaseCondition] helper parameter) is Codon's to refuse, in the scenario's own code (#541): the message says to declare it without Optional. to_lanelet2() is one untyped definition, as to_carla_world() is, because Codon tries only the last of two typed overloads; test_typecheck_model.py fails on a model function defined twice.

An actor is checked by kind for the same reason (#278). follow_with_spectator() and log_actor_position() take a getter Python types Callable[[], Optional[carla.Actor]], and initial_speeds_mps() an Optional[carla.Actor]. Each takes a carla.Actor, any subclass of it (carla.Vehicle, carla.Walker, carla.Sensor, ...), an Optional of one, or None. A getter returning a carla.Vehicle is the natural one to pass, because typesafe_carla keeps a vehicle's controls on carla.Vehicle. Codon 0.19 refused an Optional[carla.Vehicle] for an Optional[carla.Actor], so these parameters are generic in the model. The model's _expect_optional_actor unwraps the Optional and upcasts a class of a hierarchy to carla.Actor, the way a hook result is checked. Anything else is refused at the call, the framework's EgoVehicle (lambda: self.ego_entity) included:

scenario.py:70:9: error: BaseScenario.follow_with_spectator(): the getter must return a carla.Actor (or a subclass of it, such as carla.Vehicle), or None

register_cover()'s values= and ignore=, and OddAttribute(values=), are checked as openodd uses them (#279). values= must be None, an iterable (a list, a tuple, an empty one too, a set, a str, a range) or an enum class, the framework's (values=TurnDirection) or the scenario's own. Nothing is iterated: the enum class is read as a value of the type, not looped over (see Iterating an enum). ignore= must be None or a callable that takes one value of the type expression returns, unwrapped from its Optional, since the collector never passes None. The model calls it with such a value, so its body is compiled too. A wrong ignore was the worse gap. The collector calls it inside a try, and counts an exception as "cannot bucket ... counted as no sample", so a wrong ignore emptied the item for the whole run, with one warning line. What ignore returns is tested for truth, which Python takes of any value, so the result is not checked:

scenario.py:68:9: error: BaseScenario.register_cover(): ignore must take one argument, a value the expression returns
scenario.py:68:9: error: BaseScenario.register_cover(): values must be an iterable of the bucket values (a list, a tuple or an enum class), or None

What test_typecheck_model.py compares, model by model:

  • Every name __init__.codon exports, with the object of the same name in the package.
  • coordinate.codon: beside its exports, lanelet_length, on_lanelet, project_onto_road, road_traffic_rule, project_onto_lanelet, get_stop_line_linestrings, get_stop_line_linestrings_with_following, find_traffic_lights_for_lanelet2_id, get_signal_ids_for_controller, to_map_frame, MapManager, map_origin, resolve_projector, _parse_geo_reference, and pyxodr's RoadNetwork and lxml's element (below).
  • conditions.codon: beside its exports, ActionStateCondition, LaneChangeSettledCondition, compare, beside_lane_id, and ConditionStatus, all but its details (a dict[str, Any], which Codon cannot express: _OMITTED_PARAMETERS), and no other name it defines (find_actor_in_list it imports from entity_role.codon, as Python's conditions.base does). ActionStateCondition's state is an ActionState or its OpenSCENARIO name, and its actions any dict of action ids to actions: actions.codon imports conditions.codon, so an action is checked by what BaseAction declares.
  • entity_role.codon: beside EntityRole, find_actor_in_list (a carla.ActorList or a list of actors, as Python's) and find_actor_in_world.
  • kinematics.codon: beside its exports, normalize_angle_deg, and frame_of and FrameMismatchError as coordinate.codon declares them.
  • coordinate.codon: AnyPose, the Union alias, by its members' names, in order, for a scenario's own annotations (no model function takes it: a Union parameter crashes Codon 0.19, so each is generic or overloaded).
  • constants.codon: every constant, by value (EGO_ROLE_NAME as EntityRole.ego()), and no name constants.py lacks.
  • route.codon: every name it declares -- parse_anchor, scenario_route, scenario_route_frame, RouteFrame, RouteMatch, and APPROACHES, CROSSWALK_LEGS and SIDES by value. RouteMatch's constructor is generic: Python's is a frozen dataclass of variadic tuples (tuple[int, ...]), which Codon cannot express, but the model's takes the same parameters, and an overload of none is a compile_error (Codon builds a class without fields with no arguments otherwise; see What Codon builds by the fields below), so a call Python refuses fails the check too.
  • trajectory.codon: beside its exports, ResolvedTrajectory, TrajectorySample and the TrajectoryPosition Union, by its members' names, in order, and no other name.
  • traffic.codon: every name it declares -- TurnDirection, LaneChangeDirection, TrafficContext and traffic.registry's functions and TRAFFIC_BACKEND_ENTRY_POINT_GROUP (by value). TrafficBackendFactory differs on purpose (_DIFFERING): a Callable alias in Python of a mapping of any values (Hydra's options), which Codon has no type for, and an empty class in the model, there only so the checked traffic package's re-export resolves; a test checks that it stays empty.
  • utils/traffic_light.codon: its three functions, and no other name.
  • coverage.codon, entity.codon, odd.codon: the names the checked modules import (_BOUNDARY), COVERAGE_SCHEMA and CoverGroup by value.
  • The models of one framework module each (_MODULE_MODELS): _bridge_pose, action_state, carla_install, debug_markers, trajectory_recorder, environment, autoware_bridge/grpc_server, autoware_stack/launcher, autoware_stack/devcontainer (and its values), driver/egodriver_client, _map_source, maps/cache, maps/z_offset_cache, maps/road_network_cache, ui/models, _ros2, metrics, measures and utils/traffic_light, each declaring exactly the names compared; ros2/cyclone where cyclonedds is installed.
  • Every public name of a modelled module: each name a module the model has exports in Python (its __all__, or the public names it defines when it has none) is declared by the model or listed, with the reason, in typecheck/not_modelled.py (NOT_MODELLED), and a name listed there must be neither declared nor gone from Python. Each declared one is compared as above, re-exports included (kinematics.frame_of). OddSample and OddCase differ on purpose (_DIFFERING): an opaque, unbuildable stand-in for openodd's sample, and the @tuple of the pair Python's alias names.
  • Every public member of a compared class (#265): the comparisons above check that what a model class declares exists in Python; this checks the converse. For every class they compare, enums included, each public method, property, class attribute, dataclass field and instance attribute the package's Python, or openodd's, defines on the class or a class it derives from (VehicleEntity.set_desired_speed() is BackendDriven's) is declared by the model class or one of its model bases, or listed, with the reason, in NOT_MODELLED_MEMBERS (typecheck/not_modelled.py), under the class or the Python base that defines it (BaseCondition.get_details for every condition). openodd's classes, which the package re-exports (OddAttribute, OddModule, OddDefinition, OddCondition, CoverItem, CrossItem, CoverageReport), are compared as the package's are (#298), each listed under the name the package gives it (openodd's Condition is OddCondition). A listed member must still be public in Python and absent from the model. A dataclass's public field is a member too, beside the constructor's parameter it is compared as (#298): the model declares it as a field or, where a field would change the constructor Codon generates (What Codon builds by the fields, below), as a read-only property (RouteMatch.lanelet_ids, a List[int] for Python's tuple[int, ...]; TrajectoryVertex.position, the union of the ten poses, which narrows with isinstance and passes on to a new TrajectoryVertex, and which the None check's pass refuses un-narrowed where one pose is expected, #309; CoverItem's fields). A frozen dataclass's field is read-only in Python too; writing a CoverItem's is refused, which Python allows, and a scenario, which registers its items with register_cover(), has none to write. An attribute a method sets on the instance (self.<name> = ... or setattr(self, "<name>", ...), read from the class's source, __init__'s and the others', openodd's included; one set under a name computed at run time is not found) is a member too (#307), as Python reads it like any other: the model declares it as a read-only property, since a field would change the constructor Codon generates (TimeoutCondition.timeout_seconds, OddDefinition.attributes, OddAttribute.target and item, TrafficSinkAction.removed, RouteFrame's match, map, graph and lanelets). Writing one is refused, which Python allows ('TimeoutCondition' object has no attribute 'timeout_seconds'), except in the __init__ of a scenario's own subclass, where the assignment declares the subclass's own attribute. An enum is compared beyond its members (#307): a model enum is a @tuple of its value, so Codon gives it no Enum, and it declares Enum's name as a property, a chain of if self == Rule.MEMBER: return "MEMBER" that test_typecheck_model.py compares with each member's Python name, in order (it also compares each member's value), and its own methods and properties (ComparisonRule.text, CollisionTargetType.matches(), LaneChangeDirection.to_carla_bool()). A scenario's own enum gets its name from the check's rewrite (below). The scenario check adds the reason to Codon's error:
scenario.py:68:19: error: 'CaseScenario' object has no attribute 'traffic_backend': BaseScenario.traffic_backend is not part of the Codon model, on purpose: takes or returns the run's TrafficBackend, ...

Left out are what returns or takes a value Codon has no type for (a dict[str, Any]: a condition's get_details() and to_summary_dict(), to_dict(), describe(), RouteMatch.to_config() and from_config()), the run's traffic backend (set_traffic_backend(), traffic_backend), RouteMatch.junction(), junctions and segments (a RouteSegmentMatch), a field of Any (ConditionStatus.details, RouteLanelet.values, OddModule.metadata, SweepConfig's Hydra mappings, CoverItem's expression, ignore and values, OddAttribute.probe), a class held as a value (BaseScenario.ego_type: a scenario reads ego_requires_goal and calls create_ego()), RouteFrame.features (route.geometry's queries, which the library check compiles from their source), openodd's evaluation, sampling and archive of an ODD (OddDefinition.evaluate(), sample(), archive(), ..., OddCondition.evaluate()) and its report's rows (CoverageReport.entries, ...), and the members of the classes the model declares for the library check alone (CarlaDriverEntity, the egodriver and bridge servers, the ROS 2 transport and its config, the map cache's MapSource, RunEnvironment). An ODD's members compile as they run:

roads = OddModule("roads", include_and=[location.is_in(["urban"])], labels=["fair"])
roads.as_situation(cover_by="meters", target=100.0)
text = roads.conditions()[0].describe() + roads.labels[0] + location.cover_by
for attribute in odd.attributes:
    text += attribute.name + str(attribute.target)

So do an instance attribute and an enum's name and methods:

timeout = TimeoutCondition(cfg.timeout_seconds, label="timeout")
logger.info("limit %f, %s", timeout.timeout_seconds, ComparisonRule.LESS_THAN.name)
logger.info("%s %s", ComparisonRule.LESS_THAN.text, LaneChangeDirection.LEFT.to_carla_bool())
- Every model file: each .codon of the package's model is in one of the tables above or exempt with the reason (_UNCOMPARED_MODEL_FILES: the model's helpers, the modules coordinate.codon and entity.codon re-export, and the __init__ of a checked subpackage, which models nothing), so a model file no test compares fails the suite. - Third-party models: carla_driver_interface's geometry, python-dotenv's load_dotenv, pyxodr's RoadNetwork and lxml's element.

A constant whose model value is a literal (a str, int, float or a tuple of them) is compared by its value and type (a tuple's items' too: 1 is no 1.0 or True) wherever it is compared, and a Literal alias (ui.models.Status) as the type of its values. Any other constant fails the comparison unless a test of its own compares it (EGO_ROLE_NAME, BUILT_IN_METRICS, BUILT_IN_MEASURES).

What Codon builds by the fields. Codon 0.19 gives every class a constructor of its fields, its bases' first, by position or by name, beside the __init__ it declares: a class without fields is built with no arguments (VehicleEntity(), #225), a condition or an action with the label it inherits alone (TimeoutCondition("10"), TurnAction("npc1"), #236), and any class by fields its constructor does not take (DebugMarkers([]), CoverItem("speed"), RunProgress(1, 2, "case", "running"), #244), where Python refuses each. A class that derives from one of Codon's exceptions (Static[Exception]) also takes its bases' constructors, and its fields start with BaseException's eight: FrameMismatchError("x") passed by Exception(typename, msg="") (#244). A class that derives from a model class plainly does not take its base's __init__.

Codon tries the __init__ overloads a class declares from the last one up, and those it generates or inherits only after them, so the model declares, ahead of the constructor, an __init__ of as many arguments whose body is a compile_error:

class TimeoutCondition(BaseCondition):
    def __init__(self, label):
        compile_error("TimeoutCondition(): no constructor takes these arguments "
                      "(required: keyword label)")

    def __init__(self, timeout_seconds: float = 60.0, *_kw, label = _Required()):
        ...

The constructor, declared last, still wins every call it takes (TimeoutCondition(label="t"), TimeoutCondition(10.0, label="t")); the refusing overload only takes what would reach Codon's own. The one of as many arguments as the class has fields takes the fields' names, so a call by them (CoverItem(name="speed")) is refused too.

test_typecheck_model.py compares the last __init__ with Python's and finds the overloads needed. For every compared class that declares an __init__, it counts each number of positional arguments the constructor Codon generates (the fields, _codon_fields) or an exception base's (_inherited_inits, Codon's own read from _CODON_EXCEPTIONS, which a test compares with Codon's standard library) would take, and asks Python whether its constructor binds as many placeholders (inspect.signature().bind). Where Python refuses and the model's constructor does not take them either, the model declares the refusing overload of that many; where the model's constructor takes them through *_kw, its _keyword_only(_kw, ...) refuses them (OddModule, OddAttribute, BaseScenario). The classes it finds:

Arguments Classes none RouteMatch, RouteFrame, VehicleEntity, PedestrianEntity, CoverageCollector, CoverageReport, EgoDriverGrpcClient, Ros2EgoTransport (and CycloneRos2Transport, compared apart) the label the conditions and actions whose constructor Python refuses one argument (SpeedCondition, TurnAction) the fields DebugMarkers, CoverItem, OddCondition (one), RunProgress (four) an exception's FrameMismatchError (one, two, ten), DevContainerError, MapCacheError (none, two, eight)

RouteCoverage declares Python's fields in Python's order (#298), so the constructor Codon generates of them takes no call Python's refuses, and the one it declares refuses each.

Every condition and action declares the overload of one, its label, even where Python takes one argument by position: a call the constructor refuses by its type (TimeoutCondition("10")) would still reach the one Codon generates.

Those constructors take their parameters by keyword too, and a call by keyword Python refuses passes where no guard takes those names: an exception's base parameters (DevContainerError(typename="x"), FrameMismatchError("x", message="y")), or a class's field names (OddAttribute(name="speed", unit="m", text="t"), EntityRole(_value="x")). So the test also enumerates every call, by position and by keyword, the constructor Codon generates or an exception base's would bind, and requires, for each one Python and the model's constructor refuse, a refusing overload that binds it too: an __init__ of the fields' names (OddAttribute, OddDefinition, EntityRole, TrajectoryVertex, EgoConfig, BaseScenario, RunEnvironment), and of typename and typename, message (DevContainerError, MapCacheError; FrameMismatchError takes one positional typename already). A class whose __init__ takes its fields by position and by name needs none: the constructor Codon generates is its own.

A scenario that imports a module with no model (lanelet2's matching, say, or a framework module outside the public API) is refused with a message naming the module. For a framework module, the message says where the model declares the names imported as Python exports them, and only where Python's module has the same object, so the import it suggests runs too; a name the model leaves out on purpose is refused with its reason, whichever module it is imported from (#237):

scenario.py:3: error: autoware_carla_scenario.actions.base is not part of the Codon model; import ActionState from autoware_carla_scenario.action_state instead
scenario.py:4: error: autoware_carla_scenario.route.parse_route_search is not part of the Codon model, on purpose: the route search, parsed from a document's YAML ...

Third-party packages the framework reads are modelled as far as it reads them (lanelet2, pyxodr, carla_driver_interface, python-dotenv; see Making a module compile), and a scenario may use what those models declare.

docs.title: Writing a scenario that type-checks
docs.text: A scenario is ordinary typed Python. Codon is stricter than Python in a few places, and the checker smooths over most of them (it rewrites X | None into Optional[X], drops @dataclass (and appends the ==, ordering and hash it generates) and resolves field(...) defaults, accepts keyword-only parameters, required ones after a default included (a call that passes one by position is refused at the call, as Python refuses it: gap() takes 1 positional argument but more were given: scale is keyword-only,

docs.title: 622), gives a list of different conditions the type
docs.text:
list[BaseCondition], checks a tuple[X, ...] return annotation as a List[X], drops a parameter or return annotation naming a class the module defines further down, which Codon cannot name yet, gives a subclass that keeps its base's __init__ that __init__, and types the return None of a function returning Optional[X]; see below). What a scenario has to do itself:

  • Import its own modules from its own package. A module of the scenario's package imported as a module works (#310): Codon 0.19 resolves from X import name only as a name X/__init__ defines, and an absolute import a.b only from the importing file's directory, so the checker rewrites, on the same line, from . import helpers, from pkg import helpers and import pkg.helpers as helpers in pkg/scenario.py into import helpers as helpers, and from .sub import mod into import sub.mod as mod. A module outside the importing module's package (from .. import helpers in pkg/sub/scenario.py, or import pkg as p) has no such form, and neither has one imported without a name (import pkg.helpers, which binds pkg): each is refused at its line, naming the form that works, which is to import the names (from ..helpers import speed_kph) or to name the module (import pkg.helpers as helpers):
scenario.py:3: error: `from .. import helpers` imports the module pkg.helpers as a module, which Codon 0.19 resolves only inside the importing module's own package (pkg.sub): import the names instead (`from ..helpers import name`)

  • from .helpers import * binds helpers.__all__. When the helper module of the scenario's package sets __all__ as a literal list or tuple of strings, the checker rewrites the star import into an import of those names, on the same line (#506), so a scenario that uses a public name __all__ leaves out is refused (name 'SPEED' is not defined) as Python raises NameError. An __all__ built any other way is not read: the star import then binds every public name of the helper.

  • Import a name once. Python accepts from autoware_carla_scenario import ComparisonRule in the import header and again further down, and so does the check (#354): Codon 0.19 leaves a module-level name imported twice undefined in every module but the one it compiles first, so a use of it failed the whole function with a bare "cannot typecheck". The checker drops a module-level import that repeats an identical earlier one (the same module and name, under the same alias), on its line: the repeat becomes pass, or loses just the repeated names. An import in a function or an if is left as written. A name imported from two different places (from a import X, then from b import X) means the later one in Python: the checker drops the earlier import when nothing reads the name in between, and refuses the later import, naming the first, when something does:

scenario.py:12: error: `ComparisonRule` is imported again from somewhere else (first on line 5) after it was used, which Codon 0.19 cannot compile: import each name once, under its own name (`import ... as other` to tell two apart)
  • Declare the attributes it assigns on self, at class level, with their type:
class MyScenario(BaseScenario):
    _config: MyScenarioConfig

    def __init__(self, ego_config, spawn_pose, config=None, ground_projection=None):
        super().__init__(ego_config, spawn_pose=spawn_pose, ground_projection=ground_projection)
        self._config = config or MyScenarioConfig()

A bare annotation is ignored by Python, so this changes nothing when the scenario runs; Codon needs it to type an attribute of a subclass. The check names each undeclared attribute and suggests its type.

Declare them in every class of the scenario's modules, helper classes included (#218). The check refuses an undeclared attribute of a class with a base, a subclass, or at least one class-level annotation: once a class declares one attribute, Codon gives it only those it declares. A plain class that declares none has its attributes inferred from its __init__, which Codon cannot always do: not for self._samples = [] (a list of nothing yet), and not in a method the scenario check calls on its own (What is checked), on a value its __init__ did not build ('int' does not match expected type 'NoneType', during the realization of get(self: Counter[NoneType])). Codon's error is then at a line of the helper, or names the attribute holding the helper, not the helper (type of attribute '_tracker' of object 'GapCondition' cannot be inferred), so the check adds, for that helper, each attribute it assigns without declaring it, at its line, with the type to declare:

scenario.py:34: error: GapTracker._samples is assigned without a type: declare it in the class body, e.g. `_samples: list[...]` ...

And assign each attribute you declare (#588). Codon gives every field its zero value when the object is built, so a declared attribute nothing assigns reads as 0 (or "", an empty list) in the check, and Python raises AttributeError at its first read. The check refuses a bare class-level annotation (no default; not a dataclass, NamedTuple, TypedDict or Protocol field, nor a ClassVar) that a method of the class or of a subclass reads (self._count, self._count += 1: an augmented assignment reads first) when nothing assigns it, at the annotation:

scenario.py:41: error: CountCondition._count is declared but never assigned: Codon zero-initialises it, and Python raises AttributeError where a method reads self._count; assign self._count in CountCondition.__init__, or give it a default (_count: ... = <value>)

The rule is conservative: the attribute counts as assigned when any module of the scenario stores an attribute of that name, on any object and in any form (self._count = 0, self._count: int = 0, self.a, self._count = ..., setattr(self, "_count", 0), object.__setattr__(self, "_count", 0), other._count = 0), when a framework base assigns it (the base's source, or the framework assigning it from outside; for a mixin, when the framework bases of every scenario class deriving from it assign it: class VehicleInfoMixin: ego_config: EgoConfig mixed into a BaseScenario, but not when a class Plain(VehicleInfoMixin) derives from it too), and when the class or a base gives it a value (a class attribute, a property). A class that assigns attributes by a computed name (setattr(self, name, v), self.__dict__, vars(self)), defines __getattr__, or derives from a class outside the scenario, the framework and the built-ins is left alone.

  • Give a local its type at its first assignment. Codon fixes the type of an unannotated local where it is first assigned; Python and mypy let it widen later. Two common patterns are refused:

  • A float accumulator started at an int literal (total = 0, then total += v with a float v), or a conditional expression with an int literal branch (s = v if v is not None else 0 with v: float | None). Write 0.0. Codon names neither the first assignment nor the literal, so the check adds them (#583):

    scenario.py:74:9: error: 'float' does not match expected type 'int': Codon fixes the type of the local `total` at its first assignment, `total = 0` on line 72, which makes it an int: write `total = 0.0` to store a float in it
scenario.py:72:9: error: 'Optional[float]' does not match expected type 'Optional[int]': Codon fixes the type of the local `s` at its first assignment (here), a conditional expression whose int literal branch `0` makes it an int: write `0.0`

    Codon reports a float passed to an int parameter in the same words, so when the stored value holds a call (k = half(y)), the hint begins "if the float is the value stored in k here".

  • A local first assigned None and rebound later without an annotation, as in a running minimum (best = None, then best = x in a loop). Annotate it: best: float | None = None. Without the annotation, Codon 0.19 either refuses the rebinding ('Optional[float]' does not match expected type 'Optional[NoneType]', which the check completes with the = None line and the annotation) or crashes with no location at all (#584). After such a crash the check keeps the crash and adds, at its = None line, each unannotated local of the checked modules that is first bound to None and rebound, as a likely cause. The type comes from what the local is rebound to where the source says it plainly (a literal, an annotated parameter, the element of an annotated list it loops over); otherwise it is written <T>:

    error: Codon failed without a diagnostic: exit status -11
scenario.py:72: error: Codon crashed (exit status -11); a likely cause: Codon fixes the type of the local `best` at its first assignment, `best = None` on line 72, and cannot widen it when it is rebound (line 75): annotate it: `best: float | None = None`

    Codon compiles some of these as written (a None first binding read only after an is None test), so a local named after a crash is a candidate, not a verdict: the crash may have another cause. A Codon killed with SIGKILL (exit status -9: the out-of-memory killer, as when two library checks of about 8 GB each run at once) is no crash of the code: the check says so, names no local, and should be run again with more memory free. Like a timeout, it is not kept as the verdict, so the next check of the same program in the process compiles it again (#694).

    The same holds where a conditional expression tests the local before it is rebound, the previous value of a loop (prev = None, then d = v - prev if prev is not None else None and prev = v, #629): Codon decides the test while the local's type is still the unresolved Optional of its = None, completes it as Optional[int], its default, and refuses 'Optional[int]' does not match expected type 'Optional[float]' further on. The check adds the local's = None line and its annotation (prev: float | None = None). A local that is only ever None and that a conditional expression tests (z = None, then z + 1 if z is not None else None, even 1 if z is None else 2) crashes Codon 0.19 with no diagnostic; the check names it after the crash, at the conditional expression. Annotate it, or drop the branch that cannot run. - Write the element types of a class attribute (#482): xs: list[int] = field(default_factory=list), d: dict[str, float], ids: set[int], xy: tuple[float, float] = (0.0, 0.0) or tuple[X, ...]. Codon types a dataclass field, a NamedTuple field and any other attribute declared in a class body (xs: list = [], or a bare xs: list) from its annotation and cannot infer the elements of a bare list, dict, set or tuple ("type of attribute 'xs' of object 'Cfg' cannot be inferred", or a bare Tuple that matches no tuple), whatever the default is. The check refuses the field at its line and names what to write; a bare list or dict in a function's parameter or return annotation compiles, and a bare tuple there gets a hint with the error.

  • Use only the public API from autoware_carla_scenario and its listed subpackages, and the BaseScenario attributes meant for subclasses (ego_config, ego_entity, world, _ground_projection, ...). An import from a modelled framework module must also work in Python (#214): the model declares a few names the Python module does not have (coordinate.RoadNetwork, entity.EgoConfig, actions.ActionState: import it from autoware_carla_scenario.action_state, as Python does) and model-only helper modules (autoware_carla_scenario._tc, _lists), and an import of one inside a function would compile and raise ImportError when the function first runs. So the check imports each modelled module a scenario imports from, in Python, and refuses each name it lacks, as an attribute and as a submodule, at the import's line:

scenario.py:118: error: autoware_carla_scenario.coordinate has no RoadNetwork in Python, whatever its Codon model declares: `from autoware_carla_scenario.coordinate import RoadNetwork` raises ImportError when the scenario runs

An import under if TYPE_CHECKING: is exempt: Python never runs it. - Define every abstract method of what you build (#215). Codon has no @abstractmethod, and the model gives BaseScenario.is_done(), BaseCondition.check() and BaseAction.execute() bodies (its built-in conditions and actions inherit them), so a scenario whose is_done was renamed, or a condition that defines only _check, compiles, and Python refuses to build it (TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class). The check asks Python (inspect.isabstract) about each class of the scenario's modules that is built, the scenario class (the runner builds it) or a class the modules call by name (GapCondition(...)), and refuses one still abstract at its class line:

scenario.py:46: error: GapCondition is built (at scenario.py:99) but leaves abstract check undefined: define it in GapCondition, or Python refuses to build it (TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class)

A class only derived from, such as an abstract base of the scenario's own conditions with an @abstractmethod of its own, is never called and may stay abstract. - Call the framework base's __init__ from yours (#587). A scenario, condition, action or entity whose __init__ never calls super().__init__(...) compiles, since Codon zero-initialises what the base would set, and Python raises AttributeError when the runner reads condition.label or the scenario's ego_config. The check refuses such an __init__ at its def line, naming the base and what its __init__ sets:

scenario.py:52: error: LateCondition.__init__ never calls BaseCondition.__init__, which sets label, _last_satisfied, _last_message on self: Codon zero-initialises them, and Python raises AttributeError where the framework reads them; call super().__init__(...) in LateCondition.__init__

The bases are the framework's classes after yours in the method resolution order whose own __init__ (written, or the one @dataclass generates) assigns an attribute of self; a base whose __init__ assigns nothing, a class with no framework base, and an __init__ that itself assigns every attribute those bases' would, are left alone. So is a subclass of your own condition that defines no __init__; one that defines its own and does not call super().__init__ skips the framework's too, through yours, and is refused. Any mention of __init__ in the body counts as the call, on any path (super().__init__(...), super(Cls, self).__init__(...), BaseCondition.__init__(self, ...), inside an if or a try), as does a call of a method of self when a method of the class calls the base's __init__: the check does not follow paths. With @overload stubs, the last def __init__, the one Python binds, is the one checked. - Pass numbers of the declared type. An int is accepted for a float, but not inside a container: a list[float] parameter wants [1.0, 2.0]. YAML values are converted for you. - An empty [] or () is any sequence (#264). Codon gives an empty display no element type ([] is a List[NoneType], () a tuple of no items), so the model takes one wherever Python takes a Sequence[X] (RoutingAction(EGO_ROLE_NAME, goal), whose waypoints default to (), waypoints=[], self.waypoint_poses = [], derive_goal_from_route(()), AndCondition([], ...), an ODD's all_of([])) through _acs_sequence (_tc.codon), and checks the elements of any other: waypoints=[460, 265] and waypoints=[None] are refused, in EgoVehicle.route_to() too. - A sequence of names is a list or a tuple, not a str (#299). Python's typing takes a str as a Sequence[str], and the framework then reads each of its characters as a name (roots="roads" fails at run time with "no root module ['r', 'o', 'a', 'd', 's']"). Here the check is stricter than mypy, on purpose: _expect_str_sequence (_tc.codon) refuses a str (or an Optional[str]) where a sequence of names is taken, the items of BaseScenario.register_cross(), OddModule's labels and OddDefinition's roots, and takes a list or a tuple of str, an empty one too:

scenario.py:41: error: BaseScenario.register_cross(): items: expected a sequence of names (a list or a tuple of str), not a str: wrap it in a list

OddAttribute.is_in("urban") still passes: it takes an Iterable[Any] of values, and CPython takes a str's characters as values. - Call a manoeuvre your own entity class overrides with every argument, by position. VehicleEntity and EgoVehicle declare the manoeuvres they take from traffic.driven.BackendDriven (set_desired_speed(), change_lane(), lane_change_finished(), turn_at_junction(), release_from_traffic(), ...), and an EgoVehicle subclass's override of one is checked as a hook. Codon 0.19 calls a method a subclass overrides through a dispatch thunk, which takes no keyword argument, fills in no default (set_client(client) needs its tm_port then), and cannot call turn_at_junction(world, direction, **kwargs) at all: once a class of the scenario overrides it, a call of it does not compile ("cannot typecheck"), on the subclass as on its base; turn with a TurnAction instead. A class that only defines the override, and never calls it, compiles. (Declaring Python's **kwargs as TurnAction's three keywords would not help: the thunk fills in none of their defaults, so even turn_at_junction(world, direction) would fail, and a backend's own keywords would be refused.) - A dict of different actions (or conditions) is a dict of their base. Codon types a dict display by its first item, so the check rewrites one whose values are not evidently of one type, as it does a list display: {"turn": turn, "lane_change": lc} (a TurnAction and a LaneChangeAction) becomes {"turn": _acs_base(turn), "lane_change": _acs_base(lc)}, which makes each action a BaseAction (each condition a BaseCondition): a dict[str, BaseAction] as in Python, which passes as ActionStateCondition's actions. Assigned to an annotated variable, actions: dict[str, BaseAction] = {...}, it becomes a dict of the annotated type (_acs_dict_into, when the key and value types are plain names). A value of another type is still refused at the display's line:

scenario.py:73: error: 'int' does not match expected type 'BaseAction'

Any other value is left to Codon's display, which types it as before ({"a": 1, "b": speed} is a dict[str, float], a value with None is optional). Values evidently of one type (all literals, all calls of the same name, all members of one enum) are left as written. Building the dict one item at a time into a dict[str, BaseAction] stays valid. - Convert nested mappings in the config. The runner passes a YAML mapping to the config class as a dict, so a field annotated with a dataclass (goal: Goal) holds one at run time unless the config's __post_init__ turns it into a Goal, as the built-in configs do for their NPC lists. The check builds the config the same way and refuses an unconverted mapping at its scenario.<key>. The same goes for an Enum field (YAML gives its name or value as a str) and a tuple field (YAML gives a list): they compile when the __post_init__ converts them (self.mode = Mode(self.mode)), and are refused at scenario.<key> when it does not. A bad value inside a nested list is refused at its own field, e.g. scenario.legs[1].speed. A config that raises when built (a __post_init__ that rejects a value, a name Mode(...) does not know) fails the check with the exception, as it stops the run.

  • Annotate every parameter of every function and method, helpers and hook overrides included. Every function of the scenario's modules is compiled, whether setup() reaches it or not, with a value of each parameter's annotated type (What is checked). A function with a parameter that has no annotation, one Codon cannot express or one naming a TypeVar, is only compiled where setup() and is_done() call it, and the check warns about it, at the parameter's line; so is one returning Any, with the warning at its def.
  • Give each class-level default a value of its annotated type (RETRIES: int = 3): it is compiled against the annotation.
  • Return what the framework reads from a hook you override: a bool from is_done(), a ScenarioResult or None from a condition's check(), a dict[int, float] from initial_speeds_mps(), None from setup() and an action's execute() (What is checked).
  • Test an Optional for None before using it: a float | None config field, goal_pose, find_actor_by_role_name(...), and CARLA's Optional results (get_waypoint(...), get_actors().find(...), world.get_actor(...), actor.parent).
  • Read **kwargs by name with kw.get(), and test *args, like any tuple, with len() (#266). Codon makes **kwargs a NamedTuple of the keywords passed, not a dict, and *args a Tuple, and gives no tuple a truth value (#278). Codon refuses this valid Python, and the message says what to write instead:
Python Codon's error Write instead for k, v in kw.items(): (.keys(), .values(), for k in kw, len(kw)) 'NamedTuple[a=float]' object has no attribute 'items' kw.get("a", default) for each name, or keyword parameters (def f(*, a: float = 1.0)) if args: / x if args else y, or if window: of any tuple 'Tuple[float,float]' object has no attribute '__bool__' if len(args) > 0: (if len(window) > 0:)

kw["speed"] and "speed" in kw compile for a keyword the call passes; kw.get("speed", 1.0) compiles whether it does or not. A helper taking **kwargs or *args that the scenario calls and that reads them by key or position is compiled through its callers' calls, so it is checked with the keywords and values they pass (What is checked). - Give your own helper an Optional of the class it gets, not of its base. Codon 0.19 does not convert an Optional of a subclass to an Optional of its base (#278). A helper def gap(actor: carla.Actor | None) refuses an Optional[carla.Vehicle], and a plain carla.Vehicle too, which Codon wraps in an Optional first ('Optional[Vehicle]' does not match expected type 'Optional[Actor]'). Python accepts both. A parameter of carla.Actor alone takes a carla.Vehicle, and the framework's own Optional[carla.Actor] parameters take either (What is checked). Annotate the helper with the subclass (carla.Vehicle | None), or test for None before the call and pass the unwrapped value to a carla.Actor parameter. - Build an object of a class you hold in an Optional, when the class has subclasses and nothing else builds one. Codon 0.19 checks x: X | None = None (or a parameter defaulting to None) of such a class, then generates code that LLVM refuses ("LLVM: error: value doesn't match function result type 'ptr'"), when the program builds no X nor any subclass of it, or defines a subclass after Codon compiled X (#263). The model builds its own such classes once, after their subclasses: BaseCondition, BaseAction and lanelet2's ConstLanelet, ConstLineString2d, ConstLineString3d, ConstPoint3d and RegulatoryElement (the others are built by the scenario check anyway). So a scenario that builds actions but no condition compiles, though each action's condition = None is an Optional[BaseCondition], whether it registers the actions or keeps them in a list or dict of BaseAction. A class of your own, or your subclass of a framework class that nothing builds (class MyResult(ScenarioResult)), can still meet it; the check then names the class and what to do, at the class line of it or of its subclass, and keeps no verdict, as for any crash:

scenario.py:73: error: Codon 0.19 generated code it cannot compile for autoware_carla_scenario.conditions.ScenarioResult, a class with subclasses: a bug of Codon's rather than an error of the program (#263). It does so for an Optional of such a class (`x: ScenarioResult | None = None`, a parameter that defaults to None) when the program builds no object of the class or of a subclass, or defines a subclass after Codon compiled the class. Build a MyResult where setup() reaches it, or hold the value without Optional
    LLVM: error: '%obj' defined with type 'ptr' but expected '{ ptr, ptr }'

Annotations Codon cannot express (Union of two types, Any, Callable, Sequence, type[...]) are dropped from parameters, which become generic: Codon then checks each call with the arguments it is given. The appended calls give a union parameter (Lanelet2Pose | OpenDrivePose) each of its members in turn, and a Callable[[A], R] of types Codon can express a value of that signature; Any, object and Callable[..., R] give them nothing to call with, hence the warning.

The checker also rewrites what Codon spells differently: an Enum class (its members become instances with a name and a typed value; a lookup by value, ActionState("completeState"), takes a value of that type and is typed but not resolved to the member; looking a member up by name and iterating over the class work for a scenario's own enum, see Iterating an enum), a class deriving from an exception, a @classmethod (a static method of its class: cls names the class it is defined in), and an annotation naming one of CARLA's integer enumerations (carla.TrafficLightState), which typesafe_carla's Codon library has as a value whose members are int, not as a type: it becomes int.

Two things Python does that Codon 0.19 does not are filled in for you:

  • A subclass that inherits __init__. Codon 0.19 inherits no __init__: it gives a class without one a constructor taking each of its fields, which refused a scenario deriving from another scenario and keeping its constructor ("'config' is an invalid keyword argument for __init__()", #201). The check appends one to such a class, after the module, so no line moves:
@extend
class MyDerivedScenario:
    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)

It is added only where a base really defines an __init__ (a class of the scenario's modules, its own or one it inherits, or one of the model's, such as BaseScenario's), and never to a dataclass, an Enum or an exception, which are built as before. When the __init__ is a later base's (class MyDerivedScenario(MyMixin, MyScenario), the mixin having none), it is called through that base, MyScenario.__init__(self, *args, **kwargs), as Python does: Codon's super() is the first base's. The base's __init__ still checks every argument: a wrong one is reported at the class line of the subclass, with the call that passed it in the trace:

scenario.py:52:9: error: no function 'MyScenario.__init__' with arguments (Super[MyScenario], EgoConfig, Lanelet2Pose, str)
    during the realization of __init__(self: MyDerivedScenario, ...) [scenario.py:58]

A literal None passed through it is refused, though Python takes it (MyDerivedScenario(ego, pose, None), or config=None): forwarded through *args or **kwargs, it reaches the base's __init__ as an Optional[NoneType], which no Optional[X] parameter takes. Leave the argument to its default, pass a variable declared Optional[X], or give the subclass an __init__ of its own.

A subclass with an __init__ of its own that lists a mixin before its framework base (class CaseScenario(VehicleInfoMixin, BaseScenario)) calls super().__init__(ego_config, spawn_pose=..., ...), which Python follows through the MRO past the mixin to BaseScenario.__init__. Codon's super() is the mixin's constructor of its fields, which refused the base's arguments ('ground_projection' is an invalid keyword argument for __init__()), so the check rewrites the call to BaseScenario.__init__(self, ego_config, spawn_pose=..., ...) (#626), which checks every argument against the base's __init__ as before. It does so only where the MRO makes the two the same method: every base before it is a plain mixin of the scenario's modules (no __init__ of its own or inherited, no @dataclass, and only such mixins, object, ABC or Generic[...] as bases). A class whose first base has an __init__, or whose earlier bases the check cannot see, keeps super(); listing the framework base first (class CaseScenario(BaseScenario, VehicleInfoMixin)) always works.

  • return None from a function returning Optional[X]. A bare None is Codon's NoneType, so a function whose only return is return None could not be typed ("cannot typecheck 'None'"), and, when nothing else in the program used X (carla.Actor in a scenario), Optional[X] failed in code generation ("value doesn't match function result type 'ptr'", #202). The check makes each return None (and bare return) of the function itself return Optional[X](), the None of its type (a nested function is rewritten for its own annotation), and the appended calls realize X (_acs_value(X)) before they call it. So
def _find_npc(self) -> Optional[carla.Actor]:
    return None

compiles as written, and so does a local found: Optional[carla.Actor] = None returned at the end.

  • Your own dataclasses, enums and named tuples keep what Python gives them (#365), with these limits:
  • A @dataclass compares, orders and hashes as Python's does: the check appends == and != (eq=True, the default), <, <=, > and >= (order=True) and hash() (frozen=True, or unsafe_hash=True) after the module, comparing the fields in order (a dataclass base's first; field(compare=False) and ClassVar are left out; InitVar and KW_ONLY cannot be imported in the check, see "Standard library names Codon lacks"). A method the class defines itself is kept. This holds for a dataclass whose bases are dataclasses of the same module (or none): one deriving from a class the check cannot see the fields of, such as a framework dataclass, gets none, and == on it is refused. eq=False compares and hashes by identity, as a plain class does (below). Python refuses < without order=True and hash() of a non-frozen dataclass, and so does the check, with a hint naming the flag.
  • A plain class (one that does not define __eq__) compares and hashes by identity, as Python's object does (#596): a in npcs, npcs.remove(a), a == b, {t}, {t: 1} and dict[Npc, float] compile. The check gives each top-level class of the checked modules whose bases are plain (none, object, ABC) __eq__ / __ne__ (self is other) and __hash__ (id(self)), with @extend right after the class, so module-level code and the module's subclasses have them; a __hash__ (or __ne__) the class defines is kept, and a @dataclass(eq=False, unsafe_hash=True) keeps the hash of its fields. A class deriving from a framework class gets the framework model's: BaseCondition, BaseAction, VehicleEntity, PedestrianEntity and EgoVehicle compare and hash by identity in the model, as in Python ({TimeoutCondition(1.0, label="a")} compiles). Enums, named tuples, exceptions, protocols and a class with a metaclass get nothing. A class that defines __eq__ and not __hash__ is unhashable in Python (it sets __hash__ = None), and the check refuses a set of them, or a dict keyed by one, with a hint to define __hash__. The gap: such a class deriving from a plain class of the module (or from a framework class above) inherits the identity hash in the check, so a set of them compiles there and raises TypeError in Python.
  • dataclasses.replace(obj, a=x, b=y) is checked as the typed copy it is (#487): the check appends to each dataclass of the module one _acs_with__<field> method per field the constructor takes, and writes the call as replace(obj)._acs_with__a(x)._acs_with__b(y). An unknown field, a value of the wrong type (replace(w, speed="fast")) and a field declared field(init=False) (which Python refuses too) are refused at the call, and replace(plan, best=None) of an Optional field works. A field a base dataclass declares can be replaced on the base and on any subclass, however many levels (replace(derived, a=5)), also one a subclass redeclares and in a frozen hierarchy (#494): the value goes by position, as Codon cannot pass a keyword to a method a subclass overrides. A wrong value for it is reported as dataclasses.replace: field 'a' of Derived is declared int, not str. Any other error raised inside the _acs_with__<field> method is reported at the replace(...) call, not at the class (#614), also when the call is in another module than the class (replace(cfg.lanes, ids=...) in scenario.py of a dataclass of configs.py, #623). Codon names that module by its file name alone, so when two checked modules share it (configs.py and sub/configs.py) the error stays at the class. It holds for a dataclass the scenario package defines, in any of its modules, also one nested in a class or a function (Plans.Leg, #623: its methods, and its ==, hash and ordering, go at the end of its body, as @extend cannot name it; a nested dataclass whose body is on the class line, class Leg: x: int = 0, gets none), whose bases are dataclasses of the same module (of the same body, for a nested one) or none, and which has no __init__ of its own; for any other class (a framework or library dataclass) the call is refused with a hint to build the object yourself (OpenDrivePose and DevContainer have the methods in their models, as the framework uses replace on them). The object goes by position and the fields by keyword: replace(obj, **changes) and replace(obj, 3.0) are refused. The fields change one after the other, so a __post_init__ is not run between them, and replace(obj) with no change returns obj itself, not a copy (both only matter to the types). A replace that is not dataclasses' (a parameter, a local or another import of that name, str.replace) is left alone.
  • An IntEnum (also IntFlag, class M(int, Enum)) member compares with its value (M.A == 1), orders against a member or an int (M.A < M.B) and converts with int() and float(). A StrEnum or class M(str, Enum) member compares with its string (M.A == "a") and does nothing more: ordering and int() are refused, as in Python for a plain Enum, a Flag and a (str, Enum). A Flag and an IntFlag also combine with |, &, ^, ~ and in (Flag and IntFlag). A plain Enum member equals only members (M.A == 1 is False, as in Python). An enum member is not an int or a str otherwise: passing it to an int / str parameter or doing arithmetic on it (M.A + 1) is refused with a hint. Write M.A.value.
  • An enum is typed by its members' values, which must be literals of one type: all int (a signed one, LEFT = -1, too), all float, all str, or auto(), unless the base gives the type (IntEnum, class M(str, Enum)). An enum whose values are tuples (LEFT = (-3.5, "left"), unpacked into an __init__ that sets self.offset), of different types (A = 1, B = "b"), or not literals (A = WIDTH, A = 2 * WIDTH, A = True) is refused at its class line (#600), with what to write instead: for a record per member, a @dataclass(frozen=True) or a NamedTuple and a module-level dict keyed by a plain enum (LANES = {Lane.LEFT: LaneInfo(-3.5, "left")}), or one enum per field. An enum with no member (a base for others) is not refused.
  • A class Pt(typing.NamedTuple) is checked as a Codon @tuple class: its fields, defaults and methods, ==, ordering, hash(), iteration and len() work. Codon indexes and unpacks it (p[0], x, y = p) only when all its fields have one type: otherwise read p.x, p.y. It has no _replace(), _asdict(), _fields or _make(): build a new Pt(...). Only the class syntax is covered (not NamedTuple("Pt", [...]) or collections.namedtuple).

docs.title: Python the check rewrites for Codon (#376)
docs.text:
Each of these is valid Python that Codon 0.19 refuses or crashes on. The check rewrites the checked copy of your module (on the same lines; what runs is your code as written), so you write the Python you would anyway. A form the rewrite cannot express is refused at its line, with what to write instead.

You write The check compiles Refused when class MyError(Exception): ... the same with pass for ... {**a, "k": v, **b} (a \| {"k": v} \| b); {**a} is dict(a) the values of the parts have other types (Dict[str, int] and Dict[str, str]) "{:>5}\|{a}".format(1, a=x) on a string literal the f-string f"{1:>5}\|{x}" (a complex argument is bound once by a lambda) *args / **kwargs, a field inside a format spec ({:>{}}: write the f-string, which is rewritten), a missing argument, mixed auto and manual numbering, a template that is not a literal (write an f-string) f"{x:+.2f}", f"{n:>{w}d}", a spec Codon's f-string parser does not know the value's own __format__, the f-string a + of its parts: (x).__format__("+.2f"), (n).__format__(">" + str(w) + "d"). A nested field is str(w) (repr(w) for !r and !a); the result is a str, as before. In an f-string rewritten this way (or for a literal brace or !a), a field whose expression holds a double quote or a backslash is a call too, str(e), repr(e) or its __format__ (#704), where it was refused. "{:+.2f}".format(x) is rewritten to the f-string first, so it gets the same a brace or a nested f-string inside an expression of the f-string (below) An f-string (or "{}".format(...), {x=}) in the body of a lambda that reads a name the lambda does not bind: lambda v: f"{v}{p}", sorted(xs, key=lambda e: f"{e}{p}"), lambda v, lab=cfg.name: f"{v}{lab}" (#470) str() parts joined by +: str(v) + str(p); repr(p) for !r, (p).__format__(spec) for a spec, "p=" + repr(p) for {p=}, repr(p) for !a (as for ascii()). Each value is evaluated once, in order, and the result is a str. Codon looks the names of an f-string up in the lambda's own scope ("name 'p' is not defined"); a def or a comprehension does not have that limit. An f-string of the lambda's own parameters is left as written a brace or a nested f-string inside an expression (as above) f"{x!a}", f"{x!a:>6}", f"{{{x!a}}}", "{!a}".format(x) (#701) the same field with !r: f"{x!r}", f"{x!r:>6}"; a field rewritten to a call (a spec Codon does not parse, an expression holding a quote) is repr(x), as ascii(x) is.
