The scenario check is not limited by this: it compiles every scenario against the model. The model does not declare the whole public API: what test_typecheck_model.py guarantees is that every public name of a modelled module, and every public method, property and class attribute of a class the model declares, is either declared or listed with the reason it is left out in typecheck/not_modelled.py (NOT_MODELLED, NOT_MODELLED_MEMBERS), and the check refuses a use of a listed one with that reason (#249, #265). Attributes a class only annotates (set on the instance) are outside that guarantee.

docs.title: What is compiled
docs.text:
Codon checks a function only when something calls it, so the check appends a function to each checked module that calls every function and every method of every class (constructors, static and class methods, properties and their setters, dunder methods, protected _ ones and those of _ classes included) with a value of each parameter's annotated type:

def _acs_library_check():
    normalize_angle_deg(_acs_value(float))
    Vector3(_acs_value(float), _acs_value(float), _acs_value(float))
    _acs_value(Vector3).dot(_acs_value(Vector3))

_acs_value(T) is a T Codon cannot tell from a real one; nothing compiled is ever run. A parameter annotated with a union (Lanelet2Pose | OpenDrivePose, Union[BaseAction, Callable[[carla.World], None]], or an Optional of one, Optional[Union[EntityRole, str]]) is called once with each member, so the body is checked for every type it accepts. A parameter with no annotation, or one Codon cannot express (Any, object, Callable[..., R], Callable[[Any], Any], ...), gives the check nothing to call with and is reported as a problem of the module, at its line: annotate it with the type its callers pass. The exceptions are other: object in __eq__ and __ne__, which Python requires, called with the class itself, and a parameter Codon cannot express that has a default: a function whose every such parameter has one is called only leaving the defaults out (Defaults are compiled too, below), so its body is compiled with them (#199). A Callable whose argument and result types Codon can express (Callable[[carla.World], Optional[float]], a dataclass field too, or an Optional of one) is called with a value of Codon's Callable type, which a function of that signature converts to. One with a union among its argument types (Callable[[Optional[Union[EntityRole, str]]], CarlaWorldPose], the reference lookup of trajectory.resolve) is no type Codon 0.19 can hold: it crashes on it ("union already sealed"). Such a parameter is called with _acs_Returning[R, N] (_tc.codon), a callable that takes N arguments (as many as the Callable does) of any type and returns an R, so the body is compiled with the number of arguments it passes checked, their types unchecked, and with what it gets back checked.

A *args: T is given one T (run_uv(cwd, *args: str, ...) is called with one str), so the body is compiled for it; one with no annotation, or of object or Any (__exit__(self, *args: object)), is given nothing.

A method with keyword-only parameters or **kwargs is called through its class (TrafficBackend.start(_acs_value(TrafficBackend), ..., skip_actor_ids=...)): Codon 0.19 calls a method a subclass may override through a dispatch thunk, which takes neither a keyword argument nor **kwargs, and the call through the class checks the same body.

Defaults are compiled too (#183). The calls above pass every argument, so no default was ever compiled: find_nearest_traffic_light(..., max_distance: float = "far") passed the check. A function or method with a defaulted parameter is now called once more, with only the arguments that have no default, each of its first type:

    find_nearest_traffic_light(_acs_value(carla.World), _acs_value(Lanelet2Pose))
    AutowareBridge.configure(_acs_value(AutowareBridge), _acs_value(BridgePose), _acs_value(BridgePose))

A method is called through its class (AutowareBridge.configure(...), not _acs_value(AutowareBridge).configure(...)): a dispatch thunk fills in no default, and through it AutowareBridge.configure() and FakeAutowareBridge.configure() do not compile. A *args: T is still given one T (run_uv(cwd, *args: str, timeout: int, env=None) with one str and timeout), so the positional parameters before it are passed, defaulted or not: without it run_uv() does not compile. A function with no default gets no such call. An error in a default is reported at the call, which names it (<library check: find_nearest_traffic_light(world: carla.World, location: Lanelet2Pose), with the default ofmax_distance>: error: 'str' does not match expected type 'float').

That was 169 calls more, beside the 1525 others (1694 in all), when it came in. Measured before any fix, 13 of them failed, and all 13 are fixed by the transform, with no change to a module:

  • 11 had a () default on a Sequence[X] or Collection[X] parameter (RoutingAction.__init__'s waypoints, set_mission() / route_to() of BridgeHandshake and BridgedEgoEntity, EgoVehicle.route_to(), the skip_actor_ids of the three traffic backends' start(), utils.vehicles.hold_vehicles_still() and scenario_runner._hold_vehicles_still()). The parameter's annotation is dropped, so the () made it Codon's empty tuple ("'Tuple' does not match expected type 'List[Lanelet2Pose]'"). The transform makes such a default List[X](), as it does a dataclass's field(default=()).
  • 2 had a None default on an Optional parameter whose annotation the transform drops: EgoConfig.__init__'s waypoint_poses: Optional[Sequence[Lanelet2Pose]], and the Callable parameters of trajectory.resolve.resolve_trajectory(). None alone is Codon's NoneType, which has no elements and no call, and a body that tests it for None first is compiled with it all the same. The transform makes such a default the None of the Optional the library check calls with: Optional[List[Lanelet2Pose]](), Optional[Callable[[float, float], Optional[float]]](), and for a Callable with a union among its arguments Optional[_acs_Returning[CarlaWorldPose, 1]]() (the transform's prelude imports _acs_Returning; the check's own function does not import it again, which Codon 0.19 cannot type: "cannot typecheck").

So are the field defaults of a dataclass (#188). The check drops @dataclass, and Codon gives the class a constructor that takes each field, with its default; every constructor call above passes every field, so no field default was compiled: stop_timeout_s: float = "far" on CommandAutowareLauncher passed the check. A dataclass with a defaulted field is now constructed once more, with only the fields that have no default, each of its first type:

    DockerAutowareConfig(_acs_value(Path), _acs_value(Sequence[str]))
    DriverClientConfig()

A field without a default after one with (a field(kw_only=True)) is passed by keyword. A field with no default of its own (field(), or field(init=False), which the constructor leaves out anyway) is not one with a default, and neither is a field "defaulted" to OmegaConf's mandatory-value marker (spawn_lanelet_id: int = MISSING, the string "???"): the marker is no value of the field but a placeholder for one the config must supply, so the call passes the field, and the marker is not compiled against the field's type. Nothing enforces that in Python: reading the field from Hydra's config raises MissingMandatoryValue, but OmegaConf.to_container() returns "???" for it, and a dataclass built without it (NpcVehicleConfig()) holds the string, which the check does not see. A field the call leaves out because its annotation names Any (A dataclass field may hold a union or a free-form mapping, below) is left out of this call too. An error is reported at the call, which names the defaults it leaves out (<library check: CommandAutowareLauncher.__init__(argv: Sequence[str]), with the default ofenv,log_dir,stop_timeout_s>: error: 'str' does not match expected type 'float').

That is 96 calls more, beside the 1694 others (1790 in all, 265 of them leaving defaults out), at the time of writing. Measured before any fix, 5 of the 96 failed, at the first error of each. Those 5 classes have 10 defaults Codon refused, of four causes; all are fixed in the check, with no change to a module and nothing UNCALLED (9 by the transform, whose output changes at those 9 defaults alone, and 1 by the call):

  • 3 had a tuple display default on a Sequence[X] or tuple[X, ...] field (DockerAutowareConfig.colcon_args, DriverClientConfig.cameras and map_formats). The field is declared as a List[X] (the typing shim's Sequence is List), and the display is a fixed-length Codon tuple ("'Tuple[str,str,str]' does not match expected type 'List[str]'"). The transform makes it List[X]([...]), a list of the field's element type, replacing only the brackets, so the elements are rewritten as anywhere else.
  • 4 had a plain () default on such a field (DockerAutowareConfig.ros_domain_ids and docker_args, DriverClientConfig.lidars, PlannedRoute.via), which only a field(default=()) of a tuple[X, ...] was typed for. The transform makes it List[X](), written directly or through field(default=()), for a Sequence[X] as for a tuple[X, ...].
  • 2 had field(default_factory=dict) on a Mapping[str, str] field (env of DockerAutowareConfig and of CommandAutowareLauncher): the factory is typed only for a dict[K, V] field, so it was a bare {}, a dict of None ("'Dict[NoneType,NoneType]' does not match expected type 'Dict[str,str]'"). The transform makes a list, dict or set factory of an abstract collection the concrete one the typing shim maps it onto, of the field's types (Dict[str, str]()).
  • 1 was the OmegaConf marker on an int field (NpcVehicleConfig.spawn_lanelet_id: int = MISSING, "'str' does not match expected type 'int'"), which the call now passes, as above.

So are class-level defaults (#190). On a class with a constructor, its own or a base's, Codon makes a class-level x: T = v a field and drops v: no call compiles it, and BackendDriven._tm_port: int = "x", BaseScenario.STABILIZE_TICKS: int = "a" and AutowareEgoEntity.stack_name: str = 1 passed the check. The check's function now assigns each such default to a local of its type, which compiles the value against the annotation:

    _acs_cls_default_10: int = DEFAULT_TM_PORT
    _acs_cls_default_13: bool = _expect_bool(True)

Each local is named after its line in the function, and an error is reported at it, labelled with the member (<library check: class-level default of BackendDriven._tm_port>: error: 'int' does not match expected type 'str'; Codon names the two types the other way round in an annotated assignment). A bool default goes through _expect_bool() (_tc.codon): Codon converts any value assigned to a bool local with its __bool__, so ready: bool = "x" would compile, and a call converts nothing. A default written without an annotation, overriding one a base declares (REISSUES_BY_DEFAULT = True on TrajectoryRun (RoutingAction's engine), whose base declares REISSUES_BY_DEFAULT: ClassVar[bool] = False), is checked against the base's annotation, a ClassVar[T]'s T; the base is found by name among the classes of its module and the other checked modules, depth first. Left out:

  • the defaults of a dataclass, compiled by the constructor call that leaves them out (above), and the members of an enum, which are its values;
  • a ClassVar, which Codon keeps as a class variable, with its value;
  • every default of a class that has no __init__, its own or a base's, and that its module's top level constructs with no argument (_CACHE = _Cache() in measures): Codon's generated constructor takes each field with its default, and that call compiles them already (an error is reported at the call);
  • a default without an annotation that no base declares (a base outside the checked modules), a dunder (__slots__), and one over a bare ClassVar;
  • an annotation Codon cannot express or naming a TypeVar, and a value or annotation naming anything else the class body binds (TWICE: float = LIMIT * 2; a member unpacked, LOW, HIGH = 0.0, 1.0; a method; a nested class), which at the function's scope names something else, or nothing.

That is 22 defaults, at the time of writing: 20 annotated ones, in 10 classes (BaseScenario, the five ego entities, TurnAction, CollisionCondition, DrivenEntity and BackendDriven), and the 2 unannotated overrides of BaseAction.REISSUES_BY_DEFAULT (TrajectoryRun, _BackendAction). Of the 34 non-ClassVar class-level defaults outside dataclasses and enums, the other 14 are those of measures' _Cache, _Lines and _FrameMemo, which the module constructs; the 7 ClassVars are left out. None failed when it came in.

So are the values a function returns as a tuple[X, ...] (#191). Codon's tuples have a fixed length, and the transform dropped such a return annotation, so nothing checked what the function returns: signals.registry.registered_signal_controllers() returning 1 passed the check. A class-level tuple[X, ...] is a List[X], and tuple(x) of a list is one, so the transform now writes the return annotation as List[X] (Optional[List[X]], dict[str, List[X]] inside another type), and the error is reported at the return. It stays dropped when it names an abstract collection (a parameter's is dropped, so the function may return it as it got it), a class defined further down the module or a TypeVar, and so does a Union, Any or Callable return (a Callable return kept fails for a nested function). That is 10 return annotations, in 6 modules, at the time of writing: actions.routing, maps.resolver, route.model, signals.registry, 3 in ros2.config and 3 in signals.controller (one of them dict[str, tuple[int, ...]]). None failed when it came in.

Protected functions and methods are called too (#175). A _ method is often a hook a subclass or another module uses: six example scenarios call BaseScenario._setup_ego_spawn(), and the model's BaseScenario is what a scenario compiles against, so before the driver called it, nothing compiled its real body, and an error injected into it passed the check. The check now calls every _ function of a checked module and every _ method of its public classes, as it calls a public one: about 340 of them, beside about 920 public ones. Measured before any fix, 25 of them failed: 15 had a parameter the check cannot call with, 8 a bare np.ndarray parameter, and _setup_ego_spawn() and scenario_runner._build_condition_status() did not compile. 12 were fixed in the module (shape-typed arrays, an annotated local, an lxml element type for coordinate.transform._cubic(), and the driver taking Optional[Union[A, B]]), and 13 are UNCALLED, each with the reason, most of them because they take Any and only an UNCALLED function calls them.

The methods of _ classes are called too (#182). A _ class is a module's own helper, and was left to be compiled through what uses it, but what uses it does not always compile it. Of the 42 methods of the 20 _ classes of the checked modules, an error injected into each found 4 that nothing compiled: _Never.__init__ and _BackendAction.__init__ (actions.background_traffic), reached only from constructors that are UNCALLED; _BackendAction.set_traffic_backend(), which BaseScenario._hand_backend_to() calls behind a hasattr() on a BaseAction, which Codon decides statically as false; and route.search._Search.__post_init__(), which Codon's constructor does not call. The check now calls them as it calls a public class's: 53 calls (for the 48 methods of the 21 _ classes there are since #180), beside about 1470 others, none with a parameter the check cannot call with. Measured before any fix, 3 of the first 47 failed, and all 3 were fixed in the module: _ScenarioClock declares the _world and _simulated_start it assigns on self, and _BackendAction.__init__ branches into a BaseCondition local instead of choosing between until and _Never() with a conditional expression, which Codon 0.19 cannot type. Each of the 4 now reports an injected error. Two things are left out:

  • a module's dunders (PEP 562's __getattr__), which are Python's hooks, not the module's code; a class's (__eq__, __enter__) are called, as before;
  • what UNCALLED names, as for a public function.

A protected member that calls an UNCALLED one calls it in the else branch of if TYPE_CHECKING:, as a public one does (see A call into a module Codon cannot compile, from a function it must below). _setup_ego_spawn() needs no such branch: the register_route_to_goal() it ends with is checked (#174).

A constructor is compiled with the defaults of what Codon cannot express (#199). BaseScenario.__init__ takes the ego's class (ego_type: type[EgoVehicle] | None = None), and Codon cannot hold a class as a value, so the whole constructor was UNCALLED, though only one line stores it: its other ~25 lines were compiled nowhere (the example scenarios compile against the model's BaseScenario), and an injected self._tm_port = "x" passed every run. A function some of whose parameters Codon cannot express, each with a default, is now called once, leaving out every defaulted argument, instead of being a problem:

    BaseScenario(_acs_value(EgoConfig))

and the one line that stores the class is under if not TYPE_CHECKING:, which Python runs and Codon does not (ego_type stays declared at class level, so ego_requires_goal still reads it). The error is reported at its line, through the call that leaves the defaults out (<library check: BaseScenario.__init__(ego_config: EgoConfig), with the default ofspawn_pose,ground_projection,random_seed,ego_type,ego_entity>). A parameter Codon cannot express with no default is a problem as before, and so is a defaulted one that call would still pass (one before a *args: T, which is given one T). ConditionStatus.__init__ (its details: dict[str, Any]) and TrafficConfig.__init__ (a backend's options, dict[str, Any]) are compiled the same way, with no UNCALLED entry, so a wrong default of one of their other parameters is reported (#217).

Property setters are called too (#200). Codon compiles an @x.setter only where something assigns the property, so an error injected into the setter of ScenarioRunner.xodr_path passed a run of scenario_runner alone: only the full run found it, through ScenarioQueue.start(). The check now assigns each property that has a setter, once with each member of the annotation of the value it takes:

    _acs_value(BaseScenario).goal_pose = _acs_value(Optional[Lanelet2Pose])
    _acs_value(ScenarioRunner).xodr_path = _acs_value(Optional[Path])

An error is reported at its line, through <library check: ScenarioRunner.xodr_path (setter)>. That is 3 assignments, for the 3 setters of 2 modules (scenario_base and scenario_runner), at the time of writing; none failed when it came in. A deleter is not called. The scenario check appends the same calls to a scenario's own modules (#197), so a setter of a scenario nothing assigns is compiled too.

docs.title: Checked modules and the model
docs.text:
The checked modules are compiled next to the same model the scenario check uses. Every import of the framework in a checked module is pointed at what stands in for it in the check's workspace:

  • another checked module: its own (rewritten) source;
  • any other module: its model, the codon/autoware_carla_scenario/ module of the public package it belongs to (coordinate.poses is modelled by coordinate.codon), or, for a module of a package that is itself checked, a model of that module alone (utils/traffic_light.codon, autoware_bridge/grpc_server.codon, driver/egodriver_client.codon, maps/cache.codon, autoware_stack/devcontainer.codon, ros2/cyclone.codon), or, for a module of the top-level package, a model of that module (carla_install.codon, for server, declares installed_executable(); trajectory_recorder.codon, for scenario_runner, the TrajectoryRecorder it starts, records and closes, whose JSON lines hold values of mixed types; environment.codon, for scenario_runner, capture() and the id of the RunEnvironment it returns; weather_rules.codon, for visibility and actions.environment, the weather_range(), vehicle_range() and vehicle_rules_in_use() they read the weather rules through). A module with no model (utils.config) cannot be imported by a checked module until it is checked itself.

Each checked module gets the __file__ Python sets on it (its source's path, a str), which Codon 0.19 does not, bound on the last line of the prelude so it exists before any code of the module and no line moves (#515), so Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "data" and os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)) compile at module level and in a function: autoware_stack.bridge_node finds the installed autoware_bridge package with from ..autoware_bridge import __file__. Codon has no module object, so from .. import autoware_bridge and autoware_bridge.__file__ do not compile.

Two checked modules that import each other can each need the other's types the moment Codon reads it: BaseScenario declares _measures: dict[str, Measure] at class level, and measures declares the running scenario (_MEASURED: dict[str, Optional[BaseScenario]]) as a global, so neither can be read first. MODELLED_IMPORTS in typecheck/library.py breaks such a cycle: the module it names (measures, entity.ego) imports the other (scenario_base) through its model, as it did before that one was checked. Its types are the model's, which never meet the checked module's. The egos derived from EgoVehicle (entity.bridged_ego, entity.autoware_entity) do not override EgoVehicle.spawn(), so they never name EgoConfig and need no entry: Codon 0.19 cannot call super().spawn() through an intermediate class ("'EgoVehicle' does not match expected type" in its dispatch thunk), and an override that repeated the spawn instead would take scenario_base through the model as entity.ego does. Through the checked scenario_base, a run with an example scenario in it failed in Codon 0.19's code generation (LLVM: error: value doesn't match function result type '{ ptr, ptr }', in opt_ref_new of the model's BaseScenario).

A model module that stands in for unchecked code declares only what the checked modules and scenarios use of it. coordinate.codon still declares, of coordinate.projection, the map_origin(), resolve_projector() and _parse_geo_reference() that coordinate.map_manager and sweeper.map_loader import, though the library check now compiles all three from their source. Its MapManager is now the scenario check's alone: the library check compiles map_manager.py from its source, which every checked module imports, and nothing of the model takes or returns a MapManager, so it needs no REPLACED_MODELS entry.

A checked module is compiled under a name of its own (_acs_lib.autoware_carla_scenario__coordinate__frames), since Codon reads the workspace's packages only from .codon files and names a file in its errors by its base name alone; errors are reported at the line of the real source file. A type a checked module defines is not the type the model declares under the same name, so a checked module cannot hand its own value to a model function that wants the model's: check modules bottom-up, before the modules that use them.

Where the model's functions take the types a checked module defines (the poses, which to_opendrive takes and returns), the model's own declarations of them live in a model module of their own (_poses.codon), which REPLACED_MODELS in typecheck/library.py names with the modules it models. Once those are all checked, the library check compiles that model module as a re-export of their definitions, so the model and the checked modules share one Lanelet2Pose. A name the model declares that none of the checked modules defines is reported.

docs.title: Conditions: the checked base and the model
docs.text:
conditions.base is checked, so the checked conditions derive from the real BaseCondition (_acs_lib.autoware_carla_scenario__conditions__base), not from the model's. The two are different types that never meet:

  • the scenario check compiles a scenario against the model only; no checked module is in its workspace, and the model's BaseCondition, _expect_condition and _acs_list (which recognises a condition by the model-only _acs_condition marker) are unchanged;
  • the library check compiles the checked conditions against the checked base. A checked module that hands a condition to a model function (an unchecked action) cannot do so until that module is checked too (scenario_base is checked, and imports BaseCondition from conditions.base for that); _acs_list gives a list display of checked conditions the type of its first element (_acs_base leaves a checked condition in a dict display as it is), so a display mixing two checked condition classes waits for the same.

BaseCondition.__init_subclass__, which wraps every subclass's check() to record its last result for the UI, is in UNCALLED: the check sees each check() as written.

actions.base is checked the same way: a checked action takes the checked BaseCondition, so it imports it from conditions.base rather than from the conditions package, which the model stands in for until it is checked. Its BaseAction and ActionState are again not the model's, so conditions.action_state watches checked actions. An action that hands its base a condition of its own making imports that condition from its checked module too (SetSpeedAction's default SpeedCondition from conditions.composition.speed); one whose module is not checked waits for it.

docs.title: Making a module compile
docs.text:
What Codon 0.19 needs that Python does not, beyond the rewrites above:

  • Write an iterator class's __iter__ as a generator (#504): Codon has no __next__ protocol, so for k in Countdown(3) over a class whose __iter__ returns self is refused (expected iterable expression, with a hint). def __iter__(self): while self.n > 0: self.n -= 1; yield self.n compiles, and is valid Python too.

  • A dict display holds one value type (#505): {"a": 1, "b": "x"} is refused even annotated dict[str, Any] (Codon has no usable Any or Union value). Convert the values to str, use a dataclass with typed fields, or use one dict per type. The base-class annotation of #489 is for the scenario's own subclasses only.

  • Annotate what the check calls: every parameter of a function or method it calls, protected (_) ones included, with a type Codon can express. Spell a union out (Lanelet2Pose | OpenDrivePose) rather than through an alias (AnyPose); a union with object or Any in it gives nothing to call with.

  • A default must have the parameter's type (#183): the check compiles each function once with its defaults. A () default of a sequence parameter is checked as an empty List[X], so X must be a type Codon can express and name there: a class defined further down the module is not (the () is left as it is, and fails). A None default of a dropped Optional is typed only for a sequence or a Callable the check can call with; Optional[Callable[..., R]] and Optional[Mapping[K, V]] stay a bare None, so a body that uses them past an is None test fails. A tuple display default (= ("a", "b")) of a sequence parameter is checked as a list of its elements, List[X](["a", "b"]), as a dataclass field's is (#188); a fixed-length Codon tuple is no List[X]. An empty [] / {} default of a list[X] / dict[K, V] parameter (or [] of a sequence) is checked as an empty one of that type; Codon would make it a list of None. A None default is not checked against its annotation: Codon makes speed: float = None an Optional[float], which passes (mypy, in pre-commit, reports it).
  • Declare attributes on any class in a hierarchy (exceptions included) and on a class with __slots__, at class level (_value: str).
  • A class-level default is compiled as written (#190): the library check assigns it to a local of its annotation in its own function, which the transform does not rewrite. So a default the transform would rewrite in a dataclass (a tuple display or () of a tuple[X, ...] member, frozenset()) is reported: assign such a value in __init__ instead. A default naming another member of the class (TWICE: float = LIMIT * 2), or anything else its body binds, is not checked, as at the function's scope the name is not the member; neither is a None default, which Codon makes an Optional of any annotation (x: float = None compiles). An override without an annotation (REISSUES_BY_DEFAULT = True) is checked against its base's annotation only when the base is a class of its module or of a checked one.
  • hasattr() instead of getattr(x, name, default): Codon decides hasattr when it compiles, so the branch for a type without the attribute is never compiled. The check rewrites getattr(x, "name", default) so itself where the name is a literal and x a name or an attribute chain (#590, "Python the check rewrites for Codon").
  • An exception's __init__ passes one message string to super().__init__. An exception class with nothing in its body but a docstring needs that __init__ written out (def __init__(self, message: str) -> None:).
  • d.get(key, default) takes a default of the value's type, as Codon's dict.get does; d.get(key) is an Optional of it, as in Python (the model's _tc.codon declares it). So does d.pop(key, default) (#590, Codon's pop takes the key only), and d.pop(key, None) is an Optional of the value's type. dict.fromkeys(xs) of one argument (#625) is a dict whose values are all None, as in Python (Dict[K, Optional[NoneType]], so it holds only None: give the value in the call, dict.fromkeys(xs, 0), for a dict to fill with other values). Likewise if not x: continue instead of (x or {}), s.startswith(a) or s.startswith(b) instead of s.startswith((a, b)), and if x is None: return None / return x.attr instead of None if x is None else x.attr.
  • A dict of values of different types ({"at": None, "around": None} read back as a tuple and a list) becomes a small class with one declared attribute per key. A cache that told "not read yet" from a read that found nothing with an object() sentinel (cache.get(key, _UNREAD)) keeps the names it has read in a set[str] beside them: odd.probes._Frame holds the frame's waypoint, weather, lanelet tags, ... each Optional, and read, so a read that failed is still kept as None for the frame, as before.
  • Standard modules Codon does not have (inspect, concurrent.futures, ...) are not available to a checked module; the shims of codon/ are. They are these (test_shim_list keeps the list and the files of codon/ in step):

__future__, abc, atexit, contextlib, dataclasses, enum, fnmatch, hashlib, importlib.metadata, json, logging, os, os.path, pathlib, queue, shlex, shutil, signal, subprocess, sys, tempfile, threading, typing, typing_extensions and urllib.parse

tempfile declares mkstemp(suffix=None, prefix=None, dir=None, text=False) and mkdtemp(suffix=None, prefix=None, dir=None) only, with CPython 3.10's signature (a str or an os.PathLike directory; bytes affixes are not declared). The check only compiles it, so its body is a stub that makes no file (it is typed to give (int, str), the descriptor and the name; mkdtemp() gives the str name). NamedTemporaryFile(), TemporaryDirectory(), gettempdir() and the rest are not declared and fail the check. Two more modules are not shims but extensions of Codon's own collections and itertools, in codon/_stdlib/ (#422): they add collections.OrderedDict and itertools.pairwise, as listed under "Standard library names Codon lacks".

Each shim takes the arguments CPython takes, so the check accepts what CPython accepts and refuses the rest; where Python versions differ, it takes what Python 3.10, the oldest the package supports, takes. pathlib declares Path(*parts), /, str(), ==, hash(), expanduser(), resolve() and Path.home() and Path.cwd(); like Python's, it builds and joins a Path with a str or an os.PathLike only (a Path, or what shutil.copy2() returns for one; an Optional of one is unwrapped, as Codon unwraps one passed anywhere). It declares the file-system queries too: exists(), is_file(), is_dir(), glob(pattern), rglob(pattern) and absolute(), with Python 3.10's signatures (3.12 and 3.13 added the keyword-only follow_symlinks, case_sensitive and recurse_symlinks, which are refused), and name, suffix, parent, parents (indexed, iterated, len() and in; not sliced), stem, suffixes, parts (indexed, sliced, iterated, len() and in), root, drive, anchor, as_uri(), with_name(name), with_suffix(suffix) and with_stem(stem) (of a str), joinpath(*other), as_posix(), relative_to(other) (one path, by position: Python 3.10 also joins more parts, but 3.14 refuses them, so the check does too; 3.12's walk_up is refused), is_relative_to(other) (one path, by position, likewise), is_absolute() and the ordering of two Paths, so sorted() takes them. parts is not a tuple here: parts == ("a", "b"), a, *rest = p.parts and tuple(p.parts) are not supported (use list(p.parts) or index it). A Path member, or an os, os.path or shutil name, that CPython lacks too is refused as a typo, with the closest declared name. Nothing touches the file system: a query is False and a glob, or iterdir(), yields nothing; samefile(other_path) and match(path_pattern) are False. is_symlink() takes no argument, as in every supported Python. Of what reads, read_text(encoding=None, errors=None) (3.13's newline is refused) and read_bytes() are declared (autoware_stack.docker reads a launch file and hashes the package.xml files, coordinate.map_manager an OpenDRIVE file); both return "", and read_bytes() returns a str, since the check reads bytes as str (so it takes path.read_bytes() + "text", which CPython refuses, and refuses path.read_bytes().decode(), which CPython takes). BaseScenario calls them under an isinstance test on its parameter's own class, which Codon decides as true, and hands anything else (a test double) to register_entity, so at run time it is registered as before. - carla.TrafficLightState is a value in the check, not a type: its members are ints, as get_state() returns. The check reads an annotation naming one of typesafe_carla's integer enumerations (carla.TrafficLightState, carla.LaneType, ...) as int, so keep the CARLA name (the authoring code generator reads it), and compare with get_state() rather than look a member up by value. A member's name is found through the enumeration's names (for name, member in carla.TrafficLightState.names.items()), which both APIs have, as utils/traffic_light.py does. - A sensor callback gets a carla.SensorData in the check, where the CPython API hands it the measurement itself (a carla.CollisionEvent). Listen through a method that converts only when it has to (if hasattr(data, "as_collision"): data = data.as_collision(), as conditions/collision.py does): Codon decides hasattr when it compiles, and the CPython measurement has no as_<kind>(). The camera and the LiDAR (sensor/) listen the same way, with as_image() and as_lidar(). A bound method of another object (a queue's put) is no listener: wrap it in a method of the sensor. - An array is typed by its shape: Codon's numpy types an array by its dtype and its number of dimensions (np.ndarray[np.float32, 2]), which numpy.typing's NDArray[np.float32] does not say, and Codon has no numpy.typing. Annotate with numpy's shape-typed array instead, np.ndarray[tuple[int, int], np.dtype[np.float32]] (two dimensions), which mypy reads as precisely and the check translates; a shape of tuple[int, ...] or Any, and NDArray, are dropped. An annotation broken over lines keeps its line breaks inside its brackets, so newest: Optional[\n ...\n] = None still compiles. - A measurement's raw_data is a view in typesafe_carla's Codon library, and Codon's np.frombuffer takes the bytes: read np.frombuffer(image.raw_data.tobytes(), ...) under if TYPE_CHECKING: and the CPython raw_data in the else branch, which copies nothing. - queue.Queue[T] is the queue shim's, with CPython's signatures (Queue(maxsize=0), put(item, block=True, timeout=None), get(block=True, timeout=None), put_nowait, get_nowait, empty, full, qsize, and the Empty and Full exceptions). Declare the queue's item type at class level (_frame_queue: queue.Queue[carla.Image]); queue.Queue() in __init__ takes it from there. - threading.Thread is the threading shim's, with CPython 3.10's signature (Thread(group=None, target=None, name=None, args=(), kwargs=None, *, daemon=None), start(), join(timeout=None), is_alive()); the check compiles the call the thread makes, target(*args), so a target that does not take its arguments fails it. args is a tuple, kwargs None and group None. The shim replaces the threading module Codon ships, which Codon's numpy and typesafe_carla's Codon library import for Lock, so it keeps all of that module (Lock, RLock, active_count(), get_native_id(), get_ident()), as Codon has it; a test compares the two. - A datetime is formatted from its fields: Codon's datetime has no __format__, so f"{now:%Y-%m-%d}" is f"{now.year:04d}-{now.month:02d}-{now.day:02d}", the same string for every year from 1000 on (ui.runner._multirun_dir()). - A dataclass derived from a dataclass is constructed with its base's fields first, as Python's constructor and Codon's take them, wherever the base is checked (CarlaCameraSensorConfig(CameraSensorConfig)). Of two bases that both bring fields, Python takes the last one's first and Codon 0.19 the first one's, so such a constructor is a problem: list it as UNCALLED. - No variable-length tuples beyond attributes: Codon's tuples have a fixed length. A class-level tuple[X, ...] and tuple(x) are checked as lists (above), but a tuple built otherwise (a display grown in a loop, a + (b,)) is not, and turning the source's tuple into a list changes what the class does (a frozen dataclass's hash, its equality with a tuple). A function that returns one is checked as returning a List[X] (#191): return tuple(x) of a list (signals.registry.registered_signal_controllers()), not a tuple display, which is a fixed-length Codon tuple, nor (). - No ** of a dict in a call (f(**extra) with extra a dict): Codon unpacks only a named tuple into keyword arguments. Write one call per set of keywords (RoutingAction passes waypoints= only when there are some, in a call of its own). - Literal["a", "b"] is checked as the type of its values (str), an annotation and a module-level alias alike (route.model's Tristate): Codon's own Literal types a compile-time value of int, bool or str only, and the typing shim's Literal is str (its TYPE_CHECKING is declared with Static[bool], Codon's other name for its Literal). A Literal inside a Union/Optional alias is translated the same way. A Literal of values of several types is dropped as an annotation; as an alias it is left as written, which the check rejects. - No getattr(obj, name) with a name built at run time: spell the attributes out (JunctionSegmentSpec.crossing()), and keep the getattr for any other name in the else branch of if TYPE_CHECKING:, so Python still raises the AttributeError it raised. - A method only some entities have (route_to(), which an entity found as a BackendDriven has and a pedestrian does not): ask hasattr(entity, "route_to") and call it under that, and keep the call that raises the AttributeError for an entity without it in the else branch of if TYPE_CHECKING:. Codon decides hasattr by the static type, which lacks the method, so it compiles none of the calls: the check covers the lookup around them, not the calls (RoutingAction.execute()). - lanelet2's map at the model boundary: the checked MapManager hands out its lanelet_map and routing_graph as the lanelet2 model's classes (above), which the checked RouteFrame (route.frame) takes, so the checked scenario_route_frame() (route.active) builds it from them. - A model shared with checked modules is split out: the model's EgoConfig derives from VehicleEntityConfig, and the checked EgoVehicle.spawn() hands its spawn location to the checked spawn_vehicle_actor(). So the spawn locations and the NPC vehicle live in a model module of their own (_vehicle_entity.codon), which REPLACED_MODELS replaces with entity._spawn and entity.vehicle_entity: the model's EgoConfig then holds the checked SpawnLocation. maps.cache is itself checked, and the library check compiles its source; its model (maps/cache.codon) stays for the scenario check, which imports models and not sources, and takes and returns a MapSource from a model module of its own (_map_source.codon), which REPLACED_MODELS replaces with the checked maps.source, so the checked maps.resolver hands the model's GitMapCache its own MapSource. Likewise GroundProjectionConfig (_ground_projection.codon, replaced with coordinate.snap): the example scenarios import it from the top-level package, which is the model, and hand it both to the model's BaseScenario and to the checked VehicleEntityConfig (#99). The top-level package model itself is not replaced: the examples derive from the model's BaseScenario, so their constructors' calls to super().__init__() compile the model's constructor. The checked BaseScenario.__init__ is compiled by the library check's own call, with its defaults; the one line that stores the ego's class (ego_type) is under if not TYPE_CHECKING: (#199). The model of ros2.cyclone (ros2/cyclone.codon, cyclonedds) declares the CycloneRos2Transport constructor that the checked entity.ros2_entity._cyclone_transport() calls; its base Ros2EgoTransport and its Ros2EgoConfig come from a model module of their own (_ros2.codon), which REPLACED_MODELS replaces with the checked ros2.transport and ros2.config, so the transport _cyclone_transport() returns is the checked Ros2EgoTransport, and its body is compiled. For the scenario check, which has no ROS 2 package, the two are stand-ins whose constructors are a compile_error, as for a class a checked package only re-exports (below). - A class a checked package only re-exports is declared in the model by name and constructor: GrpcAutowareBridgeServer (autoware_bridge/grpc_server.codon, grpc), EgoDriverGrpcClient (driver/egodriver_client.codon, grpc) and CarlaDriverEntity (entity.codon, grpc and carla_driver_interface's protocol), which the checked autoware_bridge, driver and entity packages re-export and no checked module builds or uses, and CoverageReport (coverage.codon, openodd's), which the checked coverage package re-exports with merge_coverage(documents), the COVERAGE_SCHEMA string and the CoverGroup enum (ODD, SITUATION, SCENARIO). Each constructor takes Python's parameters and is a compile_error: its config (AutowareBridgeConfig, DriverClientConfig) is a checked class the model does not have, or the class is only ever built by openodd's merge, so a scenario that builds one fails its check rather than passing it with arguments the run would refuse. Such a class derives from nothing in the model: a subclass of the model's EgoVehicle that nothing builds breaks Codon 0.19's code generation for every scenario (LLVM: error: value doesn't match function result type). test_typecheck_model.py compares each with the Python class, and checks that its constructor is the compile_error. Of CoverageReport, which merge_coverage() returns, the model also declares what Codon has types for (runs, scenarios, groups(), group_grade(), to_markdown(), #298). - A Protocol a scenario may take is modelled with what is called of it: the library check compiles autoware_stack.launcher from its source, and for the scenario check autoware_stack/launcher.codon declares the AutowareLauncher that AutowareEgoEntity starts, polls and stops (start(*, name, bridge_address), poll(), stop()), with the prepare() and close() that ScenarioQueue calls (below), and the AutowareEpisode that start() returns. Python cannot instantiate a Protocol, so the model's constructor is a compile_error. - A model function returning a checked class: to_map_frame (coordinate.codon, which the scenario check and the checked modules that import the coordinate package compile against) returns autoware_bridge's BridgePose, which _bridge_pose.codon models (BridgePose, its Vector3 and Quaternion, as @tuples, since they are frozen, and moved_forward()); REPLACED_MODELS replaces it with the checked autoware_bridge.base, so AutowareEgoEntity hands the pose to_map_frame returns to the checked AutowareBridge.configure() (it imports coordinate.transform itself, which is checked, so the library check compiles the real to_map_frame there). - math.hypot of the differences where CPython's math.dist would do (AutowareEgoEntity, actions.background_traffic, where test_background_traffic.py pins the two to the same number): Codon's math had no math.dist when these were written; the check adds it now (see "Standard library names Codon lacks"). - A function whose only return is return None: with an Optional[X] return annotation, the check returns Optional[X]() and realizes X before calling it (Writing a scenario that type-checks, #202), so it compiles as written, as does a local declared Optional[X] = None and returned (_Never.check in actions.background_traffic). Without an Optional annotation a bare None is still Codon's NoneType ("cannot typecheck 'None'"), and del of a parameter is refused. - A method that takes **kwargs, called on a value whose class a checked subclass overrides it in, is called through the base class under if TYPE_CHECKING:, and as written in the else branch: actions.turn calls BackendDriven.turn_at_junction(entity, ...) in the check, since AutowareEgoEntity overrides it and Codon 0.19 calls an overridden method through a dispatch thunk, which takes no keyword argument. The check calls each override through its class. Codon never compiles the else copy, so test_typecheck_else_branch.py guards it: wherever the then branch calls a method through its class and the else branch calls it through an instance, both must pass the same arguments, the receiver aside (#193). - A name the model lacks at the boundary: when a checked module imports a name of a modelled package that the model does not declare (trajectory/__init__.py re-exports ResolvedTrajectory), declare it in the model module. When the package does not export it, add it to _BOUNDARY in test_typecheck_model.py, so it is compared with the Python class as an exported name is. - A Protocol that checked code dispatches through becomes a base class: Codon has no structural typing, and decides isinstance and hasattr by the static type. sweeper.constraints.Constraint was a Protocol; it is an ABC whose evaluate() is abstract (so, as before, it cannot be instantiated itself), and every constraint of the module derives from it. What walks a constraint tree asks each class what to bind (_bind_set_level(), which the composite and set-level constraints override) instead of testing the value with isinstance and hasattr. A constraint of someone else's that does not derive from it still works at run time: the walk takes the duck-typed path for it, in the else branch of isinstance(constraint, Constraint), which Codon decides as true. What a set-level constraint caches (_cached_ids) is a field(init=False, repr=False, compare=False): declared, as Codon needs, but neither a constructor parameter nor part of the repr or the comparisons, and unset until the constraint is bound, as before (dataclasses.fields() now lists it, so dataclasses.asdict() of a set-level constraint includes it, and raises AttributeError before the constraint is bound; nothing in the framework calls either on a constraint). - A Protocol that is only read through (batch_report's _Result and _Status, the results it summarises): each property and method has a typed stub body (return "", return False, return 0.0, return None, return list[_Status](), return dict[str, Any]()) instead of ..., which Codon types as returning None ('NoneType' object has no attribute '__iter__'); a bare [] or {} would be a List[NoneType] or Dict[NoneType,NoneType]. Nothing instantiates or calls the Protocol at run time, so the bodies change nothing there; an abc.abstractmethod on a @property is a Codon syntax error, so an ABC is no alternative. An attribute a result may lack (rerun_recording) is a property of the Protocol, read in try: / except AttributeError:, since Codon's getattr() takes no default. The module imports Collection, Mapping and Sequence from typing (with # noqa: UP035), since Codon has no collections.abc, and writes batch_results.json as text a member at a time, each member through json.dumps({key: value}, indent=2), since an entry was a ** merge of the result's to_dict() (dict[str, Any]) with its own keys. A key both set is written once, where the merge put it and with the value it kept; test_batch_report.py holds the text to what json.dumps of the merged entries gives. - A registry of classes at module level (sweeper.constraints' _LEAF_REGISTRY, sweeper.bindings' _BINDING_REGISTRY): Codon holds no class as a value, and cannot type dict[str, type]. Declare it dict[str, Any] and assign it in the else branch of if TYPE_CHECKING:; only the uncalled parser reads it. - An enum member looked up by name, or an enum iterated over (ComparisonRule[name], list(ComparisonRule)): write it as in Python. The check rewrites both for an enum of the package being checked and for the framework's own enums (Iterating an enum), so sweeper.constraints has no spelled-out member lists left. - An exception class raised with no arguments (raise _Exhausted() in route.search): Codon 0.19 raises no exception class without its own __init__, and its Exception takes a message where Python's takes none. The constructor calls super().__init__("") under if TYPE_CHECKING: and super().__init__() in the else branch. - An Optional chosen by a conditional expression, whose value goes to a union field (beside = graph.left(l) if left else graph.right(l), then BindingResult(value=beside.id), a float | int | list[int]): Codon 0.19 generated invalid LLVM IR and crashed without a diagnostic ("Call parameter type does not match function signature", optimize.cpp:1070). Choose with an if statement into a local annotated Optional[...]. - A function that returns a tuple with an Optional member, None in one return and a value in another (route.frame.ego_placement()): annotate the local in each return's own assignment (no_goal: Optional[tuple[int, float]] = None, goal_at: Optional[tuple[int, float]] = frame.locate(s)): one local annotated Optional where it is assigned None, and assigned the value later, was not enough. - A loop variable assigned a subclass's value is retyped: in a function that already declared other: ConstLanelet, other = near (a Lanelet) makes other a Lanelet, and a list of (float, ConstLanelet) then refuses it. Give the upcast a name of its own (nearby: ConstLanelet = near, route.geometry). - A value of a type the model holds: a checked module that hands a checked value to a checked module that imports it through the model (MODELLED_IMPORTS) hands the wrong type. scenario_runner hands the checked BaseScenario to measures.set_measured_scenario(), and its EgoConfig to EgoVehicle.spawn(), which take the model's: it makes those calls in the else branch of if TYPE_CHECKING:, and takes the spawned actor from ego.actor in the first. - No module object to assign a global through (vehicle_entity._warmup_done = True): Codon 0.19 imports no module as a value. The module sets its global in a function of its own (entity.vehicle_entity._set_warmup_done()). - The runner's boundary is modelled: coverage.codon declares the CoverageCollector (its constructor, start(), tick(), end(), write(path, scenario), and the run's case and outcome, record_case(case, space=None) and record_outcome(passed, *, failed_at=None, environment=None); openodd's backend and generator are refused), odd.codon resolve_odd(spec), whose union parameter (str, Path, OddDefinition or None) is generic and checked in its body, reset_probes(), the ODD's modules, the case a run records (OddCase, a @tuple of openodd's OddSample and ParameterSpace, which only the sampler builds) and what the runner reads of odd.route's verdict on the ego's planned route (plan_route_coverage(), RouteCoverage and RouteLanelet, which only it builds), and openodd's UNDECIDED, which the checked odd.probes returns: the one instance of a class openodd does not export (odd.model names it Undecided, for annotations), whose constructor is a compile error, as Python cannot build another, so the model allocates its one with Undecided.__new__(); environment.codon the id of the run's environment (capture() and RunEnvironment.id), and autoware_stack/launcher.codon the launcher's prepare() and close(), which the queue calls. test_typecheck_model.py compares each with the Python one. - No attribute of a union: Codon 0.19 reads pose.yaw of a value typed as a union (a vertex's position) as no type, even when every member has it with one type. After isinstance, name the value as the class (relative: RelativeLanePose = position) and read that; a union reaches a parameter typed with one of its members the same way. A generic function handed the union compiles every branch for it, so one that returns a different class per branch (route.positions.resolve_route_pose()) is called with each class on its own (trajectory.resolve._place_on_route()). - A callable of a union: Callable[[Union[A, B]], R] crashes Codon 0.19 ("union already sealed"), whether a parameter's, a variable's or a return's. Spell the callable out in the annotation (the checker drops a Callable parameter or return annotation, so the function is generic, and calls it with _acs_Returning[R, N]); a module-level alias (PositionResolver = Callable[...]) stays for Python and is None to the check, which refuses the alias as an expression ("expected type expression"). A function that takes either a resolver it is given or one it builds hands each to a helper of its own (trajectory.resolve._resolve_vertices()): one variable holds one type. - A closure calling another closure does not see that one's captures ("name 'x' is not defined"): make the inner one a module-level function taking what it read (trajectory.resolve._ego_route_s()). - A tuple display does not make a float the Optional[float] its annotation wants (return world.x, world.y, world.z, world.yaw from a function returning Tuple[float, float, Optional[float], Optional[float]]): a call does (trajectory.resolve._resolved()). - A singleton's __new__: Codon's constructor allocates and calls __init__, never a class's __new__, and its object.__new__ takes no class. The check rewrites super().__new__(cls) to C.__new__(), which allocates a C, and a class without __init__ is built by Codon from every attribute it declares: give it an __init__ that does nothing (MapManager; Python calls it after __new__). - Path.read_text() is in the pathlib shim (CPython 3.10's encoding and errors; 3.13's newline is refused); it reads an empty text.

docs.title: Usage Guide
docs.text: This guide explains how to use the autoware-carla-scenario package to run autonomous driving scenario tests in CARLA simulator.

docs.title: CLI Commands Overview
docs.text:
The package provides these CLI commands:

Command Framework Purpose scenario Hydra Run autonomous driving scenario tests in CARLA scenario-new argparse Scaffold a standalone scenario package scenario-check Hydra compose Compile scenarios with Codon without running them (the static check the runner makes before a run) scenario-slurm argparse Follow, collect, resubmit or cancel a batch run as SLURM array jobs (launcher=slurm) scenario-odd argparse Check an ODD and show its buckets; scenario-odd route checks scenarios' planned routes against it on the Lanelet2 map detect-no-3d-model argparse Detect lanelets without a matching 3D ground model in CARLA viewer FastAPI + Uvicorn Web UI for browsing and monitoring scenario test results scenario-editor FastAPI + Uvicorn Web UI for authoring scenarios and exporting reproducible packages

viewer and scenario-editor are separate applications on separate ports, and neither starts the other.

docs.title: scenario - Scenario Runner
docs.text: Runs autonomous driving scenario tests in CARLA. Uses Hydra for configuration management. Requires a running CARLA server.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
1. Parses the scenario=... argument (supports glob patterns for batch execution)
  2. Composes a Hydra config from map, server, ego, entity, and scenario configs
  3. Compiles the scenario with Codon and refuses it if it does not type-check (Static Check; typecheck=off skips it)
  4. Connects to the CARLA server and loads the specified map (OpenDRIVE or built-in)
  5. Spawns the ego vehicle at the configured Lanelet2 position (converted to CARLA coordinates)
  6. Enables synchronous mode (fixed 20 Hz tick rate) and starts the native CARLA recorder
  7. Runs a warm-up phase (5 ticks for physics stabilization)
  8. Enables autopilot and applies initial speeds
  9. Executes the main tick loop, checking pass/fail conditions each tick
  10. Writes the results as JSON, and the run's trajectory log as it goes
  11. Reloads the CARLA world for clean state between scenarios

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text:
# Run a single scenario
uv run scenario scenario=intersection_passing/straight

# Run a left-turn variant
uv run scenario scenario=intersection_passing/left_turn

# Run traffic light compliance scenario
uv run scenario scenario=traffic_light_compliance/traffic_light_compliance

# Run a lane change scenario
uv run scenario scenario=lane_change/left

# Run a temporary stop scenario
uv run scenario scenario=temporary_stop/temporary_stop

docs.title: Batch Execution with Glob Patterns
docs.text:
When the scenario= value contains glob metacharacters (*, ?, [), all matching scenario configs are executed sequentially in a single CARLA session:

# Run all intersection-passing variants
uv run scenario scenario='intersection_passing/*'

# Run all scenarios matching a partial pattern
uv run scenario scenario='intersection_passing/left_*'

# Run all lane-change scenarios
uv run scenario scenario='lane_change/*'

# Run everything
uv run scenario scenario='*/*'

# Run every lane-change scenario, however deep below lane_change/
uv run scenario scenario='lane_change/**'

The pattern is matched as scenario/{pattern}.yaml under each config directory: * stays within one path component, and a ** component crosses them. A trailing ** means everything below it and is read as **/*, so lane_change/** and ** select every config below lane_change/ and scenario/. A ** inside a component (lane_change/**left) is refused with an error naming the pattern. The pattern means the same on every supported Python version, and the viewer's Run form reads it the same way.

Batch constraints:

  • All scenarios in a batch must share the same map (CARLA loads one map per session)
  • Results are written to outputs/YYYY-MM-DD/HH-MM-SS/batch_results.json
  • A summary table is printed at the end with per-scenario pass/fail status
  • A case that cannot run at all -- its run raises on every attempt (server.cooldown_max_retries), e.g. a spawn point with no ground under it -- does not end the batch: it is reported as [ERROR] with the error, its batch_results.json entry is "passed": false with "error": true, and the batch goes on with the next case. Ctrl+C still stops the batch
  • A scenario with a sweep: section runs once, as configured; add --multirun to run every case of it (see Running every sweep case in a batch)

docs.title: Running every sweep case in a batch
docs.text:
With --multirun, a batch expands each scenario's sweep: -- lanelet constraints, a route search, the ODD sampler -- into its cases, the same ones scenario-expand prints, and runs them all in the one queue, against one CARLA session (and, with autoware.launcher, a fresh Autoware per case):

# Every lanelet case of both cut-in scenarios
uv run scenario --multirun 'scenario=cut_in/*' map=town10hd_opt

# 10 cases per scenario drawn from the ODD
uv run scenario --multirun 'scenario=cut_in/*' map=town10hd_opt \
  +sweep.odd_sample.count=10 +sweep.odd_sample.strategy=coverage

Scenarios that draw from one ODD go on from each other's draws rather than each draw the same cases: with strategy: coverage a later scenario aims at what the earlier ones left uncovered (see Sampling scenarios from the ODD).

A scenario with more than one case is listed as name#k in the summary, and batch_results.json gives each case its overrides. hydra/sweeper=... may be given but is not needed: the batch is the sweeper.

On a SLURM cluster, launcher=slurm runs a batch's cases as array jobs, several at once, each on a CARLA of its own, with the same outputs (off unless selected; see Running a Batch on SLURM):

uv run scenario --multirun 'scenario=cut_in/*' +sweep.odd_sample.count=24 \
  launcher=slurm launcher.array_parallelism=2

docs.title: Resetting the world between cases
docs.text:
Between two cases of a batch (and between two cases of a SLURM task) the world is reset, so that nothing of one case is in the next. server.world_reset says how:

server.world_reset What happens Cost per case (CARLA UE5, Town10HD_Opt) reload (default) The map is loaded again: a new episode ~5 s soft The map stays loaded; the world is put back as it was right after the load well under a second 
uv run scenario --multirun 'scenario=cut_in/*' map=town10hd_opt server.world_reset=soft
# Soft resets, with a full reload on every 10th reset anyway
uv run scenario --multirun 'scenario=cut_in/*' map=town10hd_opt \
  server.world_reset=soft server.reload_every=10

soft is opt-in: it is not yet shown that every case gives the same result after a soft reset as after a reload (#282). Compare a sweep run both ways before relying on it, and keep reload for results that have to be order-independent until that is shown for your scenarios.

What a soft reset does. Right after the map is loaded (at the start, and after every reload) the runner reads a baseline off the world: its actors, the episode settings, the weather, every traffic light's green, yellow and red times and whether it is frozen, and the spectator's transform. A soft reset then, in this order:

  1. stops the CARLA recorder (the run stops its own already; this catches one a failed run left going);
  2. destroys every actor the baseline does not list -- sensors and controllers first, then walkers, vehicles and anything else (props, an ego an external stack spawned) -- and ticks the world. Traffic lights, traffic signs and the spectator are the map's and are never destroyed;
  3. gives every traffic light its baseline timing back, resets all of them to the start of their cycle (World.reset_all_traffic_lights()) and freezes or unfreezes each as it was;
  4. puts the weather and the spectator back, and ticks the world;
  5. checks that no actor outside the baseline is left and that none of the map's is gone;
  6. applies the baseline episode settings (asynchronous, as a loaded world is; the next run makes it synchronous again).

What the run itself cleans up is cleaned up as before, whatever the reset: the ego, the conditions' sensors, the props, the T4 and Rerun sensors, the recorder, and the traffic backend (closed after every run, which is what resets the TrafficManager).

When it loads the map instead. The map is loaded, as with reload, when

  • there is no baseline (the map was not loaded by this runner yet, or reading the baseline failed);
  • the server runs another episode than the one the baseline was read in: another client loaded a world -- another map, or the same one -- on the server;
  • any step above raises, an actor survives its destroy, or an actor of the map is gone;
  • the world has a traffic light the baseline does not list (the server listed it only after the baseline was read): its timing and frozen state are not known, so whatever a case did to it could not be put back;
  • server.reload_every is N > 0 and N - 1 soft resets have been done since the last load (every N-th reset is a reload; 1 is the same as reload).

A reload reads a new baseline, so the resets after it are soft again.

What a soft reset cannot guarantee. These differ from a reload, and a scenario whose result depends on them can give a different result after a soft reset:

  • The episode goes on. The frame number and the episode's elapsed time keep counting, and actor ids keep growing (a fresh episode starts both again). The runner measures a case on its own clock from its first tick, so its conditions and timeouts do not see this, but anything that reads raw frame numbers, elapsed_seconds or actor ids does.
  • Traffic light phase. The lights are reset to the start of their cycle, which is where a load leaves them too, but how far into it they are on the case's first tick may differ by the ticks the reset itself takes.
  • Vehicle and physics state. The previous case's vehicles are destroyed and new ones spawned, but state the server keeps outside an actor (physics scene, pooled resources) is not reset. In the trials behind #282 an ego's gear differed on every tick from a fresh-world run of the same case.
  • What has no getter in the CARLA API. Map layers unloaded with World.unload_map_layer(), environment objects toggled with enable_environment_objects(), street lights switched through the LightManager, the pedestrians' cross factor and seed, and debug drawings still within their life_time. The framework changes none of these but the pedestrians' cross factor, which it puts back itself after starting each walker; a scenario that changes the others needs reload.
  • The TrafficManager. It lives outside the episode, so a reload does not reset it either: the traffic backend's close() after each run is what does.

server.world_reset applies to the cases one batch runs in one queue (--multirun with a glob or a sweep:, and the cases of one SLURM task). A Hydra sweeper such as hydra/sweeper=lanelet_constraint runs each case as a job of its own, which loads the map when it starts, so there is nothing to reset between its cases.

docs.title: Selecting a Published HD Map
docs.text:
A map group can name a git repository instead of local files, and the map is fetched into ~/autoware_data/maps on first use -- the same directory Autoware's own setup downloads maps into, so a machine that has run it clones nothing:

# Town10HD_Opt, as published for CARLA 0.10, pinned to a commit. The built-in
# scenario configs name Nishishinjuku lanelets, so place the ego on Town10's.
uv run scenario scenario=lane_change/left map=town10hd_opt \
  ego.spawn_lanelet_id=324 ego.spawn_s=10.0 ego.goal_lanelet_id=5650

# Any repository, any revision
uv run scenario map=town10hd_opt \
  map.source='git+https://huggingface.co/datasets/OWNER/NAME@REF#maps/T'

# A map directory on this machine, read in place
uv run scenario map=town10hd_opt map.directory=/path/to/autoware_maps/Town10HD_Opt

See HD Maps from a Git Repository.

docs.title: Lanelet Constraint Sweeping
docs.text:
The package ships a Hydra Sweeper plugin (hydra/sweeper=lanelet_constraint) that expands a single scenario config into one job per lanelet that matches a set of constraints, optionally deriving per-job parameters via "bindings". Each scenario YAML may declare its own sweep: section (see traffic_light_compliance.yaml for an example).

sweep.constraints sweeps one parameter: it holds a single target key (such as ego.spawn_lanelet_id) with its list of constraints, and every other parameter a case needs is derived from the matched lanelet by sweep.bindings. A sweep.constraints with a second key is refused with an error when the sweep is expanded, rather than searched together with the first.

# Run a Hydra multirun over every lanelet whose `ego.spawn_lanelet_id`
# satisfies the scenario's `sweep.constraints`.
uv run scenario --multirun scenario=traffic_light_compliance/traffic_light_compliance \
  hydra/sweeper=lanelet_constraint

# Resume a sweep from job number N (1-indexed; 0 disables).
uv run scenario --multirun scenario=traffic_light_compliance/traffic_light_compliance \
  hydra/sweeper=lanelet_constraint sweep.resume_from=10

Sweeps write results under multirun/YYYY-MM-DD/HH-MM-SS/<job-index>/, not outputs/. The result viewer scans both directories.

A failed, crashed or timed-out case does not stop the sweep: every case runs, the sweeper logs Sweep complete: P/N succeeded, F failed (T timed out)., and the process then exits 1 when any case failed (see Exit Codes).

The sweeper runs each case in a forked process of its own. With server.cooldown_max_retries it runs a case again only when it could not run: its run raised (CARLA went away, a spawn failed), timed out (sweep.job_timeout_seconds) or crashed. A case whose scenario ran to a FAILED verdict is final and is not retried, as in a batch. The sweeper owns these retries: the case's own queue does not retry it as well, so a case runs at most 1 + server.cooldown_max_retries times, as in a batch.

A case that timed out or crashed had no chance to stop the CARLA server it launched; that server's watchdog stops it within about a second, giving it 10 s before SIGKILL. So before the next attempt -- a retry or the next case -- the sweeper waits until the CARLA processes the case launched have exited (at most 15 s, then it kills them), on top of server.cooldown_seconds: the next case must neither reuse the dying server nor start one while it still holds the port, even if the case was killed while its server was still loading. A case that ended normally stopped its server itself, so nothing is waited for; nor is a server the case did not launch (one you started yourself, which it reused), which no case stops.

A sweep with no case to run exits 1 before anything runs, as a batch with no case left does: its constraints, route or ODD sample match nothing on the map (the sweep expands to no case), or --resume-from / sweep.resume_from is past its last case.

Ctrl-C or SIGTERM stops the sweep and the case it is running. The case is sent SIGTERM, so it stops its CARLA server and Autoware stack as on Ctrl-C, and SIGKILL if it is still running 30 s later (a second Ctrl-C does not wait). The sweep then exits 130 (Ctrl-C) or 143 (SIGTERM) and names the case to resume from.

To get the concrete scenarios without running them (for example, to fan them out over a cluster), use scenario-expand. It takes the same arguments as scenario and prints JSON with one list of Hydra overrides per concrete scenario. These are the same cases, in the same order, that the sweeper runs:

uv run scenario-expand scenario=traffic_light_compliance/traffic_light_compliance
# {"scenario": "...", "cases": [["ego.spawn_lanelet_id=5", "ego.spawn_s=18.62..."], ...]}

A scenario without a sweep: section is already concrete, so it expands to a single empty case. Only the Lanelet2 map is needed, not a CARLA server.

A logical scenario -- a document with a route search, whose sweep: holds route: instead of constraints: -- expands to one case per route of the map that matches its pattern, each with the ego's spawn and goal and the match itself (scenario.route.*); see Logical Scenarios from Routes.

docs.title: Resume from a Specific Scenario
docs.text:
When running large batches, you can skip already-completed scenarios. --resume-from N starts at the Nth scenario (1-indexed, as for a sweep); in a --multirun batch it counts the expanded cases:

# Resume from the 3rd scenario
uv run scenario scenario='intersection_passing/*' --resume-from 3

docs.title: Overriding Configuration Parameters
docs.text:
Any nested Hydra parameter can be overridden from the command line:

# Select a different map
uv run scenario scenario=intersection_passing/straight map=nishishinjuku

# Connect to a remote CARLA server
uv run scenario scenario=intersection_passing/straight server.host=192.168.1.100 server.port=3000

# Change ego vehicle type and speed
uv run scenario scenario=intersection_passing/straight \
  ego.vehicle_type=vehicle.tesla.model3 \
  ego.initial_speed_kmh=30.0

# Override scenario-specific parameters
uv run scenario scenario=intersection_passing/straight scenario.timeout_seconds=15.0

# Change Traffic Manager port
uv run scenario scenario=intersection_passing/straight traffic_manager.port=8200

docs.title: One Seed for the Whole Run
docs.text:
seed (top level, 0 by default) is the one number every random draw of a run follows, so the same seed runs the same scenario again:

uv run scenario scenario=intersection_passing/straight seed=42

It is the seed of:

What draws Its own seed, which wins when set The cases a sweep draws from the ODD (sweep.odd_sample), and the grip and visibility drawn for each sweep.odd_sample.seed The scenario: BaseScenario.random_seed -- The traffic backend: CARLA's TrafficManager (set_random_device_seed, each vehicle's parameter draws), SUMO (--seed, netconvert --seed, its own draws) -- (the scenario's) CARLA's pedestrian navigation (World.set_pedestrians_seed) -- (the scenario's) Background traffic background_traffic.seed The adversarial actions, AdversarialTrafficAction, AdversityFeasibleCondition, TrafficSourceAction their seed argument (Seed in the editor) The driver policy's session (DriveSessionRequest.random_seed) driver.random_seed A LiDAR's weather noise driver.lidars[].noise_seed

Every one of those seeds is null (None in Python) by default, and a null seed is the run's. In Python the run's seed lives in autoware_carla_scenario.seed: the runner sets it from the scenario's random_seed before setup() (and scenario sets it from the config before it builds the scenario), and a component built with seed=None takes it when it is built. A scenario that draws for itself seeds its own generator from self.random_seed.

A route search's seed (sweep.route.seed) is not one of them: unset, the matches are not shuffled at all. A config with no seed key (a scenario package's own config.yaml written before it existed) leaves the scenario the random_seed it was built with.

docs.title: Hydra Configuration System
docs.text:
Configuration files are located in src/autoware_carla_scenario/examples/conf/:

conf/
├── config.yaml              # Root config (defines defaults and top-level overrides)
├── server/
│   └── localhost.yaml       # Server connection settings
├── ego/
│   └── default.yaml         # Ego vehicle settings
├── entity/
│   └── default.yaml         # Entity spawn and ground projection settings
├── traffic_manager/
│   └── default.yaml         # CARLA Traffic Manager settings
├── map/
│   └── nishishinjuku.yaml   # Map file paths and excluded lanelet IDs
└── scenario/
    ├── intersection_passing/
    │   ├── straight.yaml
    │   ├── left_turn.yaml
    │   ├── right_turn.yaml
    │   └── straight_3npc.yaml
    ├── lane_change/
    │   ├── left.yaml
    │   └── right.yaml
    ├── lane_change_fail/
    │   ├── left.yaml
    │   └── right.yaml
    ├── temporary_stop/
    │   └── temporary_stop.yaml
    └── traffic_light_compliance/
        └── traffic_light_compliance.yaml

docs.title: Root Configuration (config.yaml)
docs.text:
Defines the default config group composition:

Default Group Default Value Description server localhost CARLA server connection ego default Ego vehicle configuration entity default Entity spawn and ground projection traffic_manager default CARLA Traffic Manager scenario intersection_passing/left_turn Scenario to run map nishishinjuku Map to load

docs.title: Server Configuration
docs.text: Parameter Type Default Description server.host str localhost CARLA server hostname server.port int 2000 CARLA server port server.cooldown_seconds float 2.0 Wait time between consecutive scenario runs server.cooldown_max_retries int 0 Maximum retries of a run that raised (not of one that ran and failed) server.world_reset str reload How the world is reset between a batch's cases: reload or soft (see Resetting the world between cases) server.reload_every int 0 With world_reset: soft, load the map on every N-th reset anyway; 0: only when a soft reset cannot be done

docs.title: Ego Vehicle Configuration
docs.text: Parameter Type Default Description ego.vehicle_type str vehicle.mini.cooper CARLA blueprint ID for ego vehicle ego.initial_speed_kmh float 0.0 Initial speed of ego vehicle (km/h) ego.spawn_lanelet_id int 242 Lanelet ID for spawn position ego.spawn_s float 25.0 Longitudinal offset along lanelet centerline (meters) ego.spawn_t float 0.0 Lateral offset from the lanelet centerline, positive to its left (meters) ego.spawn_heading float 0.0 Yaw relative to the lanelet's direction of travel, positive anticlockwise (radians)

docs.title: Entity Configuration
docs.text:
Controls ground projection (ray casting) and spawn retry behavior:

Parameter Type Default Description entity.ground_projection_ray_distance_upper float 5.0 Ray search range above estimated z (meters) entity.ground_projection_ray_distance_lower float 10.0 Ray search range below estimated z (meters) entity.spawn_retry_max_count int 10 Maximum retry attempts for spawn entity.spawn_retry_t_step float 0.1 Lateral offset shift per retry (meters) entity.spawn_retry_z_step float 0.5 Vertical shift per retry (meters)

docs.title: Traffic Manager Configuration
docs.text: Parameter Type Default Description traffic_manager.port int 8100 CARLA Traffic Manager RPC port

docs.title: Seeing a run
docs.text:
A run renders no video (since 15.0.0). What it leaves to look at is its trajectory log, {ScenarioName}.trajectory.jsonl: every vehicle and pedestrian tick by tick, the traffic lights, the map it ran on, the ego's plan (its debug markers), each condition's state and the verdict (Trajectory Log). To see it, make it a Rerun recording, {ScenarioName}.rrd beside the log, and open that in the Rerun viewer. The conversion is the autoware-carla-scenario-rerun package, installed with the rerun extra:

# The converter (rerun), and the Rerun viewer its recordings are made for (viewer):
pip install 'autoware-carla-scenario[rerun,viewer]'
# A recording of every run, made as each run ends:
uv run scenario scenario=cut_in/cut_in rerun.enabled=true
uv run scenario 'scenario=cut_in/*' --multirun rerun.enabled=true
rerun outputs/2026-10-18/08-48-12/CutInScenario-3.rrd     # the Rerun viewer
Parameter Type Default Description rerun.enabled bool false Convert each run's trajectory log into {ScenarioName}.rrd as soon as the run ends rerun.strict bool false Fail the conversion of a log with a record type or a field the converter does not know, rather than skip it with a warning rerun.lidar bool false Put the LiDAR sweeps the ego's driver policy gets into the recording too (Sensors) rerun.lidar_max_points int 65536 At most this many points of a sweep (an even subsample); 0 keeps them all rerun.cameras bool false Put the camera frames the ego's driver policy gets into the recording too (Sensors)

With rerun.enabled=true:

  • A run asking for recordings without the extra installed is refused before anything starts (exit code 2), saying how to install it.
  • Each log is converted on a background thread as soon as its run ends, while the next case runs (the converter releases the GIL; a log takes milliseconds). A run that raised is converted too: its log is what shows what happened.
  • At the end the run waits for the last conversions and prints how they went: Rerun recordings: N/M written, and a line per failure naming its case. A failed conversion does not change any verdict or the exit code.
  • Each case's {ScenarioName}_result.json names its recording (rerun_recording), and so does its entry in a batch's batch_results.json, with rerun_error when the conversion failed. The viewer's scenario page shows it in the embedded Rerun viewer, without converting the log again (Seeing a run in the viewer).
