  • A Hydra sweep (--multirun without a glob) runs each case in a process of its own, and each converts its own log. So does each task of a batch run on SLURM (launcher=slurm, Running a Batch on SLURM): it converts its own cases, and scenario-slurm collect reports their recordings as a local batch does.

docs.title: A T4 dataset of a run
docs.text: With t4.enabled=true each run is also written as a T4 dataset, {ScenarioName}.t4/, which t4-devkit reads: the sweeps and frames of the driver policy's sensors (driver.lidars, driver.cameras) at each policy step, and the box of every vehicle and pedestrian from CARLA's ground truth (the t4 extra; T4 Dataset).

docs.title: A T4Scene of a run
docs.text: With t4scene.enabled=true each run's trajectory log is also written as a T4Scene, {ScenarioName}.t4scene.pb with its map, {ScenarioName}.t4scene.map.pb, the scene tier4/e2e-devkit decodes, scores and draws (T4 Scene); scenario-t4scene <output dir> does the same after a run.

docs.title: Sensors in the recording
docs.text:
The trajectory log holds no sensor data. With rerun.enabled=true and:

  • rerun.lidar=true, the sweeps each driver LiDAR sends the ego's policy (driver.lidars) are recorded as world/lidar/<logical id>: points in the recording's world frame, coloured by height above the ego, drawn where the ego's pose put them when the policy got them;
  • rerun.cameras=true, the frames each driver camera sends it (driver.cameras) are recorded as world/ego/pose/cameras/<logical id>: the camera's mount on the ego and a pinhole of its field of view, so the 3D view draws its frustum with the frame in it, and the JPEG frames the policy got (a 2D view of the entity shows them).

They are written during the run into {ScenarioName}.sensors.rrd; once the log is converted they are merged into {ScenarioName}.rrd (rerun rrd merge) and that file is removed. It needs the Rerun SDK of the converter's version:

pip install 'autoware-carla-scenario[rerun-lidar]'
uv run scenario scenario=cut_in/cut_in driver=... rerun.enabled=true \
    rerun.lidar=true rerun.cameras=true

Points are most of a recording: about 0.8 MB a sweep at the default 65,536; a camera frame is its JPEG (driver.image_quality). A merge that fails keeps {ScenarioName}.sensors.rrd beside the recording (logged; not a failed conversion); converting the run again (below) merges it. The two cannot be opened together instead: the viewer registers a file by its recording id, and the second replaces the first.

A run made without it (or by a version before it) can be converted afterwards, the same way:

# Every run of a session (a sweep's directory works the same), or one log:
python -m autoware_carla_scenario.rerun outputs/2026-10-18/08-48-12
python -m autoware_carla_scenario.rerun outputs/2026-10-18/08-48-12/CutInScenario-3.trajectory.jsonl

or from Python, autoware_carla_scenario.rerun.convert_outputs(path). It also converts a run again (with --strict, or a newer converter), and keeps the sensors the run recorded:

  • a {ScenarioName}.sensors.rrd left beside the log (a merge that failed) is merged into the new recording and removed, as during a run;
  • the sensors in a {ScenarioName}.rrd it replaces (world/lidar/**, world/ego/pose/cameras/**) are carried over into the new one. That needs the Rerun SDK's CLI (rerun-lidar extra); without it, or if it fails, the old recording is left as it was and reported as [SKIPPED] (exit status 1). --overwrite (overwrite=True) replaces it anyway, without its sensors.

A log that fails to convert leaves the recording it would have replaced as it was. The converter reads nothing but the log and the map files the log names, so it runs anywhere, without CARLA. The CARLA recording ({ScenarioName}.log) is still written: CARLA's own replayer (client.replay_file()) plays it back on a server running the same map.

video.* settings (video.enabled, video.width, video.height) are accepted for old command lines and configs, and do nothing: a run that sets one warns that it is ignored and says the above.

docs.title: Map Configuration
docs.text:
Parameter Type Default Description map.name str required CARLA map name (e.g., NishishinjukuMap) map.source str | null null Git repository holding the HD map (see maps.md) map.directory str | null null Local map directory, read in place. Wins over map.source map.xodr_path str | null null Path to custom OpenDRIVE file. If null, loads built-in CARLA map by name map.lanelet2_path str | null null Path to Lanelet2 .osm file (required for lanelet-based spawn) map.no_3d_model_lanelet_ids list[int] [] Lanelet IDs to exclude from sweeps (no ground geometry)

Map paths can use environment variables with Hydra's OmegaConf resolver:

xodr_path: ${oc.env:NISHISHINJUKU_XODR_PATH,path/to/default.xodr}

docs.title: Intersection Passing
docs.text:
Tests ego vehicle traversal through an intersection. Verifies that the ego passes through the expected OpenDRIVE road sequence.

Config Turn Direction Description intersection_passing/straight none Drive straight through intersection intersection_passing/left_turn left Left turn at intersection intersection_passing/right_turn right Right turn at intersection intersection_passing/straight_3npc none Straight with 3 NPC vehicles

Scenario-specific parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description scenario.expected_route_lanelet_ids list[int] varies Lanelet IDs the ego must traverse; a junction's lanelets are judged by the roads before and after it scenario.timeout_seconds float 5.0 Maximum scenario duration scenario.min_speed_kmh float | null null Minimum ego speed (fail if below). null disables check scenario.speed_check_delay_seconds float 0.3 Grace period before speed check starts scenario.turn_direction str | null null "left", "right", or null for straight scenario.turn_indicator_before_m float | null null From this many metres before the junction (the stop line at the start of the route's first lanelet) until it is on that lanelet, the ego must show the indicator of turn_direction (left or right); it fails once it has not for turn_indicator_grace_seconds. null disables the check scenario.turn_indicator_grace_seconds float 0.5 How long the indicator may be wrong before the run fails scenario.max_steering_reversals int | null null Fail once the steering has turned back this many times since the start (the steering_reversals metric, metrics.md). null disables the check scenario.max_turn_indicator_changes int | null null Fail once the turn indicators have changed this many times since the start, counted apart from the steering (the turn_indicator_changes metric). null disables the check scenario.npc_vehicles list [] NPC vehicle configurations (see below)

NPC vehicle configuration:

npc_vehicles:
  - spawn_lanelet_id: 100
    spawn_s: 5.0
    vehicle_type: vehicle.mini.cooper
    initial_speed_kmh: 10.0

Behavior: - Sets all traffic lights to GREEN - Registers a TurnAction for left/right turns (applies steering via CARLA autopilot route) - Pass condition: ego traverses all expected OpenDRIVE road IDs (checked via StickyCondition + AndCondition) - Fail conditions: timeout, ego destroyed, speed below threshold

docs.title: Lane Change
docs.text:
Tests ego vehicle lane change maneuvers. Can test both successful lane changes and expected failures.

Config Direction Expected Result lane_change/left left success lane_change/right right success lane_change_fail/left left fail (no adjacent lane) lane_change_fail/right right fail (no adjacent lane)

Scenario-specific parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description scenario.direction str "left" Lane change direction: "left" or "right" scenario.expect str "success" Expected outcome: "success" or "fail" scenario.timeout_seconds float 10.0 Maximum scenario duration

Behavior: - Sets all traffic lights to GREEN - Immediately registers a LaneChangeAction - Derives the target lane from the current spawn position and direction - Pass condition: expect=success requires both road_id and lane_id to change; expect=fail passes when timeout is reached without a lane change - Checks via EntityLanePositionCondition

docs.title: Traffic Light Compliance
docs.text:
Tests that the ego vehicle correctly stops at a red light and proceeds after green.

Config traffic_light_compliance/traffic_light_compliance

Scenario-specific parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description scenario.light_switch_delay_seconds float 5.0 Delay before switching red to green scenario.timeout_seconds float 8.0 Maximum scenario duration scenario.stop_zone_min_m float 0.0 Near end of the stop zone: metres before the stop line (stop_line_distance_m) scenario.stop_zone_max_m float 3.0 Far end of the stop zone; standing still farther back until the green fails the run scenario.stop_line_tolerance_m float 0.0 How far the front bumper may pass the stop line on red before the run fails for running the red; that far past counts as at the line for the stop zone scenario.standstill_seconds float 0.5 How long the ego has to stand still in the stop zone, before the green, for it to count as stopped there (latched once it has) scenario.standstill_speed_mps float 0.1 Speed (m/s) at or below which the ego stands still scenario.departure_speed_kmh float 10.0 Speed (km/h) the ego must reach after green to pass; null uses moving_speed_kmh scenario.moving_speed_kmh float 1.0 The departure speed when departure_speed_kmh is null; no longer judges the red phase scenario.merging_time_seconds float 0.5 Deprecated and unused; kept so configs that set it still load

Behavior: - Sets all traffic lights to RED initially - Registers a TrafficSignalAction to switch to GREEN after light_switch_delay_seconds - Fails as soon as the ego's front bumper crosses the stop line while the light is red - At the green, fails unless the ego has stood still with its front bumper in the stop zone (stop_zone_min_m-stop_zone_max_m before the stop line), saying whether it stopped short of the zone, stopped in it too late, or had not stopped - Pass conditions: ego stood still in the stop zone before the green AND reaches departure_speed_kmh during green

docs.title: Temporary Stop
docs.text:
Tests that the ego vehicle stops at a designated stop line for a minimum duration, then restarts.

Config temporary_stop/temporary_stop

Scenario-specific parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description scenario.s_margin float 5.0 Arc-length margin around stop position (meters) scenario.speed_threshold float 0.1 Max speed considered as "stopped" (m/s) scenario.stop_duration float 0.3 Minimum consecutive seconds to remain stopped scenario.restart_speed_kmh float 3.0 Speed threshold for restart detection (km/h) scenario.timeout_seconds float 5.0 Maximum scenario duration

Behavior: - Sets all traffic lights to GREEN - Registers a TemporaryStopCondition at the configured stop position - Pass condition: ego stays within s_margin of stop line at speed below speed_threshold for at least stop_duration seconds, then accelerates above restart_speed_kmh

docs.title: Scenario Evaluation
docs.text:
Each scenario registers pass conditions and fail conditions. The tick loop evaluates them every frame:

  • First pass condition satisfied → scenario passes
  • First fail condition triggered → scenario fails
  • Common fail conditions: TimeoutCondition (exceeded time limit), EntityExistenceCondition (ego destroyed)

docs.title: ODD and Coverage
docs.text:
Every run is measured against an ODD, named by the odd key (default unless overridden). Its attributes are sampled on every tick and written, with the scenario's own cover items, to {ScenarioName}_coverage.json. scenario-coverage outputs/ merges those files into a report. See ODD and Coverage.

uv run scenario scenario=intersection_passing/left_turn odd=path/to/urban.yaml
uv run scenario-coverage outputs/ --markdown coverage.md

Before running, scenario-odd route plans each scenario's ego route on the Lanelet2 map (no CARLA server) and reports which parts of it are outside the ODD, which are undecided until run time, the metres it is expected to cover in each bucket, and the buckets no route reaches (Checking a planned route):

uv run scenario-odd route path/to/urban.yaml 'intersection_passing/*' lane_change/left

docs.title: Output Files
docs.text:
Each scenario run generates output in outputs/YYYY-MM-DD/HH-MM-SS/:

File Description {ScenarioName}.log CARLA native recording (replay format) {ScenarioName}_result.json Machine-readable result with condition statuses {ScenarioName}_coverage.json ODD and scenario coverage hits of the run (merge with scenario-coverage, see Coverage) {ScenarioName}_odd.tar.gz The run's ODD as the files it was read from (an ODD read from OpenODD YAML; openodd's transmission archive, named by its revision; see Versions of an ODD) {ScenarioName}_requirements.lock What the run ran with: every installed distribution pinned, in the requirements format (pip install -r), headed by the framework, the scenario's package, Python and the platform. A distribution from git is pinned to its commit; an editable one (a checkout) names its directory, commit and whether it had uncommitted changes {ScenarioName}_environment.json The same, structured; _result.json carries its summary (environment: the framework, the scenario's package, key dependencies, and the lock's id -- the SHA-256 of what it pins -- so runs on one environment can be found by it) {ScenarioName}.trajectory.jsonl The run, tick by tick, and the map, plan, conditions and verdict (Trajectory Log); make it a Rerun recording to see the run (Seeing a run), or a T4Scene for tier4/e2e-devkit with scenario-t4scene (T4 Scene) {ScenarioName}.rrd The Rerun recording of the trajectory log, with rerun.enabled=true (Seeing a run) {ScenarioName}.t4scene.pb, {ScenarioName}.t4scene.map.pb The trajectory log as a T4Scene and the map it names, with t4scene.enabled=true (T4 Scene) batch_results.json Batch summary (glob/batch mode only)

Result JSON format:

On a pass, message is the message of the pass condition that fired -- here an AndCondition of two StickyConditions, which joins its children's messages with AND -- or Scenario completed successfully when is_done() ended the run. When a fail condition ends the run, it is that condition's message.

{
  "scenario": "intersection_passing/straight",
  "passed": true,
  "message": "Entity 'ego' is on road '5' (any lane) (s=12.40, t=-1.75) at 1.10s AND Entity 'ego' is on road '12' (any lane) (s=3.05, t=-1.80) at 3.42s",
  "elapsed_seconds": 3.42,
  "condition_statuses": [
    {"label": "Road 5 visited", "satisfied": true, "message": "..."},
    {"label": "Road 12 visited", "satisfied": true, "message": "..."}
  ]
}

Why a run failed:

A failed run's result has a failure: the fail condition that ended it, and a category that names what went wrong the same way in every scenario, where the condition's label is the scenario author's. A batch, a sweep or two versions of a driver can then be compared by what went wrong (batch_results.json carries it for every case, and the summary prints it).

"failure": {
  "condition": "fail[1](scenario_timeout)",
  "category": "progress",
  "at": 25.0,
  "message": "Timeout after 25.00s (limit: 25.0s)",
  "detail": "stalled",
  "also_triggered": []
}
Category What went wrong collision The ego hit something traffic_rule It broke a traffic rule: ran a red light, drove against the traffic signalling It did not signal what it did (no turn indicator) lane_keeping It left its lane or the road stability It did not drive steadily: sawed at the steering, weaved, flicked its indicators safety_margin It came too close: time to collision, headway, distance progress It did not get where the scenario asked in time driver The driver ended the run itself infrastructure The run could not go on: the ego vanished, or the run raised other None of these, or a condition that does not say

A scenario gives a fail condition its category when it registers it:

from autoware_carla_scenario.failure import FailureCategory

self.register_fail_condition(
    PersistentCondition(AndCondition([...]), 0.5, label="no_left_indicator"),
    category=FailureCategory.SIGNALLING,
)

Without one, the condition says (BaseCondition.failure_category()): a collision condition is collision, a timeout progress, a time-to-collision or headway condition safety_margin, the ego's existence infrastructure, and a MetricCondition what its metric reads (the collision metrics collision, offroad lane_keeping, wrong_lane traffic_rule, the weaving ones stability). A sticky or persistent condition says what it wraps. A combination of conditions (AND, OR, NOT) says nothing, and the run's failure is other: give it a category.

detail tells a progress failure apart by how the ego ended the run: never_moved (it never drove 1 m), stalled (it had stood still for 3 s or more: waiting for something that never cleared) or moving (it was driving, but not where the scenario's pass condition asked). The other fail conditions that held when the run ended are in also_triggered. The driver ending the run is driver, and a case that raised on every attempt is infrastructure.

docs.title: Exit Codes
docs.text:
Code Meaning 0 All scenarios passed 1 One or more scenarios failed or errored, or configuration/runtime error 2 Refused before anything ran: the scenario does not type-check, or an extra it asks for (rerun, t4) is not installed 130, 143 Stopped by Ctrl-C (130) or SIGTERM (143), after the run stopped what it started (its CARLA server, its Autoware stack); a sweep first stops the case it is running

The same codes hold however the cases run: a single run, a glob batch, a --multirun (each case of the scenario's sweep in one batch, hydra/sweeper=lanelet_constraint, or Hydra's own sweeper over comma-separated values) and launcher=slurm, which waits for the array and collects it. A sweep runs every case before it exits, so 1 means at least one case failed; the summary names how many. A refusal ends a sweep at once with 2, since every case after it would be refused too. A run with no case to run (nothing expanded, or --resume-from past the last case) exits 1: exit 0 always means something ran and passed. The exceptions:

  • Under Hydra's own sweeper (scenario --multirun key=a,b, no hydra/sweeper=), a case that raises an exception ends the sweep at once with 1, as Hydra does; a case that runs and fails does not.
  • launcher=slurm with --no-wait exits 0 once the batch is submitted; its verdict is what scenario-slurm wait or scenario-slurm collect exit with. Interrupted while it waits, it cancels the array and exits with the verdict of what it collects (slurm.cancel_on_interrupt, the default), or exits 130 and leaves the array running.

docs.title: Driving the Ego with an External Policy
docs.text:
By default CARLA's TrafficManager drives the ego. To hand it to an external driving policy over the egodriver gRPC contract instead, start the policy server and select the carla_driver entity:

# 1. Start the policy (in its own environment)
uv run carla-driver-interface serve --policy route_follower --port 50051

# 2. Run any scenario against it
uv run scenario ego.entity=carla_driver driver.address=localhost:50051

ego.entity accepts:

Value Behaviour autopilot (default) CARLA's TrafficManager drives the ego autoware Autoware drives the ego, over the AutowareBridge; with autoware.launcher the framework starts a fresh Autoware per scenario (Autoware as the Ego) carla_driver An external policy drives the ego ros2 ROS 2 nodes drive the ego over DDS, with no bridge node (ROS 2 over DDS) hils ECUs under test drive the ego, through the resident HILS bridge scenario-hils (hils.host, hils.port; HILS Bridge)

Common overrides:

# Query the policy every simulation tick instead of every other one
uv run scenario ego.entity=carla_driver driver.policy_timestep_s=0.05

# Pin the rig origin offset when the derived value looks wrong (CARLA 0.9.x)
uv run scenario ego.entity=carla_driver driver.rear_axle_offset_m=-1.4

# Send a smaller, cheaper camera frame
uv run scenario ego.entity=carla_driver \
    driver.cameras.0.image_width=480 driver.cameras.0.image_height=302

See External Driver Interface for the full reference.

docs.title: Rendering sensors with carla_canvas
docs.text:
carla_canvas renders cameras and LiDARs behind the CARLA API instead of the CARLA server: a configuration file names a renderer service (3D Gaussian splatting, a LiDAR world model such as LidarVerse, ...) and the sensor types it renders, and typesafe_carla's sensor plugin hands those sensors' measurements over from the service. canvas.config points a run at such a file; nothing else about the run changes -- the scenario, the driver and the measurements they read are the same:

pip install 'carla-canvas[client]>=0.2'
uv run scenario scenario=cut_in/cut_in ego.entity=carla_driver \
    canvas.config=path/to/lidarverse.yaml
Parameter Type Default Description canvas.config str null A carla_canvas configuration: its sensors are rendered by its renderer; null leaves every sensor to CARLA

The run sets CARLA_CANVAS_CONFIG and TYPESAFE_CARLA_SENSOR_PLUGIN before any sensor listens, which is when typesafe_carla loads the plugin, once for the process: the cases of a batch name one file (a batch naming two is refused). The renderer is the configuration's: started by the plugin when nothing answers at renderer.endpoint and the file gives a renderer.command, or run by hand (carla-canvas serve --config ...). carla_canvas is not an extra of this package: it needs protobuf 7, and the vendored alpasim modules are regenerated on protobuf 4. Under SLURM the file is the nodes' path.

docs.title: scenario-hils - Streaming the Ego to ECUs (HILS)
docs.text:
A resident process on the HILS PC that follows a run's ego in CARLA, sends ECUs under test their sensors' and buses' traffic (CAN, GNSS, LiDAR packets, camera frames) through hilspy, initializes and finalizes them around each scenario, and hands their commands back to a run with ego.entity=hils; configured by one YAML file:

uvx --from 'autoware-carla-scenario[hils]' scenario-hils --example > hils.yaml
uvx --from 'autoware-carla-scenario[hils]' scenario-hils hils.yaml

See HILS Bridge.

docs.title: detect-no-3d-model - 3D Model Detection
docs.text: Detects lanelets that do not have a matching 3D ground model in CARLA. Useful for identifying areas where vehicle ground-projection ray casting will fail. Requires a running CARLA server with the target map loaded.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
1. Reads the map configuration YAML and resolves its map files the way uv run scenario does (see Input YAML Requirements)
  2. Connects to the CARLA server and loads the map -- installing the OpenDRIVE first when map.overwrite_xodr is set, by name otherwise -- and, for a map that carries no OpenDRIVE, reads it back out of the loaded world into the map cache, as a run does
  3. For each lanelet's center point, casts a vertical ray (upward and downward from estimated z) to detect ground geometry
  4. Reports lanelets where the ray does not hit any 3D surface
  5. Writes the detected IDs to the YAML configuration's no_3d_model_lanelet_ids field

The IDs go into no_3d_model_lanelet_ids in the YAML's map: section when it has one, and at the top level otherwise (the same place the map settings are read from). An existing value is replaced whatever its style (a block list, a flow list such as [1, 2], an empty value, null); a missing key is added after the section's last entry. The file is edited as text, so comments, ${...} interpolations and line endings are kept, and it is replaced atomically (a symlinked YAML is written through to its target). The edited text is parsed again first: if anything other than that one value would change -- or the section cannot be edited as text, e.g. map: {name: X} -- the tool exits with an error, prints the detected IDs, and leaves the file as it was.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Run it from the repository root: the example map configs live under autoware_carla_scenario/src/autoware_carla_scenario/examples/conf/map/, and nishishinjuku.yaml names its files relative to the root (data/nishishinjuku.osm).

CONF=autoware_carla_scenario/src/autoware_carla_scenario/examples/conf/map

# Basic detection using map config YAML
uv run detect-no-3d-model $CONF/nishishinjuku.yaml

# A map named only by map.source (its OpenDRIVE is read back from CARLA)
uv run detect-no-3d-model $CONF/town10hd_opt.yaml

# Connect to a remote CARLA server
uv run detect-no-3d-model $CONF/nishishinjuku.yaml --host 192.168.1.100 --port 3000

# Increase ray search range for hilly terrain
uv run detect-no-3d-model $CONF/nishishinjuku.yaml --ray-upper 10.0 --ray-lower 10.0

# Longer timeout for slow connections
uv run detect-no-3d-model $CONF/nishishinjuku.yaml --timeout 30.0

# Debug logging
uv run detect-no-3d-model $CONF/nishishinjuku.yaml -v

docs.title: Command-Line Options
docs.text: Option Short Required Default Description yaml_path - Yes - Path to map configuration YAML (map settings at the top level or under map:; see below) --host - No localhost CARLA server hostname --port - No 2000 CARLA server port --ray-upper - No 5.0 Ray search range above z estimate (meters) --ray-lower - No 5.0 Ray search range below z estimate (meters) --timeout - No 10.0 CARLA client timeout (seconds) --verbose -v No false Enable DEBUG logging

docs.title: Input YAML Requirements
docs.text:
The map settings are resolved exactly as the scenario runner resolves the map config group: lanelet2_path and xodr_path (~ and ${oc.env:...} work; a relative path is taken from the working directory), directory, source, projector_type and overwrite_xodr (see Map Configuration). A map given by files needs at minimum:

name: NishishinjukuMap          # CARLA map name
xodr_path: path/to/map.xodr     # Path to OpenDRIVE file
lanelet2_path: path/to/map.osm  # Path to Lanelet2 file

A map given by source or directory needs only that key (name defaults to the map directory's name); when it ships no OpenDRIVE, the tool reads the road network back out of the loaded CARLA world and caches it, as a run does. With overwrite_xodr: true the OpenDRIVE is installed into the CARLA asset named by the <MAP_NAME>_PATH environment variable before the map is loaded; otherwise CARLA's own road network is kept.

These keys may also sit under a map: section (as in the example nishishinjuku.yaml, a # @package _global_ config); no_3d_model_lanelet_ids is then written there too.

A config that cannot be read, is not valid YAML, or does not name a usable map is reported as a single detect-no-3d-model: error: ... line with exit status 1, before CARLA is contacted.

docs.title: Integration with Scenario Runner
docs.text: The detected lanelet IDs are stored in the map config's no_3d_model_lanelet_ids field. The scenario runner's sweep feature uses this list to exclude problematic lanelets from automatic spawn point selection.

docs.title: viewer - Scenario Result Viewer
docs.text: Web UI for browsing and monitoring scenario test results. Starts a FastAPI server with Uvicorn.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
1. Scans the base path directory for scenario output files (outputs/YYYY-MM-DD/HH-MM-SS/)
  2. Serves a web interface for browsing sessions and viewing individual scenario results, each with its run in an embedded Rerun viewer (Seeing a run in the viewer)
  3. Provides an API for triggering scenario runs and monitoring progress in real time

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
# Start with default settings (127.0.0.1:9000, current directory)
uv run viewer

# Custom host and port
uv run viewer --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080

# Scan another project: the directory containing outputs/ and multirun/
uv run viewer --base-path /path/to/project

# All options
uv run viewer --help

Then open http://localhost:9000 (or the configured host/port) in a browser.

Option Environment variable Default --host VIEWER_HOST 127.0.0.1 --port VIEWER_PORT 9000 --base-path VIEWER_BASE_PATH the working directory --fetch-rerun-web-viewer [--from TGZ] [--version V] — fetch the Rerun web viewer and exit (below)

Each option defaults to its environment variable, so a flag on the command line wins over the environment. An unknown option is an error (exit 2) and serves nothing.

The viewer listens on this machine only by default

The viewer has no authentication, and its API starts scenario runs (POST /api/run) and SLURM submissions (/api/slurm/...). It therefore binds 127.0.0.1 unless told otherwise. It used to bind 0.0.0.0, every interface; to serve other machines as before, pass --host 0.0.0.0 (or set VIEWER_HOST=0.0.0.0) on a network you trust. The viewer prints a warning when it listens on anything but a loopback address.

docs.title: Seeing a run in the viewer
docs.text:
A scenario's page shows its run in Rerun's web viewer, embedded in the page: the case's trajectory log made into a Rerun recording (Seeing a run). A recording already beside the log (X.rrd beside X.trajectory.jsonl) is shown as it is; otherwise the viewer makes it the first time the page is opened (in a worker thread, some tens of milliseconds for a case) and keeps it beside the log, or, where the session's directory cannot be written, in its cache directory. Making one needs the converter in the viewer's environment:

pip install 'autoware-carla-scenario[rerun]'    # or: pip install autoware-carla-scenario-rerun

Without it the page says so, and still shows a recording already made. The page's Download .rrd link is the recording itself, for the native viewer (rerun X.rrd).

The web viewer is the @rerun-io/web-viewer package of the version the converter writes recordings with (RERUN_VERSION, 0.38.1 for converter 0.1; a recording opens only in a viewer of its minor version). By default the page loads it from the unpkg CDN, pinned to that version. For a machine without the network, keep a copy that the viewer serves itself:

uv run viewer --fetch-rerun-web-viewer                 # from the npm registry, checked against its integrity hash
uv run viewer --fetch-rerun-web-viewer --from web-viewer-0.38.1.tgz   # from the package's tarball, copied in

The copy goes to ~/.cache/autoware_carla_scenario/viewer/rerun-web-viewer/<version>/ (VIEWER_CACHE_DIR moves the cache) and is used from then on. VIEWER_RERUN_WEB_VIEWER overrides where the viewer comes from: an unpacked copy of the package (a directory), a mirror of it (a URL), or none for no embedded viewer (the page then names the recording only).

docs.title: Results on the ODD
docs.text: A session's page links its results on the ODD (/session/{type}/{date}/{time}/odd): openodd's coverage matrix (openodd.CoverageView) of the cases' coverage files ({stem}_coverage.json), along two ODD attributes picked above it (by default the two the cases were drawn over that tell them apart most). Each cell holds the runs that spent time in it, coloured by what they did -- green passed, red failed, yellow flaky (both), white not sampled -- and a click on one drills into it: the matrix of the next two attributes inside it, and below, the cases in it, each linking to its page (and its run in the Rerun viewer) with its verdict, the buckets it was drawn in and a few metrics of how the ego drove, read off its trajectory log: the least gap from its box to another road user's (min gap), its hardest braking (over half a second), when it first stopped, how far it drove, its top and final speed, and the elapsed time. openodd's plot of the drawn cases (openodd.CasePlot) is shown too.

docs.title: Comparing runs
docs.text:
/compare (the navigation bar's Compare, or Compare with past runs on a session's page) compares two or more sessions of the same scenarios (?s=batch/2026-10-18/16-09-52&s=...), the oldest the baseline:

  • Cases are matched by what they ran -- their sweep overrides (less ++odd_case, which names a case's position), else the ODD values they were drawn at -- not by their index, so a case keeps its match when a sweep's order or size changes. Each is marked by how its verdict changed between the first session that ran it and the last: pass → fail (a regression, listed first and in red), fail → pass, flaky, the same, or run by one session only. Beside it, the change of each metric (bold when more than 5%), each run's verdict linking to its page, and side by side: the first and last runs in two Rerun viewers on one page (/compare/runs?run=type/date/time/index&run=...).
  • ODD cells: each session's passes and runs in each cell of the two attributes picked (the buckets the cases were drawn in), red where the last session passes fewer of them, green where more; and openodd's matrix of each session beside the others.
  • Pass rates of each session.

docs.title: Running through SLURM
docs.text:
The Run Scenarios panel's Launcher runs the batch here, case after case (local, the default), or submits it as a SLURM array job (SLURM, Running a Batch on SLURM) with the launcher.* keys the panel sets: the partition (from sinfo), array_parallelism, cases_per_task, time, mem, gres, start_stagger_seconds, extra environment variables (launcher.env), and for a viewer whose host sees the nodes' file system at another path (an sshfs or NFS mount) remote_cwd, python and the setup lines a job runs first (A submit host with other paths); the extra overrides can set any other. The viewer runs scenario [--multirun] scenario=... launcher=slurm ... --no-wait (with a sweeper, every case of the sweep) in its base path, and opens the batch's page once it is submitted. Where sbatch is not on the viewer's PATH the option is disabled, and says so.

A SLURM batch's page (outputs/<date>/<time>/ with a slurm/ directory, whoever submitted it) follows it through squeue and the records its tasks write: each case passed, failed, errored, running, pending or missing (with why: its task's state and error), each submission's job and tasks (state, host, cases done, peak memory), and the cases as they land, before the batch has a summary. Its buttons run scenario-slurm on the batch: Resubmit missing (the cases with no outcome, or that errored), Resubmit failed too (--failed), with the array parallelism and cases per task to use, Collect (the summary and batch_results.json) and Cancel jobs.

VIEWER_SCENARIO_COMMAND replaces uv run scenario as the command a SLURM batch is submitted with (.venv/bin/scenario, say, where uv run must not sync the environment).

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text: Variable Default Description VIEWER_BASE_PATH Current working directory Base path for scanning scenario result files (--base-path wins) VIEWER_HOST 127.0.0.1 Server bind address (--host wins) VIEWER_PORT 9000 Server listen port (--port wins) VIEWER_CACHE_DIR ~/.cache/autoware_carla_scenario/viewer The web viewer's copy, and recordings of sessions that cannot be written VIEWER_RERUN_WEB_VIEWER the copy in the cache, else the CDN Where the Rerun web viewer is loaded from: a directory, a URL, or none VIEWER_RERUN_MAP_DIR ~/autoware_data/maps, if it exists Where the converter looks a map up by name when the log's own map file is not on this machine VIEWER_SCENARIO_COMMAND uv run scenario The command a SLURM batch is submitted with

docs.title: Web UI Pages
docs.text: Route Description / Session list — displays all test sessions grouped by date/time /session/{type}/{date}/{time} Session detail — shows all scenarios in a session with pass/fail status /session/{type}/{date}/{time}/{index} Scenario detail — the run in the Rerun viewer, condition tree, per-condition status /recording/{type}/{date}/{time}/{index}.rrd The case's Rerun recording (made first if need be) /session/{type}/{date}/{time}/odd The session's results on the ODD (?x=, ?y= the attributes, ?at=attribute=bucket the cell drilled into) /compare Sessions compared (?s=type/date/time, two or more; ?x=, ?y= the cells' attributes) /compare/runs Runs side by side in Rerun viewers (?run=type/date/time/index, up to four)

docs.title: REST API Endpoints
docs.text:
The viewer also provides API endpoints for programmatic use and the web UI's interactive features:

Method Endpoint Description POST /api/refresh Clear result cache and return updated session table HTML GET /api/scenarios List all available scenario config names POST /api/run/preview Preview the CLI command that would be executed POST /api/run Start a scenario execution in the background (409 {"status": "busy"} while a local run is still in progress) GET /api/run/status Get current run status (non-streaming) GET /api/run/progress SSE (Server-Sent Events) stream for real-time progress GET /api/launchers The launchers a run can use here (slurm only where sbatch is, with the partitions) GET /api/slurm/submission The batch the viewer last submitted through SLURM, and its page once submitted GET /api/slurm/{date}/{time}/status A SLURM batch's cases, jobs and tasks POST /api/slurm/{date}/{time}/{resubmit,collect,cancel} scenario-slurm on the batch (resubmit takes failed, array_parallelism, cases_per_task) POST /api/recording/{type}/{date}/{time}/{index} Make the case's Rerun recording if there is none; its URL and path (503 with the install hint without the converter)

Run request body format:

{
  "scenario": "*/*",
  "extra_overrides": ["server.host=192.168.1.100"],
  "sweeper": "",
  "launcher": "local"
}

With "launcher": "slurm", "slurm" holds the launcher.* keys: {"partition": "main", "array_parallelism": 2, "cases_per_task": null, "time": "02:00:00", "mem": "12G", "gres": null, "start_stagger_seconds": 30, "remote_cwd": "workspace/OnePlanner", "python": ".venv/bin/python", "setup": "source ~/env.sh", "env": {"NAME": "value"}} (setup: a shell line per line, without ${...} or a backslash continuing it; env: NAME=value lines, or a mapping, each value exported as written, so without ${...} either -- an OmegaConf interpolation in the override the viewer passes on).

Progress SSE event format:

{
  "current": 2,
  "total": 5,
  "scenario_name": "intersection_passing/straight",
  "status": "running"
}

Where status is one of: "running", "idle", or "done".

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text: Variable Used By Description CARLA_EXECUTABLE scenario runner Path to CARLA's launcher (CarlaUnreal.sh); defaults to the one scenario-setup installed AUTOWARE_CARLA_SCENARIO_HOME scenario-setup, scenario runner Moves ~/.autoware_carla_scenario (CARLA lives in bin/carla) NISHISHINJUKU_XODR_PATH map config Override default OpenDRIVE file path for nishishinjuku NISHISHINJUKU_LANELET2_PATH map config Override default Lanelet2 file path for nishishinjuku VIEWER_BASE_PATH viewer Base path for scenario results VIEWER_HOST viewer Viewer server bind address (default 127.0.0.1; --host wins) VIEWER_PORT viewer Viewer server listen port (--port wins) VIEWER_CACHE_DIR viewer The viewer's cache (the Rerun web viewer's copy, recordings it could not keep beside their logs) VIEWER_RERUN_WEB_VIEWER viewer Where the Rerun web viewer is loaded from (a directory, a URL, or none) VIEWER_RERUN_MAP_DIR viewer Where the Rerun converter looks maps up by name VIEWER_SCENARIO_COMMAND viewer The command a SLURM batch is submitted with (default uv run scenario) SCENARIO_EDITOR_DRAFTS scenario editor Directory holding scenario drafts SCENARIO_EDITOR_EXPORT_DIR scenario editor Staging area for exported package archives SCENARIO_EDITOR_MAP_ROOTS scenario editor Directories a Lanelet2 map may be served from SCENARIO_EDITOR_HOST scenario editor Editor server bind address (default 127.0.0.1; --host wins) SCENARIO_EDITOR_PORT scenario editor Editor server listen port (--port wins) SCENARIO_EDITOR_MAP_VIEWER scenario editor URL of a self-hosted simple_lanelet2 map viewer SCENARIO_EXPORT_FRAMEWORK_VERSION package export Pin exported packages to a published framework release SCENARIO_EXPORT_FRAMEWORK_REPOSITORY package export Repository URL recorded for a commit pin

docs.title: Use Case 1: Run a Single Scenario
docs.text:
# Start CARLA server first, then:
uv run scenario scenario=intersection_passing/straight

docs.title: Use Case 2: Run All Scenarios for a Map
docs.text: uv run scenario scenario='*/*' map=nishishinjuku

docs.title: Use Case 3: Test on a Remote CARLA Server
docs.text:
uv run scenario scenario=intersection_passing/left_turn \
  server.host=192.168.1.100 server.port=2000

docs.title: Use Case 4: Detect Missing 3D Models Before Running Scenarios
docs.text:
# 1. Detect lanelets without ground geometry (from the repository root)
uv run detect-no-3d-model autoware_carla_scenario/src/autoware_carla_scenario/examples/conf/map/nishishinjuku.yaml

# 2. The detected IDs are written to no_3d_model_lanelet_ids in the YAML
# 3. Now run scenarios — sweep will skip these lanelets
uv run scenario scenario='intersection_passing/*' map=nishishinjuku

docs.title: Use Case 5: Browse Results in the Web UI
docs.text:
# 1. Run scenarios
uv run scenario scenario='*/*'

# 2. Launch the viewer from the project directory: it scans outputs/ and
#    multirun/ there (from elsewhere: --base-path <dir containing outputs/>)
uv run viewer

# 3. Open http://localhost:9000 in a browser

docs.title: Use Case 6: Resume a Failed Batch
docs.text:
# Original batch run (5 scenarios, stopped at the 4th, e.g. by Ctrl+C)
uv run scenario scenario='intersection_passing/*'

# Resume from the 4th scenario
uv run scenario scenario='intersection_passing/*' --resume-from 4

docs.title: "Connection refused" or timeout when connecting to CARLA
docs.text:
Cause: CARLA server is not running, or host/port is incorrect.

Solution: - Verify the CARLA server is started and accessible - Check server.host and server.port overrides match the server - Increase --timeout for detect-no-3d-model

docs.title: "batch scenarios must share the same map"
docs.text:
Cause: Glob pattern matched scenarios configured for different maps.

Solution: - Use map=<name> override to force all scenarios to use the same map - Or narrow the glob pattern to match scenarios for one map only

docs.title: Ego vehicle falls through the ground
docs.text:
Cause: The spawn lanelet has no corresponding 3D ground geometry in CARLA.

Solution: - Run detect-no-3d-model to identify problematic lanelets - Add them to no_3d_model_lanelet_ids in the map config - Increase entity.ground_projection_ray_distance_lower for deeper ray casting - Increase entity.spawn_retry_max_count for more spawn attempts

docs.title: Scenario times out unexpectedly
docs.text:
Cause: scenario.timeout_seconds is too short, or the ego vehicle is stuck.

Solution: - Increase scenario.timeout_seconds - Check ego.initial_speed_kmh — a value of 0.0 requires autopilot to start moving - Enable verbose logging and check condition statuses in the result JSON

docs.title: "Unknown scenario name" error
docs.text:
Cause: The scenario.name field in the YAML does not match any registered scenario class.

Solution: - Supported scenario names: intersection_passing, lane_change, traffic_light_compliance, temporary_stop - Check the name field in your scenario YAML config

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• API Reference — Detailed API documentation for programmatic usage
  • Development Guide — Contributing and development setup

docs.title: Example Scenarios
docs.text:
The examples shipped in autoware_carla_scenario.examples are logical scenarios: none of them names an intersection, a lane or a map. Each says what the lanelet it starts on has to be -- the approach to a signalised junction, a lane with a lane on its left, a road's right-hand edge -- and the lanelet-constraint sweeper expands it, on whatever map it is run on, into one concrete scenario per lanelet that qualifies. Every other place the scenario names follows from the lanelet the sweep picked.

Scenario What it checks Variants Traffic Light Compliance Waits at a red light, goes on green -- Temporary Stop Stops at a stop sign's line, then goes -- Intersection Passing Turns or goes straight through a junction left, right, right from a standstill, straight Lane Change Changes lane -- or refuses where there is none left, right, refused left, refused right Pedestrian Dart-out Does not hit a pedestrian who runs out -- Cut-in Does not hit a vehicle cutting in from the left, from the right Adversities TeraSim's adversities carried out in CARLA (concrete, on Town10HD_Opt) brake check, ignore leader, cut-in, traffic rule, jaywalking, NADE

docs.title: How each page reads
docs.text:
In the Scenario Editor. The screenshot is the example authored in the Scenario Editor, open on Town10HD_Opt. The Places panel binds one of the lanelets the search matches -- the same one the video below it runs -- and draws every place that follows from it: an NPC on the lane beside the ego, the lanelet a condition watches, the ego's goal.

The video. Each page's clip is not something a run writes (runs render no video since 15.0.0; see Seeing a run): it is recorded for these pages by tools/scenario_video/, a separate tool in the repository that films the run with a chase camera of its own, lays it beside a sumo-gui replay and encodes the result with the ffmpeg command-line tool.

A lanelet in the editor is chosen one of three ways:

  • Fixed -- this lanelet.
  • Constraint search -- the lanelets matching a constraint tree; the sweeper runs the scenario once per match. One lanelet per scenario is searched for.
  • From the search -- worked out from the lanelet the search picked, case by case, by a binding:
Binding The lanelet it gives The matched lanelet The pick itself Beside the matched lanelet The lane on its left or right a vehicle may change into Along the route from the matched lanelet The lanelet that many steps on Lanelet before the stop line The lanelet a spawn that far before the pick's stop line stands on

A spawn's position along its lanelet can be derived the same way -- Before stop line puts it a fixed distance short of the stop line.

Scenario. What happens, in the order the editor lays it out: who starts where, what is done and when, and what makes the run pass or fail.

Parameters. The values the example runs with. Each can be overridden from the command line like any Hydra key -- scenario.timeout_seconds=30, ego.initial_speed_kmh=10 -- and the sweep's constraints are what decide where it runs.

Result. One case, run on CARLA 0.10 with SUMO driving the traffic: CARLA's chase camera on the left, sumo-gui replaying the same run on the right.

docs.title: Running one
docs.text:
# Every case on a map, one after another
uv run scenario --multirun hydra/sweeper=lanelet_constraint \
    scenario=cut_in/left map=town10hd_opt traffic=sumo

# Or list the cases, to run them anywhere
uv run scenario-expand scenario=cut_in/left map=town10hd_opt

docs.title: Adversities
docs.text:
Each of TeraSim's phase-1 adversities, carried out by a road user placed so that its own trigger fires, and NADE among background traffic: the CARLA check of the adversarial actions (#404).

Unlike the other examples these are concrete scenarios, not logical ones: each case names its lanelets, on Town10HD_Opt.

uv run scenario scenario=adversity/cut_in map=town10hd_opt

docs.title: Scenario
docs.text:
The ego is driven by the TrafficManager, as in the other examples. Every light is set green, except in traffic_rule, which sets them all red. The road user that carries the adversity out is held at its speed until the adversity takes it over.

The adversity's own trigger (AdversityFeasibleCondition, the action's default, at AdversityLocation.ANY) decides when it fires. The case is placed so that the trigger holds:

Case Who Placed The adversity Fires brake_check NPC1 15 m ahead of the ego on lanelet 324, both at 30 km/h AdversarialBrakeAction: brakes at 9 m/s² for 2 s, to a stop about 1.3 s in ignore_leader NPC1 25 m behind a slow ego (8 km/h) on lanelet 324, at 25 km/h IgnoreLeaderAction: speeds up at the free-flow rate for 2 s, as if the ego were not there about 0.7 s in cut_in NPC1 6 m ahead in the lane on the ego's left (324 beside 446), at 30 km/h AdversarialCutInAction: changes in front of the ego in 1 s at once traffic_rule NPC1 10 m ahead of the ego on lanelet 719, every light red RunTrafficRuleAction: slowing for its red light, drives on through it at the free-flow rate for 2 s about 24 s in, at the light jaywalking pedestrian1 at the kerb 35 m ahead of the ego, off any crosswalk JaywalkAction: walks straight across the road at once nade the background vehicles 40 of the TrafficManager's, around the ego on lanelet 324 AdversarialTrafficAction (NADE) over the five kinds several times a run

When it passes. A single adversity's run passes once the adversity has been carried out and its road user handed back to traffic: its action reaches completeState (ActionStateCondition). It fails if that has not happened by timeout_seconds.

NADE.

  • NADE samples far more often than TeraSim's numbers would, so that one 45 s run shows several adversities:
  • each kind's naturalistic probability is p = 0.05 a tick while its trigger holds;
  • each is drawn with q = 0.5;
  • the cooldown is 2 s;
  • an adversity counts when it challenges another NPC, not only the ego.
  • The run passes after nade_seconds.
  • The run's log records each sampled adversity as an adversity record, and the importance-sampling weight as the importance_sampling_weight metric (see The weight).

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Key Default What it sets scenario.kind brake_check brake_check, ignore_leader, cut_in, traffic_rule, jaywalking or nade scenario.npc_lanelet_id 324 The NPC's lanelet, or the pedestrian's kerb scenario.npc_ahead_m 15.0 How far ahead of the ego's spawn s it starts (negative: behind) scenario.npc_offset_m -3.0 The pedestrian's offset from its lanelet's centreline (negative: right) scenario.npc_speed_kmh 30.0 The NPC's speed until the adversity takes it over scenario.ego_speed_kmh null The ego's speed, held for the run; null: the TrafficManager's scenario.red_light false Every light red scenario.timeout_seconds 30.0 Fails when not carried out by then scenario.nade_seconds 45.0 NADE: the run's length scenario.nade_probability 0.05 NADE: each kind's naturalistic probability a tick scenario.nade_is_probability 0.5 NADE: the importance-sampling probability scenario.nade_cooldown 2.0 NADE: no adversity for this long after one (s) scenario.nade_challenge_npcs true NADE: an adversity may challenge another NPC scenario.nade_seed 7 NADE: the sampler's seed

docs.title: Result
docs.text:
Each case was run on CARLA 0.10 with Town10HD_Opt through scenario. The ego was driven by the TrafficManager and the run-time static check was on. Every case PASSED: brake_check at 3.45 s, ignore_leader at 3.05 s, cut_in at 1.20 s, traffic_rule at 26.40 s, jaywalking at 6.10 s, and nade after its 45 s. The trajectory logs show the following:

Case What happened brake_check The NPC braked from 8.3 m/s to a stop in 1.25 s. It was held there to the command's end and handed back 2 s after firing. ignore_leader The NPC's path sped it up from 6.8 to 8.3 m/s for 2 s behind the 2.2 m/s ego. cut_in The NPC was in front of the ego 1 s after firing. traffic_rule The NPC, slowing for its red light at 8.2 m/s, drove 16 m on through the junction in 2 s. jaywalking The pedestrian walked straight across the ego's lane, at its speed times a factor drawn from the run's seed. nade Ten adversities in 45 s among 40 background vehicles: five cut-ins, three brake checks and two ignore-leaders. Each was sampled at q = 0.5, so the weight fell to about 4e-23.

docs.title: Placed for the trigger
docs.text:
• ignore_leader. An NPC faster than its speed limit would slow down even as it ignores its leader. Its free-flow acceleration, towards the limit, is then negative too. This matches TeraSim, so the NPC drives below the limit.
  • traffic_rule. The trigger fires only for an NPC that slows for its light rather than for a leader, so the NPC is placed ahead of the ego.

docs.title: Cut-in
docs.text:
A vehicle in the next lane, 10 m ahead of the ego, changes into the ego's lane 2 s into the run. The ego must not hit it -- on every lane with a lane on that side.

# Every case on the map, one run each
uv run scenario --multirun hydra/sweeper=lanelet_constraint \
    scenario=cut_in/left map=<map>

docs.title: Scenario
docs.text: Ego Constraint search: a lane with a lane on the cut-in side, not in a junction, at least 60 m long, excluding the map's lanelets with no 3D model. 5 m along it, 30 km/h. NPC1 Beside the matched lanelet, on the cut-in side: the lane next to the ego's. 15 m along it, 30 km/h. Initialization Every traffic light green. NPC1, after 2 s Change lane towards the ego. Pass 3 s have passed since NPC1 reached the ego's OpenDRIVE lane (lane of a position: the matched lanelet at the ego's spawn, the same lane), with no collision. Fail The ego collides with anything -- NPC1, another actor, a static object, map geometry such as a wall or a kerb (ego_collided); the ego's centre is on none of the lanes ahead of it -- the matched lanelet and the lanelets that follow it, up to 1000 m from its start -- for 0.2 s: it changed lanes, turned onto a lanelet that does not follow it, or left the road (ego_left_its_lane); or 20 s pass.

docs.title: Variants
docs.text:
From the leftFrom the right

scenario=cut_in/left -- a lane on the ego's left; NPC1 changes right.

Town10HD_Opt, the first case: the search matched lanelet 324, where the ego starts; NPC1 starts beside it on lanelet 446. Result: PASSED.

scenario=cut_in/right -- a lane on the ego's right; NPC1 changes left.

Town10HD_Opt, the first case: the search matched lanelet 446, where the ego starts; NPC1 starts beside it on lanelet 324. Result: PASSED.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Value NPC1 ahead of the ego 10 m along its lanelet (at s = 15 m): npc_ahead_m or, measured npc_gap_m: the gap vehicle_ahead_gap_m reads at the start (bumper to bumper, along the ego's lane); NPC1's s is solved for so it does. Unset by default; an ODD-sampled sweep sets it, 2-30 m NPC1 and ego initial speed 30 km/h Cut-in after 2 s Held in the ego's lane for 3 s Lanelet at least 60 m Timeout 20 s Fail on any collision of the ego on: fail_on_any_collision (off: only a collision with NPC1, hit_cut_in_vehicle) Fail on leaving the lanes ahead on: fail_on_leaving_lane The lanes ahead reach 1000 m from the start of the matched lanelet: lanes_ahead_m Off them for 0.2 s: leaving_lane_seconds (0: the first tick off)

docs.title: Staying on the lanes ahead
docs.text:
The ego is to keep its lane while NPC1 cuts in: braking, or slowing, is the answer the scenario is after, and a run that swerved into the next lane or off the road has not passed it, whatever it did not hit. The lanes ahead are the lanelet the ego spawns on and the ones that follow it in the routing graph (lanelets_ahead: following without lane changes, every branch, up to lanes_ahead_m); in none of them is in the lane beside, on a lanelet that turns off them, or in no lanelet at all.

It is not a condition of its own but a composition of the framework's, left_lanes_ahead in examples/cut_in.py, which any scenario can build the same way:

on_lanes = [
    EntityLanePositionCondition(
        EGO_ROLE_NAME, Lanelet2Pose(lanelet_id=i, s=0.0), label=f"ego_on_lanelet_{i}"
    )
    for i in lanelets_ahead(spawn.lanelet_id, 1000.0)
]
self.register_fail_condition(
    PersistentCondition(                     # off them for 0.2 s, not one tick at a seam
        NotCondition(                        # on none of them -- off the road included
            OrCondition(on_lanes),           # on one of them
            holds_when_pending=True,
        ),
        0.2,
        label="ego_left_its_lane",
    )
)

holds_when_pending=True is what makes it a logical NOT. A condition that has not fired returns nothing, and a plain NotCondition only flips the verdict of a child that has, so it could not say "on none of these". The position tested is the vehicle's centre (its CARLA location), so a wheel over the line is not leaving the lane; a seam between two lanelets is covered by the next one, and the 0.2 s wait absorbs a tick that falls between them.

A scenario document says the same with the editor's cards -- Persistent, NOT (with Holds while the child does not), ANY and one Position (Lanelet2) per lanelet:

- type: persistent
  params: {duration: 0.2}
  children:
    - type: not
      params: {holds_when_pending: true}
      children:
        - type: any
          children:
            - {type: entity_lane_position, params: {entity: ego, lanelet_id: 79016}}
            - {type: entity_lane_position, params: {entity: ego, lanelet_id: 79017}}

docs.title: Placing NPC1 by the measured gap
docs.text:
npc_ahead_m is a raw setting: NPC1's s on its lanelet less the ego's on its own. It is not the gap the vehicle_ahead_gap_m measure reads: the measure is bumper to bumper -- NPC1's rear bumper less the ego's front bumper -- along the ego's lane (Scenario measures), and lanelets side by side are not the same length on a curve (the outer one is longer), so their s do not line up and the difference changes from place to place.

npc_gap_m is that gap itself. When it is set, the scenario places NPC1 with place_at_vehicle_ahead_gap: from the ego's spawn pose, it finds the s on NPC1's lanelet at which the measure -- the same code, run on the poses the two will spawn at -- reads npc_gap_m, so the run starts at exactly that gap wherever it is placed. The bumpers are the vehicles' own: before either is spawned, a vehicle of each blueprint (ego.vehicle_type, npc_vehicle_type) already in the world is read, or else one is spawned high above the map, its bounding box read and the vehicle destroyed (vehicle_bumpers, once per blueprint), so NPC1 is spawned once, where the gap reads right, rather than spawned and moved. A gap the lanelet cannot reach (too short, or curving out of the lanes the measure counts) fails the setup, saying what gaps it does reach.

On CARLA 0.10 Town04_Opt, with the ego (a Lincoln MKZ) on lanelet 79016 at s = 640 and NPC1 (a Mini) placed on lanelet 77298 beside it, gaps of 2.5, 8, 12, 15, 20, 25 and 30 m were measured back within 0.001 m on the first tick (within 0.01 m two ticks later). Placed by a calibrated npc_ahead_m offset instead, and measured centre to centre, the same place read 2.2 m more than drawn.

The scenario's controls draw the gap this way (target: measure, Controls), so a sweep's vehicle_ahead_gap draws are the gaps the runs start at:

uv run scenario scenario=cut_in/left map=<map> scenario.npc_gap_m=15

The relative speed needs no solving: npc_initial_speed_kmh less the ego's initial speed is what the vehicle_ahead_relative_speed_kph measure reads at the start, up to the cosine of the small heading difference on a curve.

docs.title: Intersection Passing
docs.text:
The ego approaches a junction from 25 m short of its stop line and takes one movement through it -- left, right or straight on -- on every junction movement of that kind on the map. Every light is green, so nothing stops it.

# Every case on the map, one run each
uv run scenario --multirun hydra/sweeper=lanelet_constraint \
    scenario=intersection_passing/left_turn map=<map>

docs.title: Scenario
docs.text: Ego Constraint search: a junction lanelet whose turn_direction is the movement and which has a stop line -- any, or a traffic light's (see the variants) -- excluding the map's lanelets with no 3D model, except from a standstill. Position before stop line: 25 m short of it -- which walks back onto the lane that approaches the junction, where the run starts. Goal from the search: the lanelet after the junction lanelet. Initialization Every traffic light green. Ego, from the start Turn at the next junction, in the movement's direction. Pass The ego has been on the road of the junction lanelet (the matched lanelet), and on the road of the lane it comes out on (along the route, one step on). Any lane of each road counts. Fail The timeout -- and, going straight, slowing below 3 km/h after 0.3 s.

Town10HD_Opt, the first case: the search matched lanelet 4412 and the ego starts on lanelet 5975, 15.2 m along it. Result: PASSED.

Town10HD_Opt, the first case: the search matched lanelet 4766 and the ego starts on lanelet 3235, 7.0 m along it. Result: PASSED.

Town10HD_Opt, the first case: the search matched lanelet 4766 and the ego starts on lanelet 3235, 7.0 m along it. Result: PASSED.

scenario=intersection_passing/straight -- turn_direction: straight at a signalised junction only, 5 km/h, 15 s. Also fails if the ego drops below 3 km/h after 0.3 s: with every light green it never has to stop.

Town10HD_Opt, the first case: the search matched lanelet 4503 and the ego starts on lanelet 860, 3.0 m along it. Result: PASSED.

docs.title: Lane Change
docs.text:
The ego is told to change lane as soon as the run starts. Where there is a lane to change into, it has to end up in it; where there is none, it has to stay where it is.

# Every case on the map, one run each
uv run scenario --multirun hydra/sweeper=lanelet_constraint \
    scenario=lane_change/left map=<map>
uv run scenario --multirun hydra/sweeper=lanelet_constraint \
    scenario=lane_change_fail/left map=<map>

docs.title: Scenario
docs.text:
Ego Constraint search: a lane that is not in a junction and is long enough, excluding the map's lanelets with no 3D model -- with a lane on that side to change into, or, for the refused change, without one. 1 km/h. Initialization Every traffic light green. Ego, from the start Change lane, left or right. Pass Changing: the ego has been on the OpenDRIVE lane beside the one it started on (lane of a position: the matched lanelet at the spawn, the lane to its left or right). Refusing: the timeout passes. Fail Changing: the timeout. Refusing: the ego reaches that lane.

The lane checked is the OpenDRIVE lane next to the spawn's, anywhere along its road, rather than the lanelet next to the spawn's: a refused change has no such lanelet to name.

docs.title: Pedestrian Dart-out
docs.text:
A pedestrian waits at the kerb 35 m ahead of the ego and runs out across its lane once the ego is within 20 m. The ego must not hit them -- on every lane at the right-hand edge of a road, where the pedestrian steps straight off the kerb into it.

# Every case on the map, one run each
uv run scenario --multirun hydra/sweeper=lanelet_constraint \
    scenario=pedestrian_dart_out/pedestrian_dart_out map=<map>

docs.title: Scenario
docs.text: Ego Constraint search: a lane with no lane on its right, not in a junction, at least 55 m long, excluding the map's lanelets with no 3D model. 5 m along it, 30 km/h. Goal from the search: 50 m along the matched lanelet, past the crossing. Pedestrian On the matched lanelet -- the ego's -- 40 m along it, 3 m to the right of its centre, turned 90° to face across the lane. A walker CARLA refuses inside the kerb is tried again higher up. Initialization Every traffic light green. Pedestrian, once the ego is within 20 m Walk straight ahead at 2 m/s. With turn_back_ttc_s or turn_back_distance_m set, it turns back to the kerb when a vehicle comes that close along the road while it is still within turn_back_within_m of the kerb (see below). Pass The ego has come within 3 m of the point 50 m along its lane, 10 m past the crossing. Fail The ego hits the pedestrian, or 25 s pass.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Value Pedestrian ahead of the ego 35 m (at s = 40 m) Off the lane's centre 3 m to the right Runs out when the ego is within 20 m Walking speed 2 m/s Passed once within 3 m of 10 m past the crossing (s = 50 m) Ego initial speed 30 km/h Timeout 25 s Turn back at TTC (turn_back_ttc_s) off Turn back at distance (turn_back_distance_m) off Turn back within (turn_back_within_m) 1 m of the kerb

docs.title: A pedestrian who turns back
docs.text:
By default the pedestrian runs across whatever comes. Set scenario.turn_back_ttc_s or scenario.turn_back_distance_m and it watches the vehicles as it goes (WalkStraightAction's turn-back options):

  • When. Once a vehicle's time to collision with it, or its distance to it, is at or under the threshold. Both are measured along the road, centre to centre, as the lane-frame TTC and distance conditions measure them.
  • Where it can. Up to turn_back_within_m onto the road -- a driving lane under it, measured from where it stepped off -- it turns round, walks back to half a metre behind the kerb (no further back than where it set off) and stands. One not on the road yet steps back the same way. Further out, it keeps going.
uv run scenario scenario=pedestrian_dart_out/pedestrian_dart_out map=<map> \
    scenario.turn_back_ttc_s=1.5 scenario.turn_back_within_m=1.0

docs.text: Town10HD_Opt, the first case: the search matched lanelet 324, where the ego starts. Result: PASSED.

docs.title: Temporary Stop
docs.text:
The ego starts at a standstill 15 m short of a stop line that no traffic light governs -- a stop sign's. It has to stop at the line and then go again -- on every such stop line of the map.

# Every case on the map, one run each
uv run scenario --multirun hydra/sweeper=lanelet_constraint \
    scenario=temporary_stop/temporary_stop map=<map>

docs.title: Scenario
docs.text: Ego Constraint search: a lanelet with a stop line that is not a traffic light's, excluding the map's lanelets with no 3D model. Position before stop line: 15 m short of it, on the lanelet before when the line is nearer its lanelet's start than that. Goal from the search: the lanelet after the matched one, past the line. Initialization Every traffic light green. Pass The ego has made a temporary stop -- under 0.1 m/s for 0.3 s within 5 m of a stop line -- and is moving at 3 km/h again. The stop lines are read off the map, from the lanelet the ego starts on and up to three after it (lanelet before the stop line, from the search). Fail 12 s pass.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Value Spawn 15 m before the stop line Ego initial speed 0 km/h Stopped below 0.1 m/s Held for 0.3 s Within 5 m of the stop line Restart speed 3 km/h Stop lines searched the spawn lanelet and 3 lanelets on Timeout 12 s

docs.title: Result
docs.text: Town10HD_Opt, the first case: the search matched lanelet 5164 and the ego starts on lanelet 3095, 39.0 m along it. Result: PASSED.

docs.title: Traffic Light Compliance
docs.text:
The ego starts at a standstill 10 m short of a signalised stop line with every light red. It has to drive up to the line and stop with its front bumper in the stop zone, 0-3 m before it, without crossing it while the light is red; then pull away once it turns green 5 s in -- on every lane that leads into a signalised junction.

# Every case on the map, one run each
uv run scenario --multirun hydra/sweeper=lanelet_constraint \
    scenario=traffic_light_compliance/traffic_light_compliance map=<map>

docs.title: Scenario
docs.text:
Ego Constraint search: a lanelet before a junction lanelet that has a traffic-light stop line, excluding the map's lanelets with no 3D model. Position before stop line: 10 m short of it. Goal: up the road, past the junction. Initialization Every traffic light red. After 5 s Every traffic light green. Pass Both have happened: before the green the ego stood still (0.1 m/s or slower) for 0.5 s with its front bumper 0-3 m before the stop line (the stop zone), and after 5.5 s it was moving at 10 km/h or more. Fail Its front bumper crosses the stop line while the light is red ("ran the red"); or at the green it has not stood still in the stop zone -- standing farther back ("stopped N m before the stop line, outside the stop zone"), stopped in the zone too late ("stopped in the stop zone … only X s before the green: less than standstill_seconds") or still rolling towards the line ("had not stopped by the green: still moving"); or 8 s pass.

Distances are the stop_line_distance_m measure's: along the ego's lane, from its front bumper to the stop line ahead. That measure reads only stop lines ahead, so the scenario keeps the line the ego started before and carries it on the ego's own travel once the reading jumps away -- to the next line, or to nothing -- and a crossing is a negative distance however the measure then reads. The run's result details carry where the ego stopped (stopped_at_stop_line_distance_m) or when and how far it crossed (crossed_at_seconds, crossed_by_m).

Where the measure's reading jumps beyond the line the ego had while that line is still at least 0.5 m ahead -- the other branch's line where the lane forks, the line of the lane it changed out of -- the reading is the ego's own line and is taken; so is a reading that jumps nearer (a lane whose line is staggered nearer). A front bumper up to stop_line_tolerance_m past the line has not crossed it, and counts as at the line (0 m) for the stop zone.

Approaching the line while the light is red is not a failure: an ego that starts 30 m back may roll up to the zone and stop there. One that starts inside the zone has to stay there. Having stood still in the zone is latched: if the ego then rolls back, or creeps on without crossing the line, before the green, it still passes.

The light turns green before the world steps from 5 s, so the step that ends at 5 s still ran under red (a crossing on it runs the red), and the verdict at the green is given on the first step driven under green, from where the ego was on the last red one: a standstill that only completes on the green step does not count.

docs.text:
Parameter Value Light turns green after 5.0 s Stop zone 0-3 m before the stop line (stop_zone_min_m, stop_zone_max_m) May pass the stop line on red by 0 m (stop_line_tolerance_m) Must have stood still in the stop zone for 0.5 s (standstill_seconds) Counts as standing still at 0.1 m/s or less (standstill_speed_mps) Counts as pulling away on green from 10 km/h Ego initial speed 0 km/h Spawn 10 m before the stop line Timeout 8 s

Note

On Nishi-Shinjuku the search also leaves out lanelet 222, where CARLA's TrafficManager moves the ego onto another lane in the junction.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: Town10HD_Opt, the first case: the search matched lanelet 719, where the ego starts. Result: PASSED. Recorded with scenario.moving_speed_kmh=15, from before the green check had a threshold of its own (departure_speed_kmh); that run was judged by an earlier rule, under which moving on red at 1 km/h or more (15 km/h with that override) failed the run.
